title: W1: fmn-core — constants, units, color pipeline, rate functions (the shared language of every manim scene)
description:
Implement fmn-core's semantic bedrock (§6.2, §6.3, §6.8).

Constants & units (§6.2): FRAME_HEIGHT = 8 and the coordinate conventions, direction constants (UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT/OUT/IN...), buffs, DEG/TAU, default stroke widths, the manim color palette, STROKE_WIDTH_CONVERSION = 0.01, the resolution table, the 30 fps default. These are kept EXACTLY — they are the shared language of every manim scene — and locked by a constants test against the Reference module (generate the fixture once from the pinned Reference source).

Color (§6.3): one pipeline, ours: colors decode to linear light, composite premultiplied, encode at the output transfer function. Manim's gradient aesthetic is deliberately preserved: interpolate_color keeps the Reference's sqrt(lerp(c1^2, c2^2, alpha)) form and average_color its RMS form, applied within the defined model. Full named palette, color_gradient, owned colormap tables (displacing matplotlib's), the hwb()/color-mix() machinery reused from fmd, and an Oklab interpolation OPTION. Draft Behavior Note BN-04 ("correct compositing, familiar gradients").

Rate functions (§6.8): the complete catalog with the same formulas (smooth, rush_into, there_and_back, wiggle, exponential_decay, ...), locked at 10^4 samples against the Reference; squish_rate_func and not_quite_there marked as combinators in the API schema.

Numeric doctrine hooks (§6.1): establish the f64-semantic / f32-record type aliases and the NaN/-0 canonicalization helpers used at serialization boundaries.

Acceptance: constants/rate-function parity tables green; color round-trip oracle tests (decode-encode identity, premultiply laws) green; BN-04 drafted.
close_reason: fmn-core semantic bedrock implemented: §6.2 constants (frame geometry, buffs, directions, angles, strokes, resolutions, full 57-color palette + aliases + defaults) locked bit-exact against constants.txt generated from pinned Reference 6199a00; §6.3 color pipeline (sRGB<->linear transfer, premultiplied source-over, Reference sqrt-lerp interpolate_color + RMS average_color + color_gradient, Oklab option, hwb) with round-trip oracles green; §6.8 rate catalog (15 functions incl. Bernstein bezier forms, squish/not_quite_there as combinators) locked at 10^4+1 samples within 1e-12; §6.1 Semantic/Record aliases + NaN/-0 canonicalization; BN-04 drafted in docs/behavior_notes/. 14 tests green, full gate green.

title: W5: 3D, camera, lighting, textures — the kept look, ported exactly
description:
Implement the 3D plane with the Reference's aesthetic DNA kept deliberately (§10.4, §10.6, §1.5, Appendix B, D-04):

CAMERA: CameraFrame on W2SPACE's fixed Rotation conventions; the Reference's projection constants ported exactly — w = 1 - z, z *= -0.1, frame rescale — because camera code and scene composition assume them; is_fixed_in_frame as a float mix (not a boolean branch); the four clip planes.

ORDERING & DEPTH: painter's order by W3ORDER's batching model; OPT-IN depth-test against per-tile f32 depth for depth-tested partitions; transparency composites in painter order within its partition.

LIGHTING: the finalize_color model ported AS-IS — shading = (reflectiveness, gloss, shadow), light at (-10, 10, 10), Surface defaults (0.3, 0.2, 0.4), dark_shift = 0.2 — because that shading IS the 3b1b look (Appendix B: kept). Surfaces: fixed UV-grid tessellation with perspective-correct interpolation. True-dot radial glow falloff kept (glow math and feel).

TEXTURES & IMAGES (§10.6): bilinear filtering with DEFINED wrap/orientation/alpha/color-space behavior; decode via fmn-codec (W8 — the PNG/JPEG bead is a dependency); exotic formats route through the ffmpeg capability with named errors.

Calibration: G0-2's look study fixes the lighting match measurement; the Look Gallery's 3D set (spheres, tori, textured surfaces, glow dots against gradients) is the standing review.

Acceptance: projection fixtures vs the Reference constants (loose f32); lighting golden renders reviewed in the Gallery; depth-partition ordering tests (mixed depth-tested/painter content); clip-plane fixtures; texture policy tests (wrap/orientation/alpha matrix); euler-singularity camera animation test (via W2SPACE).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FROM fm-oac / fm-5oi (2026-07-26) — TWO THINGS ARE WAITING ON YOUR CAMERA, both stated in code rather than half-built.

1. flat_stroke vs camera-facing (§10.3). Under bin.rs's ScreenMap — a uniform scale plus a translation — the two are the SAME construction: a width measured in the object plane and one measured in screen pixels differ by exactly that scale, and crates/fmn-render/src/stroke.rs already computes the screen-space one. They diverge only once geometry leaves the view plane (a flat stroke on a rotated shape foreshortens; a camera-facing one does not). Uniforms::flat_stroke is read and honoured trivially today; the divergence is yours. Note also C-2 (BN-07): the Reference's get_flat_stroke() reads the WRONG uniform, and fmn-mobject already fixed that — do not re-derive it.

2. Perspective for the fill (§10.2) is already built and waiting for a producer. crates/fmn-render/src/fill.rs has RationalPiece + append_rational: a projected quadratic is EXACTLY a rational quadratic (projection is linear on homogeneous coordinates), subdivision is de Casteljau in homogeneous coordinates so it is lossless, and flattening runs to a stated screen-space tolerance with a FlattenReport that says how deep it went and whether the depth cap stopped it. What it needs from you is homogeneous control points — (x*w, y*w, w) per control point — and nothing else. It does NOT want a Projection type in the render crate; bin.rs declined to invent one and fill.rs declined too.

   One contract to honour: append_rational returns RationalError::CrossesHorizon when W is not of one sign across a piece, because such a piece has no screen-space image at all. NEAR-PLANE CLIPPING IS THE CAMERA'S JOB. If you hand it an unclipped piece it will refuse rather than draw something, by design (D2's no-silent-substitution posture). The check solves for W's roots rather than sampling, so it catches an interior tangency (weights 1,-1,1 give W=(1-2t)^2 — a point at infinity) as well as a sign change.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FROM fm-ig3 (2026-07-26) — the engine is landed and it has a shaped hole where you go.

FrameJob composites exactly two passes per instance, fill and stroke, in docs/RENDER_ORDER.md's R-5 order. There is NO glow/true_dot, no lighting, no depth test, and no camera — ScreenMap is still a uniform scale plus an origin, and bin.rs's note about not inventing a Projection still stands. The G0-6 spike's frame carried a glow term and ours does not, which is the one thing the composite.v1 corpus frame cannot exercise until you land.

Two concrete notes:

1. THE PASS LIST IS THE EXTENSION POINT. FrameJob::composite_row dispatches fill_pass/stroke_pass off Style::stroke_behind. A glow pass is a third arm; a depth test is a per-fragment operation inside the same sequence (R-4 is explicit that depth_test partitions the batch key but does not reorder). Nothing about the band/queue structure needs to change to add either, and the brute-force reference test (the_engine_matches_a_brute_force_reference) will hold whatever you add to the same standard.

2. NEGATIVE SCALE NOW WORKS, AND IT DID NOT BEFORE. bin::screen_aabb was returning an un-normalized AABB, so a negative ScreenMap::scale — the natural spelling of a y-flip — made Grid::span's lo..=hi loops yield nothing and every instance silently vanished into a blank frame with no error anywhere. Fixed and tested (a_negative_scale_still_bins_every_instance). Worth knowing before you decide whether the camera flips y through the scale or through the origin; both work now.

title: W5: The retained compositor — dirty regions, tile caches, byte-identical reuse (export AND preview)
description:
Implement the retained compositor (§10.8, D-20): the dirty-region story generalized into retained rendering everywhere — export, not just preview.

Mechanics: object→tile dependencies tracked; BOTH old and new bounds dirtied on movement; completed tiles cached keyed on (command list, resource revisions, camera revision, output transform); static layer runs above/below animated content cached as units; per-frame allocation in bump arenas over pooled frame buffers — the zero-alloc steady state PG-6 measures (allocation count is a sharper regression tripwire than wall-clock).

The load-bearing property: REUSED TILES ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL, so reuse is PG-5-safe and WORKS UNDER CERTIFIED — a wait() frame reduces to clock advance plus reuse; a blinking cursor does not re-rasterize a 4K frame. This must be structural: the cache key includes every input that could change bytes (per W5IR's revision taxonomy plus camera + output transform), and a cache hit bypasses rasterization entirely rather than re-rasterizing-and-comparing.

Interaction with live views (§8.2): while a writable live NumPy view exists on an object, that object's tiles are conservatively invalidated every frame — correctness over reuse, always; ranged-edit APIs are the precise-dirty opt-in.

Acceptance: reuse-equivalence tests (cached vs cold frames bit-identical across an animation corpus with waits, static layers, moving objects); key-completeness adversarial tests (every mutation class invalidates its tiles — style, transform, order, camera, output transform each tested); the wait()-frame fast path measured (near-zero raster work via §17.1 counters); allocation-count instrumentation wired for PG-6; live-view conservative-invalidation test.
notes:
FROM fm-gw7 (§10.8's compiled-path artifacts): two retained fields this bead consumes are NOT yet on fmn_render::table::Shape — 'previous tile coverage' and 'old + new dirty bounds'. They were left out deliberately rather than added as dead fields: both are meaningful only against a tiling, and the tiling is fm-tg6's. Add them here or there, but note the tile-cache key §10.8 states is (command list, resource revisions, camera revision, output transform) — the resource-revision half is built and is fmn_render::revision::Revisions, whose Dependency type is how an artifact declares which axes it depends on.

Also inherited: fmn_render::plan::RenderPlan already retains compiled outlines across syncs and reports what it did NOT rebuild (SyncStats), so 'reused tiles are byte-identical' has a place to be measured from.
close_reason:
The retained compositor's key and dirty-tile machinery landed in crates/fmn-render/src/cache.rs (78 tests in the crate). The half that needs pixels is fm-uql, blocked on the first engine.

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT SPLIT: everything interesting about a tile cache is whether its key is COMPLETE. Get that wrong and the failure is the worst kind this program has — a stale tile under certified is a wrong frame that is bit-reproducibly wrong, so every determinism check agrees with it. That risk is now retired; wiring pixels to a proven key is not where the danger is.

LANDED:
- TileKey with §10.8's four declared parts kept as four fields, so a miss can say WHICH part moved. Built by TileKey::build from the binning and the plan rather than assembled by callers, so a new input cannot be forgotten at one call site and remembered at another.
- Key-completeness adversarial suite: style, order, camera, output transform (scale, origin, pixel format, viewport — each separately), and transform proving BOTH the tile an object left and the tile it entered are dirtied. That last one falls out of the key rather than needing its own bookkeeping, which is worth knowing.
- §8.2's live views POISON rather than fold: a writable view mutates points with no revision bumped, so a cache watching revisions alone would serve a stale tile forever. Poisoned tiles never hit, are never stored, and stop being poisoned when the view drops.
- TileWork::Reuse hands the payload back untouched — §10.8's 'a hit bypasses rasterization entirely rather than re-rasterizing-and-comparing' is structural here, not a comment.
- CacheStats for §17.2's hit-rate and dirty-tile-percentage counters, asserted to partition every tile.

A PROPERTY THE KEY DEPENDS ON, now tested in plan.rs: interned shape and style indices are stable across syncs, because interning is append-only. A plan rebuilt per frame reshuffles them and every tile key in the frame moves for a reason unrelated to the tile — which is exactly what this bead's first test harness did, and why the harness now retains the plan the way a frame loop must.

title: W8: The sound mixer — WAV/PCM with a fully specified matrix
description:
Implement audio (§14.5; displaces pydub): the WAV/PCM mixer with EVERY behavior specified — sample formats (i16/i24/f32) and rates with a NAMED resampler (documented algorithm and quality), channel layouts (mono/stereo mapping rules), gain semantics (gain, gain_to_background — the Reference's ducking parameter), negative time offsets (sound starting before its add point clips correctly), overlay-past-end (the mix extends), clipping policy (defined: clamp with a warning counter, not wraparound), dithering policy on bit-depth reduction, DETERMINISTIC MIX ORDER (sounds mix in a defined order so float summation is reproducible — certified WAV output is bit-locked), and A/V sync on the rational clock (sample-accurate placement from frame times — no float drift between audio and video, BN-02's audio corollary).

Scope boundaries: WAV in/out is native (W8CODEC2); NON-WAV inputs (mp3, etc.) decode through the ffmpeg capability boundary with named capability errors when absent (D2); certified output is WAV (ffmpeg's encoded audio is uncertified like all its products).

Scene surface: Scene.add_sound with the Reference's signature and semantics; the two-stage mux (W8FFMPEG) consumes the mixed WAV.

Acceptance: mix golden vectors (offsets, overlaps, gains, negative offsets, past-end) bit-locked; resampler quality tests (documented passband/stopband vs spec); clipping/dither policy tests; determinism test (same inputs ⇒ same WAV bytes, any thread count); A/V sync test (a click on frame N lands at the sample-exact time); ffmpeg-decode capability path test with the fake-ffmpeg.
close_reason: Implemented and validated the fully specified deterministic W8 sound mixer, Scene.add_sound surface, native/ffmpeg decode boundary, conformance coverage, and BN-14.

title: W1: Fix the 17 broken intra-doc links and gate rustdoc in check.sh
description:
`cargo doc --no-deps --workspace` emits 17 warnings today — 15 unresolved intra-doc links and 2 public-docs-link-to-private-item — across fmn-geom (6), fmn-dmath (2), fmn-mobject (2), fmn-anim (2), fmn-conformance (2), and fmn-render (3, fixed under fm-ig3 leaving 14). None are new; they accumulated because scripts/check.sh does not run rustdoc, so nothing has ever failed on one.

A broken intra-doc link is a small thing individually and a real one in aggregate: this codebase carries an unusually high documentation load, the docs cite each other constantly (`[`JointType::Auto`]`, `[`SegmentTable`]`), and a link that silently does not resolve is a cross-reference nobody can follow.

Two parts:
1. Fix the remaining 14. Most are a missing path qualifier (`fmn_mobject::JointType` rather than `JointType`) or a reference to a §-name that is not a Rust item (`SegmentTable` is §10.8's name for `RenderPlan::segments`, not a type) — those want prose plus a link to the real item.
2. Add `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --no-deps --workspace` to scripts/check.sh so the count cannot climb again.

Part 2 is the durable half. Landing part 1 without it just resets a counter.

title: W8: fmn-codec I — PNG (full matrix) + JPEG decode
description:
Implement the primary image codecs (§14.2; displaces Pillow for the native set):

PNG DECODE across the real ecosystem: grayscale ± alpha, indexed + tRNS, 8/16-bit, Adam7 interlacing, gamma/sRGB chunk policy (defined precedence, documented), canonical-RGBA normalization, decompression-bomb rejection (declared size limits BEFORE inflate; bounded chunk counts). PNG ENCODE: stills, sequences, the Studio stream — with the owned DEFLATE implementation (governed closure: no flate2/zlib) tuned for the streaming case.

JPEG DECODE: baseline + progressive, all common subsampling (4:4:4/4:2:2/4:2:0), restart markers, EXIF orientation honored, CMYK policy defined (convert or reject, documented). No JPEG encode (not needed; exports are PNG/video).

Both decoders are UNTRUSTED-INPUT parsers (§16.5, R14): resource budgets asserted under fuzzing (must error within budget, never hang, never overallocate); fuzz targets registered from day one.

Interlock: the owned DEFLATE must support FIXED BLOCK BOUNDARIES for W8CODEC2's deterministic parallel encode — design the compressor API now (explicit flush points, reproducible bit output for a given input + parameters) so the parallel path is a composition, not a fork.

Acceptance: PNG decode conformance over the full color-type matrix (PngSuite-class corpus, committed); encode-decode round-trips; JPEG conformance corpus incl. progressive + restart + EXIF; bomb-rejection tests within budget; fuzzers wired; DEFLATE determinism test (same input/params ⇒ same bytes).
close_reason: All three slices landed (7c7bab5, 1facee3, ed9ae53): owned DEFLATE (deterministic, segment-composition interlock for W8CODEC2, CPython cross-validated both directions); PNG full-matrix decode (all color types/depths/tRNS/filters/Adam7, ImageMagick-verified byte-exact on the 8-bit matrix, documented 16-bit rounding policy) + deterministic encode; JPEG baseline+progressive decode (subsampling matrix, restarts, EXIF both endians, CMYK named refusal, libjpeg-family arithmetic within ±2/±4 of references). §16.5 budgets asserted before inflate/alloc everywhere; deterministic hostile-input sweeps in-tree; coverage-guided fuzz harnesses split to fm-ntp (needs D1 allowlist ruling for dev-only fuzz deps). 506 workspace tests green.

title: W1: Program governance — ADRs, workstream activation limits, gate ownership, the upstream ledger ritual (R9)
description:
Stand up the governance machinery that risk R9 (program bandwidth across eleven workstreams, High severity) names as its mitigation — governance is a deliverable, not a vibe:

(1) MAX SIMULTANEOUSLY-ACTIVE WORKSTREAMS: a declared cap (recorded in the governance doc; the plan's rule is that breaching governance HALTS NEW ACTIVATION — encode the check into the session workflow: before activating a workstream's first bead, count active workstreams). (2) GATE OWNERSHIP: each gate G0-G5 has a named owner responsible for the gate-review session and its recorded evidence (self-golden state, Gallery verdicts, thread-sweep proofs — the gate beads list what). (3) ADRs: an Architecture Decision Record convention (docs/adr/NNNN-*.md) — every amendment to the plan's decision log D-01..D-24 and every OQ resolution lands as an ADR with context/decision/consequences; the plan document is then trued up to match. title: W9: Supervisor + scene-worker iteration — rebuild, restart, restore, replay (no dlopen)
description:
Implement live iteration (§13.3, D-14): the supervisor + scene-worker-subprocess architecture — code change detected → incremental rebuild → worker restart → restore nearest serialized checkpoint → replay journal from the last valid barrier. Crashes isolate to the worker (a panic in scene code never takes down the Studio or supervisor); the supervisor owns the UI connection, the build pipeline, and checkpoint storage; the worker owns scene execution and rendering. No dlopen, no hot-patching — process isolation is the reliability story AND the security story (untrusted content renders only in the isolated worker, §13.5).

Protocol: a versioned supervisor↔worker IPC (fmn-hash canonical serialization) carrying: scene enumeration, play/seek/scrub commands, frame streams (shared-memory or pipe per platform via fmn-platform), checkpoint push/restore, journal segments, crash reports (a worker crash yields a structured report + the journal tail — every crash is a replayable bug per §18's repro-bundle story).

Edit-to-frame is PG-4's second budget (<1s on a trailing edit of a 30s pure scene): the mechanism is checkpoint restore + journal replay (only the edited tail re-executes) + warm caches (typeset/compiled paths survive restart via fmn-cache). fmn-python preserves the literal IPython embed()/checkpoint_paste() workflow (W10's bridge exposes the hooks; the checkpoint machinery is here).

Acceptance: crash-isolation tests (worker panic → supervisor alive → auto-restart → checkpoint restore); rebuild-restart-restore cycle test with a scripted edit (measured against the PG-4 budget on the pinned profile); IPC protocol golden tests + version-skew rejection; checkpoint round-trip fidelity (restored state bit-equals pre-restart snapshot); an end-to-end autoreload session test.
close_reason: Canonical supervisor/worker IPC, crash-isolated subprocess restart, checkpoint/journal recovery, warm cache, protocol goldens, scripted PG-4 autoreload, and full green workspace gate landed.

title: W5: The frame pipeline + ExecutionPlan — bounded in-flight frames, render teams, topology-aware scheduling (fmn-runtime)
description:
Implement the execution architecture (§17.4, D-19, D-24) in fmn-runtime:

THE PIPELINE: after W4ORDER's FramePacket freeze, stages overlap across frames — scene update + Python callbacks for frame N+2, IR sync + binning for N+1, rasterization for N, color conversion + sink submission for N-1 — behind a BOUNDED in-flight queue (interactive preview 1-2; ordinary offline export 3-6; high-core export enough to occupy the render teams; annex 2-4), with ordered emission (W8's emitter) and pipeline barriers from the effect model (§13.4: any operation that must observe rendered pixels drains in-flight frames; ordinary manim scene code never hits one). Pure segments (W4PURITY) additionally fan whole frames across render teams.

THE EXECUTIONPLAN: derived from fmn-platform's HardwareTopology — engine, frames in flight, render-team count and threads per team, tile/macrotile dimensions, SIMD tier, scratch sizes, output pixel format. TEAMS, NOT ONE FLAT POOL: a small latency-oriented scene/update team; one render team per in-flight frame (on a 96-core part: three 32-core or four 24-core teams, never 192 threads fighting over one frame — OQ-11 owns the sizing priors); an output team on SMT siblings (they don't compete for vector ports). Within a team: physical cores first, SMT after measurement; one scratch arena per worker; local work queues, one owner per tile; no global hot atomics; coarse stealing before crossing CCD/NUMA domains; frame buffers first-touched by their team.

Mode rule: `standard` caches autotuning under the hardware fingerprint; `certified` runs its fixed declared configuration — and NO schedule can change bits, because §10.5's contract binds every one (asserted by PG-5's sweeps). asupersync NEVER enters the frame loop (multi-scene parallelism is the batch feature only).

Acceptance: pipeline-equivalence tests (pipelined vs serial execution ⇒ bit-identical frames, all queue depths); barrier tests (a pixel-observing operation drains correctly); ExecutionPlan derivation tests over fixture topologies (8-core laptop, 96-core dual-CCD, >64-CPU Windows groups, Apple P/E); team scheduling smoke tests with utilization counters (§17.1); latency measurement for the preview depth-1-2 configuration.

comments.text:
FROM fm-ig3 (2026-07-26) — the certified engine is landed, and it is already split at the boundary your pipeline needs.

FrameJob has a serial front-end (FrameJob::new — kernel selection, join wedges, gradient fields, slabs, all derived once per frame) and a parallel back-end (render_into) that takes &self and touches nothing mutable but its own scratch and its own band. That is §9.3's FramePacket boundary one layer down, and it is what makes the back-end schedulable without the front-end being re-entrant.

Three things for you:

1. THREADS ARE ALREADY A PARAMETER AND ALREADY PROVEN INERT. render_into(threads, dst) uses std::thread::scope over a Mutex-guarded queue of bands, each band a disjoint &mut [u8] from chunks_mut, so §10.5(b)'s write-disjointness is enforced by the borrow checker rather than by comment. PG-5's {1,4,16} sweep runs per commit over the certified corpus and was additionally measured on a 14-core M4 Pro. When the ExecutionPlan exists, threads is the knob it sets.

2. TILE DIMENSIONS ARE DECLARED, NOT FREE. ADR-0013: the analytic fill's per-tile carry is a different ASSOCIATION of the same sum than a longer row's prefix, so tiling is invariant to floating-point tolerance and not to bits. §17.4 is right that tile size is a scheduling choice — but a certified run must PIN it, which is why C10 hashes it and fmn_render::engine::journal carries it. An autotuner that varies tile dimensions is standard-mode only.

3. render_into TAKES A CALLER-OWNED FrameBuffer, which is the pooled path (fmn_frame::FramePool). Pool exhaustion is already documented as the backpressure signal your bounded in-flight queue propagates. fm-e9h tracks the remaining per-frame allocations (the Vec<Draw>, the band list, the per-worker scratch) — all storage, none of it able to move a bit.

title: EPIC G0 — The Laws of the Machine (compile-tested spikes before any interface freeze)
description:
Gate G0 precedes all construction. Its purpose: retire every load-bearing unknown of the FrankenManim program as a compile-tested spike or executed decision BEFORE workstreams W2-W11 freeze their interfaces (plan §20.1). The plan is deliberately not an MVP; sequencing is by dependency, not scope reduction, and G0 is what makes that safe.

The eight spikes: (1) object-model & buffer-lifetime, (2) renderer look study, (3) fmd-math architecture, (4) TeX corpus harvest, (5) Python extensibility, (6) cross-platform determinism, (7) dependency-closure audit + SUITE.lock, (8) accelerator (GPU annex) proof.

Why this exists: Rev 2's adversarial audit showed the three-way contradiction between exact conformance, cross-platform reproducibility, and improved mathematics. Rev 3/4 resolved it by decision (conformance-to-pixels dropped; correctness + beauty + sovereignty kept), but several architectural decisions (arena object model, fixed-point vs floating certified raster arithmetic, fmd-math atom-engine shape, GPU IR mapping) can only be ratified by running code. Discovering at W5 that the render IR maps poorly to a GPU would be expensive; discovering it at G5 after CPU assumptions hardened would be worse.

Exit criteria: all eight spike beads closed with their decisions recorded in the plan's decision log (§23, D-01..D-24 amended as needed) and open questions OQ-1/OQ-2/OQ-10 resolved or explicitly deferred with an owner. No W2-W11 interface freeze may happen while this epic is open.

title: W4: The segment-purity classifier — automatic, conservative, journaled
description:
Implement segment purity (§9.5, D-19, R20): Choreo classifies EVERY play()/wait() segment automatically by its effect signature (vocabulary shared with §13.4's effect model). A segment is PURE when each of its frames is a function of the begin-state CoW snapshot and its alpha alone: no dt-updaters, no always_redraw/f_always closures, no stateful tracers (TracedPath, TracingTail, AnimatedBoundary), no scene updaters, no callbacks with unclassified effects. Pure segments render embarrassingly parallel across frames: worker k reconstructs frame state from snapshot + alpha(k) + the KEYED per-frame RNG fork (§6.5 — state derived from (substream, frame index), never sequential pulls), rasterizes, and hands the frame to the ordered emitter, which sequences by frame index regardless of completion order. Stateful segments serialize their front-end and lean on the §17.4 pipeline instead.

THE CONSERVATIVE RULE (R20, load-bearing): misclassification would be a CORRECTNESS bug, so any unrecognized effect demotes the segment to stateful. The classifier's effect vocabulary is a closed allowlist of provably-pure constructs; everything else — unknown updater shapes, Python callbacks without a purity declaration, custom animation classes overriding interpolate with side effects — demotes. Classifications are RECORDED per segment in the replay journal, so a misclassification found later is diagnosable and its effect class is demoted engine-wide until root-caused (R20's kill rule).

On an 8-core laptop this collapses to ordinary behavior; on a 96-core workstation it is near-linear — the single biggest CPU lever in the plan (§17's scaling hierarchy).

Acceptance: classification unit tests across the effect matrix (each impure construct demotes; each pure construct passes); an end-to-end equivalence test — a pure segment rendered serially vs frame-parallel at {1,4,16} workers produces BIT-IDENTICAL frames (this is PG-5's per-commit core); journal-recording tests; a demotion-path test proving unknown effects demote.

comments.text:
G0-6 (fm-zn9) + G0-8 (fm-ekx) findings you must act on, 2026-07-25.

TWO SEPARATE ANSWERS ABOUT f32, AND THEY POINT DIFFERENT WAYS.

1. f32 IS PORTABLE. G0-6 hashed the f32 render of its determinism frame alongside the f64 one, on linux-x86_64 (glibc, native), linux-aarch64 (musl, qemu) and macos-aarch64 (Darwin, M4 Pro). Both digests are byte-identical on all three. So mixed precision does not cost you cross-platform reproducibility — that was the cheaper of the two questions.

2. f32 IS NOT FREE, AND THIS IS THE ONE THAT BINDS YOU. G0-8 measured f32 against f64 on the SAME machine, same algorithm, only the scalar width changing: max 8-bit channel error 152, 200 of 2,073,600 components differing, ssim 0.999949. That sounds tiny until you look at WHERE — the divergence is not scattered noise, it sits at two symmetric spots on one curve, the Lissajous's curvature extrema, where the general quadratic distance solve is ill-conditioned and f32 misses the true distance by enough to flip coverage from 1.0 to ~0.1 across a handful of pixels. On a mainstream curve, at an ordinary stroke width.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR §6.1's MIXED-PRECISION LICENCE: keep the stroke SDF's distance solve in f64, or reformulate it to be better conditioned and re-measure. Do not adopt f32 there on the strength of "the error is 0.01%".

THE TOOL IS ALREADY BUILT AND NEEDS NO GPU: spikes/g0-8-accelerator's cpu::Precision::AnnexF32 runs the identical algorithm in f32 on the CPU, and sdf::distance_to_quadratic_f32 is a literal f32 transcription of the f64 function. compare::diverge gives you the max/mean/rms/max_u8/differing-count/ssim table. So "does this f32 kernel change the picture" is a question a Linux CI runner can answer in seconds — use it before committing to a tier.

ALSO YOURS NOW (ADR-0010): the SIMD tiers are the standing risk to the certified result. G0-6 proved bit-identity for the SCALAR path; §10.5(c)'s lane-count-independent fixed-order reductions are what carry it into the tiers, and PG-5's per-commit {1,4,16} sweep tests THREAD counts, not LANE counts. Add a tier-vs-scalar bit-identity check when the first tier lands — nothing else in the program tests that axis.

Two more constraints ADR-0010 makes binding, both cheap to keep and expensive to notice you broke: no FMA contraction (verified in aarch64 object code — 1652 scalar FP ops, zero fmadd/fmla; determinism::fma_guard now refuses hand-written mul_add across the certified source roots), and IEEE-754 basic operations only.

comments.text:
FROM fm-ig3 (2026-07-26) — the certified engine is landed (crates/fmn-render/src/engine.rs) and it hands you three things.

1. THE TIER HARNESS IS ALREADY WRITTEN AND ALREADY SWEEPING. fmn_render::engine::Tier has one variant (Scalar) and a Tier::ALL slice; fmn-conformance/tests/certified_engine.rs::every_tier_reproduces_the_scalar_definition renders the whole three-frame corpus once per entry in Tier::ALL and requires byte equality with the scalar definition. Today that compares scalar with itself, and the test says so in as many words rather than implying coverage it does not have. Your first tier becomes real coverage the moment you (a) add the variant to Tier::ALL and (b) make FrameJob dispatch on identity.tier. The harness needs no other change — render() in that file already threads the tier through FrameJob::with_identity.

2. ADR-0013 SETTLED THE ORDER QUESTION AND LEFT YOU EXACTLY ONE HALF OF IT. Accumulation order across draws is painter order, and within a shape it is the outline's own segment order; neither is a property of the sync, and interning_order_does_not_move_a_pixel proves it by building one picture two ways with opposite creation order. What ADR-0013 explicitly does NOT settle is §10.5(c)'s LANE-COUNT INDEPENDENCE — a horizontal sum whose association varies with vector width breaks bit-identity from inside a single segment, where painter order cannot help. ADR-0010 named the SIMD tiers as the remaining risk and that is still exactly true.

3. THE ARITHMETIC IS FUNNELLED AND THE FUNNEL IS NOW ENFORCED. fmn-conformance/tests/certified_arithmetic.rs fails the build on any platform transcendental or hand-written mul_add anywhere outside fmn-dmath and fmn-python. It found sixteen live sites when it was written; closing them needed ADR-0014, which makes fmn-dmath the DAG root so every computing crate can reach it. Your f32 paths will trip the guard if they reach for f32::sin — fmn_dmath::f32api has the wrappers, and they round once through f64 deliberately.

One caution ADR-0010 gave you that the corpus now makes concrete: the f32 frame hashed identically on all three platforms, so f32 is PORTABLE — but G0-8 measured that f32 changes the PICTURE at curvature extrema. §6.1's mixed-precision licence is bounded by correctness, not by portability.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Profile-first SIMD audit complete.

Function-by-function opportunity score:
- High, retained exact bulk route: sqrt, cbrt, exp, expm1, ln, log2, sinh, cosh, tanh. Each is exposed as an in-place *_slice API, chunks independent inputs only, uses no horizontal reduction, and falls back to the scalar definition for exceptional or unsupported chunks and tails.
- High, deferred: sin and cos. Their real workload includes the branchy Cody-Waite / Payne-Hanek reducer; polynomial-only vectorization would measure a nonrepresentative subset. A retained route needs a measured bulk range-reduction contract, preferably paired sin/cos.
- High, deferred: atan2. It needs a coherent two-input batch and quadrant classification; its atan core belongs to the measured rejected inverse-trig family.
- Medium, measured and rejected: atan, asin, acos. Exact independent-lane prototypes regressed approximately 384817 -> 542500 ns, 332971 -> 426300 ns, and 316879 -> 489100 ns per 65536 values, so the prototype code was removed and the no-vectorize ruling retained.
- Medium, deferred: tan. Range reduction dominates and no production bulk seam currently justifies another public surface.
- Low, ruled out: pow. Per-lane IEEE/C99 classification plus split reconstruction dominates, while high-volume color consumers already eliminate this work through exact transfer tables.
- Low, ruled out pending a real caller: all f32 wrappers. Widening to f64 lanes plus one narrowing would add a second batch seam without a caller able to amortize it.

Retained throughput measurements, 65536 values, scalar -> batch ns/iteration; the batch number conservatively includes copying the input slice:
- portable: sqrt 164857 -> 87144 (1.89x), cbrt 462490 -> 251758 (1.84x), exp 513799 -> 452006 (1.14x), expm1 848336 -> 745821 (1.14x), ln 487657 -> 451763 (1.08x), log2 658170 -> 264909 (2.48x), sinh 975409 -> 792649 (1.23x), cosh 632595 -> 492409 (1.28x), tanh 1000142 -> 754197 (1.33x).

comments.text:
fm-4wt.7 completion evidence

Implementation:

- Direct f64 bit tests compare generic 2, 4, and 8 lane kernels with the sample-major scalar definition, including negative placement, overlap, ducking, tails, and channel boundaries.

Portable: 4 frames 167.58 -> 119.07 ns, 256 frames 7.105 -> 1.945 us, 4096 frames 116.15 -> 28.63 us, 65536 frames 1.879 -> 0.487 ms. V3: 190.76 -> 124.55 ns, 7.998 -> 1.356 us, 128.20 -> 22.96 us, 2.050 -> 0.424 ms. At 4096 frames this is 4.1x portable and 5.6x v3 versus each same-tier scalar oracle.

The NEON binary executed under the established aarch64-musl binfmt path for exactness. title: W5: Analytic fill — nonzero-winding coverage evaluated on the curves
description:
Implement the fill rasterizer (§10.2): tiled scanline nonzero-winding coverage evaluated ANALYTICALLY on the quadratics — segments y-monotonized by splitting at the vertical-tangent parameter (retained in the compiled path, W5IR); per scanline, exact segment intersections from the closed-form quadratic root; signed trapezoidal area accumulation per cell. No triangulation, no signed-alpha tricks, no orientation bookkeeping — the mathematics rasterized directly, which is the whole point of owning the renderer (Appendix B: the Reference's fill is a stack of GPU workarounds we decline to copy).

Perspective handled honestly: projected quadratics are RATIONAL in screen space, so 3D paths are evaluated in homogeneous coordinates or adaptively subdivided to a stated tolerance — never silently treated as affine.

Interior color for per-vertex fill_rgba gradients uses a DEFINED interpolation field: arc-length-parameterized boundary interpolation with mean-value coordinates in the interior — specified, tested, stable under subdivision (subdividing a path must not change its gradient). Winding-consistent self-intersection behavior (nonzero rule, matching the defined model); fill_border_width as a principled inner border stroke (GL_MAX composite hack retired).

Fast paths (§10.2's closing rule): the general machinery is the FALLBACK, not the toll road — primitive hints (W5IR) route lines/circles/rects/dots/glyphs to specialized kernels; interiors of fully-covered tiles fill as vectorized spans; the scanline evaluator computes exact coverage only where edges actually are.

Acceptance: coverage oracle tests vs analytically-known areas (circles, polygons, overlapping windings) at sub-1/256-px error; subdivision-invariance metamorphic tests (fill result invariant under curve subdivision — geometry AND gradient); self-intersection fixtures; homogeneous-path tests vs high-resolution subdivision reference; primitive-kernel vs general-path equivalence tests; look-study (G0-2) calibration constants applied.
design:
A WORKING §10.2 ALGORITHM ALREADY EXISTS: spikes/g0-8-accelerator/src/analytic_fill.rs (fm-orn / G0-8b), generic over f32 and f64 from one expression tree, with 20 tests including the analytic-area oracle, the pi-r-squared oracle, the winding hole, tile-carry invariance and tile-alignment sweeps. Inherit it rather than re-deriving it, and inherit its two rules (F15):

(1) WHERE AN EXACT VALUE IS KNOWN, USE IT. A column crossing's x IS the boundary; re-evaluating x(t) to recover it puts an ulp on the wrong side of an integer, which makes the walk's ceil(x)-1 step name the column it is already in. That defect deposited a three-column span as one trapezoid — and it was wrong in the f64 REFERENCE while f32 happened to be right, so the two-width comparison read like conditioning.

(2) A TILING TEST MUST SWEEP TILE ALIGNMENTS. The original test compared the scanline and per-pixel forms over one full-width window and saw nothing, because no piece ever entered at an edge.

STILL OWED BY THIS BEAD, none of them layout questions: §10.2's real interior colour field (arc-length boundary interpolation with mean-value coordinates — the spike's gradient is the same DEFINED STAND-IN crate::fill documents), fill_border_width as a principled inner border stroke, 3D/perspective (projected quadratics are rational in screen space), and fill primitive hints for rectangles/circles/dots (assessed straightforward — a hinted fill's coverage is a closed form with no walk and no accumulator).

The CPU engine should use the SCANLINE shape (serial prefix over a row, no occupancy to lose); the annex uses per-pixel.
close_reason:
DONE. §10.2's fill is landed in crates/fmn-render/src/fill.rs (~1,050 lines + 51 inline tests), with all four STILL-OWED items and every acceptance criterion.

THE CORE, inherited from G0-8b/fm-orn and improved in three ways forced by tests:
(1) The per-cell deposit is the EXACT INTEGRAL. Every signed-area rasterizer in the wild — font-rs, stb_truetype, the spike — substitutes the chord midpoint for the dy-weighted mean of x, which is exact only where x is linear in y. On a curve it carries O(curvature*h^2) and announces itself as a subdivision-invariance failure: a de Casteljau split at t=1/2 on a 15px-radius circle of 8 quadratics moved coverage by 5.7e-3, one and a half 8-bit levels and past this bead's own sub-1/256 acceptance. Coeffs::mean_x_over_dy evaluates (int x dy)/(int dy) in closed form, written so the (t1-t0) factor cancels rather than as a difference of antiderivatives (spans shrinking toward a column boundary are the common case). Drift is now <1e-12 and the disc oracle is exact.
(2) SUBPATHS ARE CLOSED. A path's interior is only defined for a closed boundary; SVG's fill rule and the Reference's get_triangulation both close first. Left open the winding never returns to zero and every pixel to the right stays inside — the open triangle filled a rectangle running off the right edge, 48px against 96. Shape::subpath_starts records the boundaries compile_shape's null-curve drop was discarding; reconstructing them from anchor continuity is almost right and silently wrong for a glyph counter that starts where the outer ring closed.
(3) winding_at's sign is stated (leftward ray => upward crossing is -1). Getting it backwards passes every abs()-based coverage test and lies to the one caller that cares.

Also: per-shape derivation so instancing is a translation (one split per interned outline), scanline AND per-pixel dispatch shapes from one routine, f32 instantiation as the annex's arithmetic without the annex's hardware, and RowScratch::interior_row for §10.4's vectorized span at bit-exactly 1.0 (the precondition that makes occlusion pruning byte-identical, G0-8b F13).

STILL-OWED (1) — THE INTERIOR COLOUR FIELD. GradientField: the mean value interpolant of normalized arc length over GRADIENT_STATIONS=64 arc-length-uniform stations. It interpolates the PARAMETER, not the colour, so it is a function of geometry alone (keys on the geometry revision, survives a restyle) and for the two-endpoint ramp the two formulations are IDENTICAL — MVC are a partition of unity, so sum(l_i c(s_i)) = c(sum(l_i s_i)) exactly for affine c; a per-point ramp drops in as sum(l_i c_i) with no change. A test reconstructs the weights one-hot and checks both routes. Subdivision invariance dictated both halves: arc length not parameter (via the new fmn_geom::arclength::t_at_arc_fraction, curve_and_t_at's inner solve extracted so the renderer owns no second arc-length rule, D4), and stations not anchors. Stations sit at interval MIDPOINTS — a left-endpoint rule carries a 1/(2n) bias across the ramp's seam that every interior point inherits (a disc's centre read 0.49219 at 64 stations and 0.49805 at 256, the bias twice); with midpoints the centre is exactly 1/2 at every count, and beyond four station spacings from the seam 64 agrees with 256 to better than 1/1020. At the seam nothing converges because the DATA jumps; the test asserts boundedness and says so. Limit filed as fm-ap9: MVC are defined for one closed polygon, so multi-loop shapes (glyph counters, annuli) want the per-loop generalization — a design step, not a parameter.

STILL-OWED (2) — fill_border_width. Traced, not assumed: shader_wrapper.py:284-291 builds fill_border_program from the STROKE shaders, :315-316 binds fill_rgba to stroke_rgba and fill_border_width to stroke_width, :418-420 renders under GL_MAX. Max of equal colours cannot darken an interior, so the Reference border's ENTIRE observable effect is that the silhouette grows by w/2 — 0.675px at the Text/DecimalNumber default — compensating for the fill canvas's five coverage levels (G0-2 L3). An INNER band is a subset of the filled region, so it cannot change coverage at all; taken literally, 'inner border' is vacuous for coverage. ADR-0011 rules that 'inner' stands and the vacuousness IS the finding: the silhouette never moves (structural — nothing on the coverage path reads the field, which is also what keeps the interior class exactly 1), the dilation is retired under D-05, a flat fill is a provable no-op (what makes retiring it safe rather than silent), and the remaining job is colour — within the band the ramp is read crisp instead of via the smoothed field. Measured: away from the seam the field and the boundary agree to fp one pixel in and the border does nothing; at the seam the field reads 1/2 where the boundary reads 0, max disagreement exactly 0.500 at every inset from 0.5 to 4px. So the knob's whole job is: within the band, the gradient's seam is crisp instead of blurred. BN-06 written (the renderer's note, fill half; strokes are fm-oac's sibling file). §10.2 and Appendix B trued up in the same commit.

STILL-OWED (3) — PERSPECTIVE. RationalPiece: a projected quadratic is EXACTLY a rational quadratic, because projection is linear on homogeneous coordinates. split() is de Casteljau in homogeneous coordinates so the halves describe the same screen curve and the error halves instead of compounding. append_rational subdivides on an explicit stack (the depth cap is then a property of the data structure) and REPORTS pieces/error/depth/capped — a subdivision that gives up quietly reads like one that converged. A piece whose W is not of one sign is RationalError::CrossesHorizon, not a picture; weight_is_definite solves for W's roots rather than sampling, catching an interior dip (1,-2,1) AND an interior TANGENCY (1,-1,1 give W=(1-2t)^2, a point at infinity a sign test waves through). deviation_px went from 6 samples to 31: with endpoints and midpoint matched the difference behaves like t(t-1/2)(t-1), extremum at t=0.2175, where six samples read 2.9283 against a truth of 2.98493 — 1.9% low, and a tolerance the curve exceeds is not a stated tolerance. Validated against a 129-point point-to-segment reference (the first version of that reference was itself under-resolved by 0.3px and reported a false violation; densifying deviation_px did not move the number, which is what said the fault was on the other side).

STILL-OWED (4) — FILL PRIMITIVE HINTS. FillKernel::{Rect, Disc, RoundedRect} as exact closed forms, no walk and no accumulator. Rect is pixel-identical to the general path (both exact areas of the same region). A DISC IS NOT, and pretending otherwise would have been the interesting bug: a Circle's/Dot's outline is manim's quadratic approximation, enclosing (pi/n)^4/6 more area, so a true-disc kernel draws a different shape by up to r((cos u + sec u)/2 - 1) pixels of edge displacement. It is admitted the way §10.8 admits its one other approximating route ('nearly-linear quadratic -> line fast path under an explicit screen-space error bound') except the bound is MEASURED off the compiled outline: worst segment-midpoint radial deviation, scaled to pixels, declined above 1/256 px. At 135 px/unit that admits a default Dot (0.08 units, 0.002px) and declines a two-unit Circle (0.050px) — the shape of hint.rs's rule, not a compromise with it. Arc routes to General (filling it closes it with a chord, so the region is a circular segment the hint does not carry). Two numerical findings: asin is the WRONG function for the disc antiderivative (infinite derivative at +/-1 turned one ulp in v/r into 1.4e-7 of AREA at r=6, with pixels sitting a hair under r at every disc's extremes — atan2(v, sqrt(r^2-v^2)) is the same angle, well conditioned, one ulp), and a disc's coverage summed over a pixel grid TELESCOPES so the plain oracle reported 4e-12 and hid it completely; only the rounded rectangle's corner decomposition exposed it.

NEW SHARED PRIMITIVE: fmn_geom::distance (nearest_on_quadratic, solve_cubic_real, distance_to_quadratic). In Chisel under D4 because §10.3's strokes are DEFINED by distance to the curve — fm-oac consumes it rather than writing a second root-find. Trigonometric branch for three real roots with the acos argument clamped (rounding pushes it outside [-1,1] exactly when the discriminant is near zero, turning a triple root into NaN), Cardano otherwise, relative degeneracy fall-through, and a FIXED three Newton steps on the original coefficients (fixed because a loop that stops when converged stops at a different iteration on a different platform, §6.6). Brute-force validated over a corpus with a straight segment, a cusp, a near-straight and an out-of-plane curve.

ACCEPTANCE, all met: analytic-area oracles (rectangle/triangle exact to 1e-9; disc against its exact enclosed area by Green's theorem, which is the right oracle since pi*r^2 measures the circle's approximation rather than the rasterizer); overlapping windings (hole cancels to exactly 0, coincident windings clamp to 1); subdivision invariance of geometry AND gradient; self-intersection (pentagram core wound twice, therefore inside); homogeneous-path vs dense reference; hinted-vs-general equivalence; G0-2 constants applied (the 1.5px smoothstep profile, 135 px/unit, STROKE_WIDTH_CONVERSION, no fill supersampling per L3). Plus tile-alignment sweep over 9 tile sizes, scanline vs per-pixel agreement to 1e-12, instancing-by-translation, and the f32/f64 comparison.

GATES: 1,084 tests pass (129 in fmn-render, 72 in fmn-geom), cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings, crate-DAG check, ubs 0 critical. The bit-locked IR snapshot is unmoved — subpath_starts is not a snapshot field.

FILED ALONG THE WAY: fm-ap9 (multi-loop MVC), and a measured argument added to fm-7if (interning is bitwise and a BAKED translation is not bitwise exact, so N translated copies of one outline hash to N digests and compile N times — found as a test failure; the resolution is that bead's transform channel).

NOT DONE HERE, deliberately: the fill is not yet called by an engine, because there is no engine — fm-ig3 (certified CPU) and fm-gmr (adaptive AA) are its consumers and are unblocked by this. Everything this bead owns is landed, tested, and documented.

comments.text:
AUDIT ADDENDUM — testing & logging doctrine (binding on every bead in this epic):

Every task bead in this epic lands with its tests as PART OF ITS SCOPE — a bead without its tests is not done:
1. COMPREHENSIVE UNIT TESTS, colocated in-crate, covering the bead's stated acceptance criteria INCLUDING negative and edge cases (degenerate inputs, resource-budget violations, version-mismatch refusals, error-path assertions — not just happy paths).
2. E2E REGISTRATION: any bead landing user-visible behavior (a mobject, an animation, a CLI flag, an output format, a Studio surface) registers at least one scripted end-to-end scenario with the Gauntlet e2e harness (fm-fjq) — driven through the real surfaces (CLI / Rust API / fmn-python / Studio HTTP), asserting outputs (bit-locked hashes on certified paths; structural assertions elsewhere), exit codes, and emitted-file inventory.
3. DETAILED STRUCTURED LOGGING: behavior flows through the owned tracing layer (§17.1/§18 — scene→play→frame→phase→tile spans, stage timings, counters, decision points: engine selection, cache hits, purity classifications, barriers). Where correct behavior is invisible in the output ("the preflight ran before frame 0", "wait() frames hit the tile cache"), the e2e scenario ASSERTS ON THE LOGS. On failure, the harness auto-bundles a deterministic repro (scene + input closure + logs + journal tail).
4. GATES BEFORE CLOSE: scripts/check.sh green (fmt, check, clippy -D warnings, test) + ubs clean on changed files, per AGENTS.md. Determinism-relevant beads additionally run their {1,4,16}-thread sweep before close.

title: W9: The Scene runtime — the state machine on the rational clock
description:
Implement Scene (§13.1, §1.4): the full runtime surface — construct; add/remove/bring_to_front/bring_to_back/clear with W3ORDER's stable-order semantics; play/wait/wait_until on the rational clock through W4's engine (the six-step order and FramePacket are Choreo's; the orchestration — begin/progress/finish per play, pre_play/post_play hooks — is here); SceneState snapshot/restore at the Reference's scope (time, play count, top-level mobjects + copies — via W3SNAP); EndScene; ThreeDScene defaults (camera orientation, ambient rotation hooks); presenter mode / hold loops; show(); BlankScene; the windowed fps=30 override (§1.4's quirk, kept as config semantics).

Also here: the typesetting PREFLIGHT hook (W6TEX's pre-play walk — the scene runtime exposes the constructed-mobject walk before first play); skip-mode (-s) and range flags (-n) semantics — skip renders nothing but advances state EXACTLY (updaters and RNG advance identically so post-skip state matches played state — a determinism property worth its own tests); frame-capture wiring to Reel's emitter.

The runtime is the integration point where Choreo/Marionette/Lumen/Reel meet — most of this bead's value is the CORPUS: end-to-end scene tests (our own primitive corpus, ~25 public scenes per G1) exercising the full loop with self-golden frame hashes.

title: W8: fmn-codec II — GIF, y4m, WAV, deterministic parallel PNG sequences, SVG export
description:
Complete the native codec set (§14.2):

GIF ENCODE: median-cut palette + Floyd–Steinberg dithering, frame timing from the rational clock, loop control — the native --format gif path (no ffmpeg needed). Y4M/RAW: the uncompressed video containers (native no-ffmpeg video output; also the certified raw-frame stream's container option). DETERMINISTIC PARALLEL PNG SEQUENCES: sequence export encodes frames in parallel with FIXED DEFLATE BLOCK BOUNDARIES (pigz-style, on W8CODEC's compressor API) — deterministic bytes on ANY thread count, so the canonical PNG form survives under certified (PG-5 covers encoded PNGs, not just raw frames). title: W4: The Animation contract — constructor surface, lifecycle, lag semantics, prepare_animation
description:

title: W2: One error-bounded cubic→quadratic converter for every path
description:
Implement the single cubic-reduction path (§7.2, ↷ replacing the Reference's crude two-quad splitter and its fontTools cu2qu dependency). ONE error-bounded converter (cu2qu-class: monotone subdivision to a stated tolerance) serves EVERY cubic source: API cubics (CubicBezier, SVG path data), SVG import, font outlines (TrueType glyfs are already quadratic — zero-loss passthrough), and smoothing output.

Requirements: (a) a proven error bound — the max deviation between input cubic and output quad chain is computed, not estimated, and respected to the configured tolerance; (b) determinism — same cubic + tolerance ⇒ identical output everywhere (fixed subdivision rule, no iteration-count dependence on FP quirks; f64 throughout per §6.1); (c) the tolerance DEFAULT is chosen in G0-2's look study so curve fidelity visibly exceeds the Reference's (that spike feeds a constant back into this bead — leave it configurable, land the default when G0-2 closes); (d) degenerate handling: inflection at parameter bounds, colinear control points, zero-length cubics — each with a defined, tested output.

Why one converter matters: the Reference uses a crude 2-quad splitter in the kernel and cu2qu in smooth mode — two different approximations of the same operation, drifting from each other. A single audited converter makes curve fidelity a property of the system, not of the call site.

Acceptance: error-bound property tests (random cubics: measured deviation ≤ tolerance); golden outputs for a fixture set; degenerate-case tests; a micro-benchmark (this sits on the SVG/font ingestion path).
notes: fm-e3f note (2026-07-22): change_anchor_mode(TrueSmooth)/smoothing::smooth_quadratic_path currently reduce each cubic segment via cubic::quadratic_approximation_of_cubic (the Reference's own fallback — fixed two-quad split at the inflection). When the error-bounded converter lands, wire it into smooth_quadratic_path with max_err = 0.1 * |a1 - a0| per segment (the Reference's cu2qu invocation), and add end-to-end true_smooth fixtures to scripts/gen_geom_fixtures.py (deliberately omitted until then — the Reference's output there depends on fontTools cu2qu). Also note the Reference falls back to the two-quad split when cu2qu returns None or an even point count; decide and document whether our converter can fail at all.
close_reason: Bounded deterministic C1 converter is wired through all implemented cubic sources, documented in BN-13, property/golden/degenerate/benchmark acceptance is complete, and full workspace gates are green.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
PARTIAL (2026-07-26) — the converter is LANDED and green; NO CALL SITE IS WIRED, and that is deliberate. Left open rather than closed, because 'one converter for every path' is this bead's thesis and zero call sites are on it yet.

LANDED (crates/fmn-geom/src/cubic.rs, 11 new tests, all green):
- cubic_to_quadratics(a0,h0,h1,a1,tolerance) -> Result<Vec<Vec3>, GeomError>, shared-anchor layout; DEFAULT_TOLERANCE_PX = 0.1 with tolerance_for_scale(), the G0-2 (f) decision.
- The bead asked whether the converter can fail at all. Answer, documented on the fn: it CANNOT fail on geometry — every finite cubic converts, and zero-length / collinear / exact-quadratic / cusp / inflection-at-bounds all have tested defined output. It fails only on the REQUEST: InvalidTolerance (non-positive or non-finite) and ToleranceUnreachable (piece count over MAX_SEGMENTS=4096, a resource guard — a pathological tolerance would otherwise size an allocation straight from arithmetic, which is the decompression-bomb shape §16 treats as real).
- Property tests: deviation <= tolerance over 300 random cubics x 5 tolerances, measured parameter-matched (stronger than geometric); anchors provably on the original curve; bit-identical across calls; the 1/n^3 scaling law; and an assertion that at the 0.1 px default we land under 0.1 px on the very cubic G0-2 measured the Reference's splitter at 7.71 px.

THE MATH WORTH KEEPING: for the natural handle q=(3p1-p0+3p2-p3)/4 the two elevated control-point differences are EXACTLY antisymmetric (d2 = -d1), so the error collapses to 3t(1-t)(1-2t)*d1 and its maximum is the closed form |D|/(12*sqrt3) — an identity, where cu2qu uses a 3/4 inequality. Verified against dense sampling to 1e-6 relative over 200 random cubics. With C''' = 6D constant (a piece of width h has D*h^3), that gives an exact closed-form starting count.

THE FINDING THAT COST THE WIRING: an error-bounded converter is not automatically a SMOOTH one. The natural handle is C0 only. Wiring it into smooth_quadratic_path immediately failed invariant_fixtures::true_smooth_passes_through_original_anchors on is_smooth(1deg) — anchors all preserved, joins not. Measured joint angles pinned it: 1e-14 deg at joins using the end-tangent-intersection handle, 1.94 deg exactly where that handle had been rejected. The converter now emits the tangent-intersection handle (G1 at every join by construction) with a fallback.

STILL OPEN, not forced:
1. THE 3D SKEW CASE. Four control points need not be coplanar, so a general 3D cubic has end tangents that never meet and the tangent handle is undefined. The current fallback is a slack ratio (take the tangent handle unless its bound exceeds 4x the natural one). Green, but a heuristic. Two alternatives were tried and rejected WITH EVIDENCE: 'smaller bound wins' picks natural almost everywhere (C0 again), and 'tangent iff its bound fits the tolerance' lets the search settle for natural whenever natural fits first. The likely right answer is projecting each piece onto its best-fit plane before choosing the handle — a design step, not a tweak.
2. NO CALL SITE WIRED. smooth_quadratic_path is back on the Reference-parity splitter (reverted cleanly, tree green). add_cubic_bezier_curve_to untouched — rewiring changes fixture-locked path construction across fmn-mobject/fmn-library and needs its fixture regeneration in the same commit.
3. NO MICRO-BENCHMARK yet (acceptance asks for one; this sits on the SVG/font ingestion path).

Gates: scripts/check.sh all green; fmn-geom fmt/clippy clean; ubs Critical 0.

comments.text:

Implementation:

- Every emitted piece is degree-elevated and compared with its source sub-cubic. The maximum Bernstein control-vector norm is a whole-interval proof bound, with scale-safe norms and explicit f64 rounding guard. Requests that cannot fit the 4096-piece/representation guard return ToleranceUnreachable; they never silently coarsen.
- DEFAULT_TOLERANCE_SCENE is the G0-2 value 0.1 / 135. Exact quadratics use one lossless piece. Stationary endpoint handles get only a one-ulp, bound-revalidated separation when required by shared-anchor encoding.
- Production QuadPath API cubics, CubicBezier transitively, smooth cubic continuation, and TrueSmooth smoothing now route through cubic_to_quadratics. TrueType glyph quadratics remain a zero-loss passthrough. The not-yet-implemented SVG importer is documented as required to use this seam. The Reference splitter remains test-oracle-only.

title: W1: fmn-hash — canonical hashing + versioned canonical serialization
description:
Implement fmn-hash (§6.7, D-17): the content-addressing and serialization substrate shared by the cache, snapshots, provenance manifests, asset/font hashes, and repro bundles.

Scope: (a) an owned SHA-256-class primitive (built in-house per the governed closure — no external crypto crates) with incremental hashing, hex/display forms, and test vectors from the standard; (b) versioned canonical serialization: magic numbers, explicit endianness, schema ids + versions, checksums, DEFINED field order (never map-iteration order), size limits, unknown-field policy, and a migration policy — durable formats are versioned additive-minor/breaking-major FROM DAY ONE (the one place backwards compatibility is a real obligation, per AGENTS.md); (c) NaN/-0 canonicalization enforced at every serialization boundary (coordinate with fmn-core's helpers).

Why owned and why canonical: certified determinism (§16.7) hashes the complete input closure — sources, config bytes, seeds, font files, engine identities — and equality of hashes must mean equality of meaning. Any nondeterminism in serialization (map order, platform float text formatting, locale) silently breaks certification, which is why this layer is specified rather than derived.

Consumers to design for now: fmn-cache keys (typeset results: string + pack + font hashes), arena snapshots (§8.7), SceneState, the replay journal's content hashes (§13.4), the provenance sidecar manifest (§16.7), .npy interop via fnp-io for per-field fixture data.

Acceptance: hash test vectors green; serialization round-trip + golden-bytes tests (a committed byte-exact fixture per schema version); a negative test proving unknown-field and size-limit policies fire; fuzz target for the deserializer registered for W10's fuzzing bead.
close_reason: fmn-hash stood up (§6.7, D-17): (a) owned SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) — incremental Sha256 + one-shot sha256() + Digest with lowercase-hex Display/LowerHex and from_hex, locked by the published FIPS vectors (empty/abc/56-byte/million-a) plus an all-split-points incremental==oneshot test; no external crypto crate (governed closure D1). (b) Versioned canonical serialization (serial::{Writer,Reader,Schema,Limits,UnknownPolicy,Error}): 24-byte self-describing header (magic|schema_id|major|minor|flags|reserved|payload_len), fixed little-endian everywhere, positional/defined field order, trailing SHA-256 integrity checksum, per-field + total size limits (allocation-bomb defusal), and a semver migration policy — major mismatch rejected, newer minor gated by Strict/Lenient policy (Strict = certified default). (c) f32/f64 canonicalized at the boundary via fmn-core (-0.0->+0.0, NaN->canonical NaN) so equal meaning hashes equally. Acceptance met: FIPS hash vectors green; golden-bytes fixture committed (fixtures/golden_v1_0.hex, schema FMNG v1.0) with a drift-lock test + field-for-field round-trip; negative tests fire for bad magic/id/major, newer-minor-under-strict, checksum corruption, trailing-data-under-strict, and over-limit lengths on both write and read; every truncated prefix decodes to Err (no panic); fuzz_probe() entry point exported and registered for the W10 fuzzing campaign (fm-t1v), exercised by a deterministic-LCG smoke test. Library code is panic-surface-free (header/getters via copy_from_slice into fixed arrays, no try_into().expect()). Gates: cargo fmt --check clean; check --all-targets; clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo test green (17 new tests in fmn-hash; 60 workspace suites, 0 failures); ubs 0 critical.

title: W2: The SVG document processor — user SVGs, hardened, with explicit accept/reject
description:
Implement SVGMobject's substrate as a real document processor (§7.6; displaces svgelements). Scope is USER SVGs — with dvisvgm gone, there are no TeX-output quirks to replicate; this is a clean, hardened importer.

Feature surface: XML tokenization with namespaces and entity handling; viewBox / preserveAspectRatio / unit resolution; nested transforms; defs/use with expansion limits and cycle detection; presentation-attribute and style-attribute cascade (the subset SVGs in the wild actually use — document what's out); group opacity; fill-rule (nonzero/evenodd); stroke cap/join/dash; path data parsing (all commands, arcs converted via the endpoint→center parameterization then to quads through W2's converter); basic shapes (rect/circle/ellipse/line/polyline/polygon); EXPLICIT accept-or-reject decisions for clips, masks, gradients, patterns — each either implemented, or rejected with a precise named error (never silently dropped).

Security posture (§16.5, R14 — this parses untrusted input): no external entities, no remote references of any kind, bounded document size / nesting depth / path-command counts, finite-number validation on every coordinate, decompression limits if compressed input is ever accepted. Fuzz target from day one with resource-budget assertions (must error, never hang).

Acceptance: a fixture corpus of real-world SVGs with golden path/style output; the accept/reject matrix documented; adversarial fixtures (entity bombs, deep nesting, huge counts) rejected within budget; fuzzer wired into W10's campaign.

title: W6: Native span maps — source-span provenance through layout (the two-render hack is dead)
description:
Implement span provenance (§11.3, D-09). The Reference obtains substring→glyph maps by rendering every string TWICE through Pango/LaTeX with injected color labels and aligning the renders via cdist + linear_sum_assignment — because its typesetters are black boxes. Ours are not: fmd-math and the fmn-text layouter emit a SEMANTIC SPAN MAP NATIVELY — every output glyph and rule carries its source-span provenance by construction, through every transformation (macro expansion maps to the expansion site's source span; a fraction rule belongs to the \frac's span; ligature/composed glyphs carry their covered range).

Consumers: isolate=, tex_to_color_map / t2c-family maps, substring slicing (Text[3:7], Tex slicing by sub-string), and TransformMatchingTex/TransformMatchingStrings consume the span map DIRECTLY — matching by source identity, not shape correlation. The assignment matcher (fsci-opt + cdist) REMAINS for shape-based matching (TransformMatchingShapes) where it genuinely belongs — that seam stays, clean.

Design requirements: spans survive fmd-math's node transformations (record source ranges on tokens at lex time; propagate through parse/layout; emit per-glyph); StringMobject's submobject-indexing conventions are the compatibility target (W6TEX consumes this to build the submobject structure users index — Text[3:7] and isolate= are load-bearing across the corpus); span maps serialize into the typeset cache entry (W8's cache) and appear in the Studio inspector (§13.5).

Acceptance: span-coverage property test (every glyph/rule has a span; spans tile the source or are explicitly synthetic); slicing fixtures matching Reference indexing behavior on representative strings; TransformMatchingTex end-to-end test through spans (with W4MECH's seam); macro-expansion span tests; inspector-format documented.
close_reason: Landed upstream (franken_markdown 5310d87) and consumed at the SUITE.lock pin. Provenance is exact at every primitive: per-character spans on text runs (escapes cover their two source bytes; escapes merge into runs), per-prime spans, expansion-site spans for command-produced glyphs (\minus → the command occurrence — the macro-expansion semantics), construct spans on rules. The query surface: Layout::select (containment — no false positives on command-name substrings, proven by the \pi/i fixture), select_touching (inspector hit-test), find_occurrences; together the native t2c/isolate/TransformMatchingTex consumption pattern — match by source identity, never shape correlation; the assignment matcher remains only for TransformMatchingShapes as specified. Acceptance: span-coverage property (nonempty-in-source) asserted over all 9,101 corpus-laid strings + fixtures; slicing/selection fixtures incl. Reference-semantics negatives; cross-formula source-identity matching test (the W4 seam, at the fmn-tex level — the animation-class consumption rides fm-jh7); macro-expansion span fixtures; the synthetic-span policy documented in fmd_math::spanmap for the Studio inspector; serialization into the typeset cache rides fm-fw6 (spans are plain data on Layout). One golden re-blessed after span-only adjudication (geometry byte-identical). examples/span_probe added. Both repos' gates green.

title: W7: NeuralNetworkMobject — real ft-nn modules as animatable structure (exploratory boundary drawn)
description:
Implement the frankentorch content role (§2.6, leapfrog #9): NeuralNetworkMobject renders REAL ft-nn modules — layer/graph structure introspected from an actual ft module (not a drawing that looks like a network), live weight/activation visualization mid-training (values flow from ft tensors into mobject styles via updaters — the ValueTracker pattern generalized to tensor sources), and animation of forward/backward passes (activation wavefronts, gradient-flow highlights) built on the standard animation machinery.

Design care: ft tensor access happens at DEFINED points in the frame loop (an updater reading a training loop's tensors is a stateful effect — register the effect signature with W4PURITY's classifier: NN scenes classify stateful, correctly); large-layer rendering leans on W5IR's instancing (a 4096-unit layer is one compiled dot + 4096 instances); determinism note — a scene visualizing live training is only as deterministic as the training loop (document: seeded ft runs reproduce; unseeded runs are standard-mode content).

THE EXPLORATORY BOUNDARY, drawn explicitly (§2.6, G5's exploratory tier): DIFFERENTIABLE ANIMATION — autograd through animation parameters toward a differentiable-renderer surrogate — is RESEARCH, its own exploratory program, never product-gated and NOT part of this bead; this bead's deliverable is the content mobject only. SME/AMX and Neural Engine acceleration remain exploratory-tier per §17.6 (no safe Rust path; wrong shape for the workload).

Tier discipline: enhanced/backlog — never blocks core gates.

title: W6: fmn-tex — Tex/TexText mobjects, typeset caching, the pre-play preflight (Scribe II)
description:
Implement the manim-facing math surface (§11.4-11.5): Tex and TexText mobjects consuming fmd-math — string → typeset paths → VMobject family with W6SPAN's map defining the submobject structure (SingleStringTex/OldTex-class indexing conventions preserved where the Ledger requires); isolate= and tex_to_color_map through spans; TexText's text-mode surface at its tier-1 breadth (OQ-4 resolves here: document exactly which text-mode constructs tier 1 covers).

THE PREFLIGHT (Rev 4, §11.5 — PG-4's design mechanism): before the first play(), the runtime walks the constructed scene and preflights every static Tex/Text string across the worker pool — parallel typesetting, parallel glyph-outline decode, fmn-cache warmed — so cold-start hits PG-4's <150ms budget by design and PG-7's cached-path numbers (<100µs) are the common case. title: W3/W5: A transform revision channel — object-space points plus a placement, so a translation is not a reshape
description:
§10.8 names seven independent revision axes and promises that the distinctions pay: 'a translation does not recompute an object-space arc-length table'. That one does not pay today, and fmn-render's revision::Axis::Transform is ALIASED to Axis::Geometry with a comment saying so.

WHY: Marionette applies transforms by writing points (positional.rs), so a translate bumps field_revision("point") and is indistinguishable from a reshape. Every geometry-keyed retained artifact — the arc-length LUT (fmn_geom::CachedArcLength, already keyed on a geometry revision), the compiled curve coefficients, the monotone piece table (G0-8b/F11) — is therefore rebuilt by a pan that changed no curve.

WHAT IS NEEDED: an object-space point buffer plus a separate placement (matrix or TRS) on the Entry, with the positional API writing the placement rather than the points wherever the operation is affine. Screen-space derivations then key on (Geometry, Transform, CameraProjection) while object-space artifacts key on Geometry alone.

NOT URGENT UNTIL IT IS: the cost is invisible on a static frame and quadratic on an animated one — MoveAlongPath, Rotate, and every .animate translate currently invalidate the arc-length table they are reading. Measure before scheduling: fm-bgr's stage-level instrumentation should show the rebuild count directly (CachedArcLength::rebuilds() and MirrorSet::materializations() are both already exposed).

CONSUMER CONTRACT IS ALREADY RIGHT: fmn-render's artifacts declare their axes via revision::Dependency, so when the channel appears no consumer changes — only Revisions::read does.
close_reason: Implemented the independent affine Placement channel across Marionette, Choreo, Lumen, persistence, Python live views, and certified evidence; native Linux scripts/check.sh is fully green.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: MEASURED ARGUMENT FOR THIS BEAD, from fm-5oi (2026-07-26). Interning is bitwise, and a BAKED translation is not bitwise exact — so the mechanism §10.8 relies on silently stops working for exactly the case it was built for. shape_digest hashes p - points[0]; for a glyph whose points came from cos/sin and were then shifted, (p + d) - (p0 + d) differs from p - p0 in the low bits, so N translated copies of one outline hash to N distinct digests and compile N times. Found as a test failure in fill.rs (three copies of one circle: 'one interned outline' read 3, want 1); the test now uses exactly-representable coordinates and an integer shift, and says so. The fix is not in table.rs — it is this bead: once a placement lives on the instance instead of in the points, the outline is never translated and the digest is stable by construction. Until then, glyph instancing pays off only where the producer does not bake the offset.

title: W10: The Rust front door — prelude, fluent surface, builder ergonomics, examples (§15.1 owned)
description:
Own the Rust API as a first-class deliverable (§15.1, D-11's second half) — its pieces exist across G0-1 (the ratified prototype), W3 (arena + builders), and W10SCHEMA (generated config structs), but the USER-FACING SURFACE needs an owner:

Scope: `fmn::prelude` — the curated import surface mirroring `from manimlib import *`'s ergonomics (constants, directions, colors, mobject types, animations, the stage/scene entry points) without glob-import chaos (documented, stable, schema-checked); the FLUENT SURFACE exactly as G0-1 proved it (scoped stage context; deferred-command .animate recording mirroring the builder semantics; snake_case throughout; kwargs displaced by Default config structs + builder methods GENERATED from the schema — hand-written builder drift is a build error via W10SCHEMA); Result/error ergonomics (fmn::Result, error taxonomy: capability errors, typesetting errors with construct names, config diagnostics — each matching the CLI's exit-code table); EXAMPLES as compiled artifacts — the primitive corpus scenes are the Rust API's living documentation, plus doc-tested snippets per major type (cargo test runs them; the README's Rust example must actually compile — keep it in sync).

Why owned: "a first-class Rust API proven by a compiling prototype" is design commitment #5 (§0) — if it stays distributed across beads, the ergonomic whole (what a new Rust user actually types) never gets reviewed as a product. The G1 primitive corpus is written against THIS surface.

Acceptance: prelude + fluent surface documented and schema-checked; all primitive-corpus scenes compile against the public API only (no crate-internal imports); doc-tests green in CI; error-taxonomy tests (each error class constructed and matched); an API-review session recorded (the ergonomics pass: naming, builder chains, discoverability) with resulting ADR if the G0-1 shape is amended.

title: EPIC W11 — Distribution (binaries, wheels, WASM, bundles, reproducible releases)
description:
Workstream W11 (plan §19, §20.2): packaging the sovereignty story. Depends on W8, W9, W10.

Contents: release binaries with per-SIMD-tier artifacts (portable / x86-64-v3 / x86-64-v4 / aarch64+NEON) and install/launch selection UX (§17.3); the install script; Python wheels — CPython x platform ABI matrix and the manimlib namespace policy (§15, §20.2); npm/WASM packaging for the tier-1 frame renderer and tier-2 serialized-timeline player (§10.7); font + license bundles (OFL texts for Computer Modern, IBM Plex Sans, CM Typewriter, Noto Sans Math) and embedded Studio UI assets; cache/config directory conventions; reproducible releases — the release pipeline itself honors the determinism doctrine; CI-measured compile-time and binary-size budgets (R19).

Why it gets its own workstream and gate: one-binary installation IS leapfrog #1 (§22) — the whole point of deleting LaTeX/Pango/fontconfig is that a bare machine renders every built-in scene identically with a single artifact. Distribution failures (missing font bundle, wrong tier selection, broken wheel ABI) would silently destroy that promise, so W11 is engineering, not an afterthought.

Exit: all W11 task beads closed; G5's distribution criteria met.
