title: W1: fmn-dmath — owned deterministic elementary functions (the certified transcendental layer)
description:
Implement fmn-dmath (§6.6, D-17): an owned, fixed-implementation elementary-function layer, because std's transcendentals defer to platform libm and differ across glibc/macOS/WASM — and this engine is transcendental-dense (arc construction, per-vertex atan2 joints, rate functions, glow falloffs, tanh normalization, Euler conversions).

Scope: sin, cos, tan, atan, atan2, asin, acos, exp, ln, log2, pow, sqrt, cbrt, tanh, sinh, cosh at minimum — f64 and f32 entry points; fixed polynomial/range-reduction implementations with DOCUMENTED accuracy bounds (state max ULP error per function per domain); bit-identical on every certified target (linux-x86-64, linux-aarch64, macos-aarch64, windows-x86-64 functional) — locked by cross-platform vector files in CI: a committed table of (input, expected-bits) pairs covering normals, denormals, near-branch-cut and near-singularity inputs.

Mode policy: standard mode MAY use fast paths (std/libm); certified uses fmn-dmath EXCLUSIVELY. The seam is a trait or function-table chosen at engine construction, never a scattered cfg.

SIMD posture (§6.6, §17.3): design the kernels as fixed-coefficient, fixed-order polynomials so they vectorize bit-reproducibly later — same operation order in scalar and every lane width. Do NOT vectorize in this bead; just don't preclude it (no table-lookup designs that defeat lanes).

Interlock: G0-6 (determinism spike) consumes a prototype of this crate; its cross-platform findings may force implementation adjustments — budget for one revision pass after the spike lands.

Acceptance: accuracy docs per function; cross-platform vector CI green; property tests (range reduction identities, symmetry laws); the standard/certified seam demonstrated in a test.
notes: In progress 2026-07-22: crate scaffolding + mode seam (Transcendentals table, CERTIFIED/FAST) + bits helpers landed; sqrt delegated (IEEE correctly rounded, documented). Ground-truth vectors committed: 16 files, ~9.6k (input-bits, correctly-rounded-expected-bits) pairs from mpmath prec=150 via scripts/gen_dmath_vectors.py, incl. denormals, near-branch-cuts, Payne-Hanek stress inputs. tests/vectors.rs asserts per-fn ULP bounds (sin/cos/atan/asin/acos/exp/expm1/ln/cbrt ≤1; tan/atan2/log2/pow/sinh/cosh/tanh ≤2). f32 API = f64 layer + single rounding (documented double-rounding caveat). FDLIBM-structure f64 implementations being written by three parallel subagents (trig+rem_pio2 / inverse-trig+cbrt / exp,log,pow,hyper).
close_reason: fmn-dmath landed: owned FDLIBM-structure f64 implementations of sin/cos/tan (+Payne-Hanek rem_pio2), atan/atan2/asin/acos, exp/expm1/ln/log2, full e_pow, cbrt, sinh/cosh/tanh; sqrt delegated (IEEE correctly rounded). f32 API = f64 + single rounding (documented). Mode seam = Transcendentals fn table (CERTIFIED/FAST) chosen at construction, demonstrated in test. Accuracy documented per module and enforced by tests/vectors.rs against 16 committed mpmath ground-truth vector files (~9.6k vectors incl. denormals, branch cuts, reduction stress): measured max 1 ulp everywhere within bounds (sin/cos/atan/asin/acos/exp/expm1/ln/cbrt ≤1; tan/atan2/log2/pow/sinh/cosh/tanh ≤2). Known inherited FDLIBM pow limitation for |y|>2^31 with |x-1|<2^-20 documented in module doc + dedicated test. All constants pinned via from_bits hex. Gates green; ubs critical = test-harness panic only. Built by 3 parallel subagents + integration; generator fix: mpf() collapses -0.0 (atan2 specials now via IEEE-exact libm).

title: W2: Scalar-field isolines + ear-clip triangulation utilities
description:
Two owned geometry utilities (§7.7–7.8):

(1) ISOLINES: an adaptive quadtree isoline extractor for ImplicitFunction (displaces the isosurfaces package), honoring the Reference's min_depth / max_quads API knobs as BUDGET semantics (the knobs bound work; they do not promise a particular mesh). Everything underdefined in the original is DEFINED here: traversal order (deterministic), truncation behavior when max_quads is hit (which regions coarsen, in what order), segment orientation convention, domain-boundary handling, and NaN/undefined-region behavior (functions may divide by zero — cells containing non-finite samples are handled by a stated rule, not UB). Quality target: "ours, and good" — adaptive refinement should visibly beat uniform sampling on curvature-varying implicit curves.

(2) EAR-CLIP: a polygon triangulator with hole support (displaces mapbox-earcut) — deterministic tie-breaks, honest acceptance criteria (valid triangulation of valid input; no Delaunay quality pretensions). It is a UTILITY for booleans' flatten fallback, mesh export, and future mesh work; the live fill path needs no triangulation at all (§10.2 rasterizes winding coverage analytically — that independence is a design feature, keep it).

Acceptance: isoline determinism tests (same field + budget ⇒ identical segments); budget-semantics tests (max_quads respected exactly); NaN-region tests; known-curve accuracy tests (circle/lemniscate implicit forms vs analytic); triangulator validity property tests (area preservation, no flipped/degenerate triangles, hole containment) over fuzzed polygons.

title: W3: Arena snapshots & serialization — SceneState, undo, replay barriers, fixtures
description:
Implement Marionette's persistence layer (§8.7): arena snapshots in the fmn-hash canonical format (§6.7), with per-field .npy export via fnp-io for fixture interchange. Backs four consumers with one mechanism: SceneState (§13.1 — time, play count, top-level mobjects + copies, at the Reference's scope), Studio undo, replay-journal barriers (§13.4 — snapshot at a barrier so replay can restore and continue), and the Gauntlet's geometry-snapshot self-goldens (§16.3 — lifecycle-point snapshots bit-locked per platform).

Scope boundaries stated honestly (§8.7, §13.4): NO claim to serialize Python closures — updater callables snapshot as identity + version hash (the effect model's callback-hash vocabulary); restoring across a code change that alters a callback invalidates the barrier (conservative invalidation is the replay bead's rule; this bead provides the hashes).

Format requirements: versioned schema id per §6.7's policy (additive-minor / breaking-major from day one — snapshots persist in caches and repro bundles); deterministic bytes (canonical field order, NaN/-0 canonicalization at the boundary, no map-order leakage) so that snapshot-hash equality is meaningful for the replay journal and self-goldens; size limits and corruption detection (checksums) on read.

Acceptance: snapshot/restore round-trip across representative scenes (geometry + uniforms + family topology + RNG state via fmn-core); byte-determinism test (same state ⇒ same bytes, twice, and across a re-open); versioning negative test (future-major refused cleanly); .npy field export readable by NumPy in a fixture-generation script.
close_reason: Durable snapshot codec over fmn-hash serial (FMNA/1+2): deterministic bytes, versioned schema, checksum+limits on read, handle re-binding for cross-stage restore, updater identity manifest per the §8.7 honesty clause, SceneState with RNG state words, per-field .npy export. 7 acceptance tests + npy export test; 452 workspace tests green.

title: G0-5: Python extensibility spike — real subclassing against the prototype bridge
description:
Compile-tested spike proving fmn-python's hardest promise before its contract freezes (§20.1 spike 5 → §15.2; risk R10, High). The manimlib compatibility claim is SOURCE compatibility with normal Python object semantics — which means dynamic subclassing must actually work against a Rust engine, not merely wrap it.

Scope — a real Python subclass exercising, against the prototype PyO3 bridge: overriding init_data / init_points / init_uniforms / interpolate with the ENGINE calling back into the Python overrides at the right lifecycle points (MRO/override dispatch, not static binding); arbitrary instance attributes in __dict__ participating in copy remapping; a custom data_dtype declared by the subclass flowing through the RecordBuffer schema machinery; live self.data["point"] structured-view mutation under the §8.2 view protocol; identity/hashing/weakref behavior across engine collection round-trips; exception mapping across the FFI boundary both directions.

Interlocks: consumes G0-1's object-model prototype (the Python proxy identity scenario is shared). Findings feed PG-8's class-tiered binding-tax budgets — measure and record the per-callback crossing cost observed, since the §15.2 binding-tax program (cached method resolution, batched crossings, GIL release windows) is designed against these numbers.

Acceptance: the spike subclass suite green against the prototype bridge; a written gap list — anything that cannot be honored gets tiered in the Parity Ledger BEFORE G4a per R10's pivot rule; measured crossing-cost numbers recorded for the W10 perf-rig baseline.
close_reason: G0-5 ratified (docs/g0/G0-5-python-ext-ratification.md). spikes/g0-5-python-ext: a NON-member pyo3 0.26 cdylib over the G0-1 arena (ADR-0003 fuzz-crate pattern: own committed Cargo.lock, 20 class=dev allowlist rows; the pending ffi row untouched — shipped consumption stays fm-aqv's decision). 29-test Python suite green: engine-driven init_data/init_points/init_uniforms/interpolate through real MRO (mixins + cooperative super() included); __dict__ copy remapping per the Reference Mobject.copy rule (family-internal remap, external shared, updaters by reference); subclass data_dtype through the RecordBuffer schema; §8.2 view protocol observed from Python (alias both ways, revision bumps, detach-on-resize); pin-backed identity/hash/weakref with delete-defers-under-pin finalizing on GC; exceptions mapped both directions (typed StaleHandleError/ForeignStageError; Python errors propagate out of engine loops intact). KEY FINDING — the reentrancy law (the question G0-1 deferred): the engine must never hold a state borrow across a Python callback; every callback window dispatches lock-free. Measured crossing costs seed PG-8: 47ns noop floor, 141-236ns data ops, 325-408ns engine→Python dispatch. Gap list (no Parity-Ledger demotion needed): tp_init shim via pure-Python manimlib base, NumPy buffer-protocol skin at W10, RecordSchema owned names at W3, copy/deepcopy/pickle protocols at W10, GIL windows unmeasured, sub-interpreters out of scope. governed_closure gained audit_with_aux (walks non-member locks; fuzz/Cargo.lock ready for fm-ntp). All gates green: 568 workspace tests + 29 spike tests, fmt/clippy clean, DAG green. Unblocks fm-aqv's contract; G0 epic needs only the hardware-gated spikes now.

title: W2: Planar path booleans — flatten-and-clip certified first, curve-aware pipeline behind topology-aware acceptance
description:
Implement path booleans (§7.4; displaces skia-pathops) in the plan's two-stage posture:

STAGE 1 (certified at W2, permanent): the deterministic FLATTEN-AND-CLIP boolean — flatten curves to tolerance, run a robust polygon clipper, return the result. Ships first as (a) the escape hatch for unsupported overlap classes, (b) the reference implementation for differential testing, (c) the primary fuzz target. Deterministic tie-breaks throughout.

STAGE 2 (progressive replacement): the curve-aware pipeline — fat-line-pruned quad–quad intersection with Newton polish, winding-number classification, and curve stitching — replacing the fallback class-by-class. Numerical posture: double-double predicates where needed, WITHOUT exactness overclaims; a WRITTEN topology spec per degenerate class (tangencies, shared endpoints, overlapping segments, zero-area lobes) before code handles it.

ACCEPTANCE IS TOPOLOGY-AWARE, not point-wise: point-in-fill sampling grids, winding-number equivalence, component/hole counts, Euler characteristic, boolean algebraic identities (A∪B = B∪A, A∖B ∩ B = ∅, ...), and multi-scale raster equivalence between stage-1 and stage-2 results; plus captured skia-pathops fixtures (generated once from the Reference toolchain) and adversarial fuzzing with resource budgets (pathological intersection counts are a DoS surface — §16.5).

Risk R4 rule: unsupported overlap classes route PERMANENTLY to the fallback rather than shipping wrong topology. Union/Difference/Intersection/Exclusion mobjects (W7) consume this.

Acceptance: stage 1 green under the full acceptance battery + fuzzing; stage-2 classes each land with their topology spec + differential tests vs stage 1.

Full repository gate and UBS are green. Unproved curve-aware topology classes remain correctly on the fallback and are tracked by dependent follow-up fm-qjy.

title: W8: fmn-frame — frame buffers, pixel formats, transfer functions
description:
Implement the frame substrate (§14.1): buffer types over pooled allocations (the preallocated ring the emitter and pipeline ride — no frame-sized allocation on the hot path, PG-6's zero-steady-state-alloc rule); pixel formats — RGBA8/BGRA8, RGBA16F intermediates where quality demands, NV12/P010 video planes (with correct chroma siting and range semantics), canonical RGBA for certified output; transfer functions applied ONCE, natively, at the defined point (the ffmpeg boundary's "no obligatory eq" rule depends on us owning transfer correctly); row-stride discipline (sinks negotiate stride; internal buffers may pad).

Format conversion kernels: linear-light RGBA16F → sRGB RGBA8; RGBA → NV12/P010 (BT.709 matrix, defined rounding — these are §17.3 hot-list adjacent: color transfer functions are named); orientation is ALWAYS output orientation — fmn-frame renders the right way up and no vflip exists anywhere in the system (D-23).

Certified interaction: canonical RGBA output bytes are part of the certified artifact set — conversion kernels on the certified path use fixed-order, defined-rounding arithmetic (W5CERT's rules extend here); NV12/P010 conversions are standard-mode (they feed ffmpeg, whose products are uncertified by construction).

Acceptance: format round-trip tests (within documented precision per conversion); NV12/P010 golden vectors vs reference matrices; pool reuse tests (steady-state render loop performs zero frame allocations — instrumented via §17.1); stride/negotiation unit tests; certified-conversion determinism tests.

title: W5: Mean-value colour field over multiple boundary loops (glyph counters, annuli)
description:
fm-5oi landed §10.2's interior colour field as the mean-value interpolant of normalized arc length over GRADIENT_STATIONS=64 arc-length-uniform boundary stations (crates/fmn-render/src/fill.rs, GradientField).

Mean value coordinates are defined for ONE closed polygon. For a shape whose path has several subpaths the stations currently run over the whole path in path order, so the station polygon connects one subpath's end to the next one's start. That field is defined, deterministic, and subdivision-invariant — the three properties §10.2 requires — and it coincides exactly with the region boundary whenever there is a single subpath, which is every gradient fill in the corpus so far.

It is NOT the region boundary for a shape with holes: a letter 'o' with a counter, an Annulus, a Sector with an inner arc. The per-loop generalization (Hormann-Floater's MVC for polygons with holes: sum the weights over every loop, with the outer loop and the hole loops carrying opposite traversal) is a DESIGN step, not a parameter — it has to decide what the boundary colour is on a hole's loop when the ramp is defined on the path's arc length as a whole, and whether a hole's stations get the same station count as the outer loop or a share proportional to its arc length.

Do not guess it. Trigger: a corpus case (or a Look Gallery panel) where a gradient-filled shape has a hole. Acceptance: subdivision invariance must survive the generalization (it is the property the whole construction exists for), and the single-loop case must be bit-identical to today's field.

Recorded in GradientField's doc comment as the module's stated limit.

title: G0-8 route decision: the W5 chain is gated on hardware this program does not have
description:
STRUCTURAL BLOCKER, filed 2026-07-24 from a triage observation, not from a code defect.

bv ranks fm-5xm (W9 Scene runtime) the highest-value open bead in the graph — betweenness 100%, unblocks fm-39s/fm-c53/fm-eiw. Its dependency chain is fm-5xm <- fm-hv4 <- fm-3df <- fm-tg6 <- {fm-gw7, fm-jsc} <- fm-ekx. fm-jsc is now closed; every other link is open, and the ROOT of the chain, fm-ekx (G0-8, the accelerator proof spike), requires Apple silicon with Metal via frankentorch. The development machine is linux-x86-64 with no NVIDIA GPU either (nvidia-smi absent), so fm-ekx as written cannot be executed here at all. The entire W5 render-IR lineage and the W9 scene runtime therefore sit behind a spike that no available machine can run.

This needs a decision, not more waiting. The options, for the record:
(a) Execute fm-ekx on an Apple-silicon machine (the plan's intent: §20.1 spike 8, §10.7, §17.5). Needs hardware access.
(b) Execute the CUDA-via-ft half instead, on a Linux box with an NVIDIA GPU, and record the Metal half on the upstream ledger. §2.9/§10.7 already frame CUDA as a ledger spike, so this is a re-ordering of the annex's two backends, not a new claim. Needs a CUDA machine.
(c) Split fm-ekx: land the parts that need no GPU — the written IR-to-GPU mapping report (which IR tables/stages translate cleanly, which need layout changes, fed back into §10.8's design NOW, which is the spike's actual purpose) and the CUDA ledger item with its feasibility notes — and record a dated, public deferral of the executed-frame half under OQ-12's declared CPU fallback (GOVERNANCE §5's leapfrog-postponement policy, whose clause 1 says postponement never weakens core work). Then fm-gw7 unblocks on the mapping report rather than on a Metal frame.

(c) is the only option executable today and is the one the postponement policy is written for; it must be a recorded ruling (ADR or a dated note in the G0 epic), never a silent re-wiring of the dependency graph. The acceptance criteria of the executed half travel unmodified to whichever gate takes it.

Acceptance: the route is chosen and recorded (ADR if it amends a decision or resolves OQ-10/OQ-12's opening, otherwise a dated note in fm-3g6); if (c), fm-ekx is split with the deferred half re-pointed at its gate and fm-gw7's dependency updated to the artifact that actually gates it.

This dev box (sensedemobox, x86-64, 64c, Matrox G200eH3 server VGA) indeed has neither Metal nor CUDA. But the program owner confirmed the fleet and mac-mini-max is reachable from here over SSH right now: Apple M4 Pro, Darwin 25.2.0 arm64, 14c/64GiB, with the SUITE.lock nightly-2026-07-05 pin installed and a live Metal compiler (Apple metal 32023.830). That is §17.6's Apple-silicon exemplar and the machine §20.1 spike 8 was written for, so no split, no deferral, no re-wiring: fm-ekx executes as written and is now unblocked. Per GOVERNANCE §3 this is a dated note on fm-3g6, not an ADR — nothing in the decision log is amended and no OQ is resolved. Options (b) and (c) declined with reasons on the record. Two operational findings carried onto fm-ekx: (1) mac-mini-max has no FrankenSuite checkout at all, so provisioning from SUITE.lock is the spike's step zero, and ft's Metal backend must be proven to build on pin e4c6bdd before kernels are written; (2) the 'trj' alias in this box's ssh config is STALE (HostName localhost -> resolves back to sensedemobox), so the owner's dual-4090 machine is NOT reachable here — the only reachable NVIDIA part is ts2's GTX 1070, fine for a CUDA feasibility probe but not PG-A's RTX-4090-class profile. title: W3: The RecordBuffer — interleaved f32 records, the live-view protocol, and lazy revisioned render mirrors
description:
Implement Marionette's data plane (§8.2, §1.1, D-20). Three layers, one bead, because their contracts interlock:

(1) THE AUTHORITATIVE BUFFER: interleaved f32 records with typed field views, matching the Reference dtypes exactly — [(point f32x3), (rgba f32x4)] for Mobject; the VMobject layout with stroke_rgba/stroke_width/joint_angle/fill_rgba/base_normal/fill_border_width; Surface/DotCloud/Image declaring their own; USER-DECLARED custom dtypes through the schema machinery. This layout is API surface: mobject.data is a zero-copy NumPy structured export (fnp-dtype is a structured-record engine — this is its native representation). Port field-for-field: aligned_data_keys / pointlike_data_keys, data locking as copy-elision, resize-with-interpolation, null-padding family alignment.

(2) THE VIEW PROTOCOL (G0-1-ratified): exported views pin their buffer; resize is copy-on-resize (old views detach with NumPy-natural semantics); mutation through a view marks render state dirty; reallocation under a live view is impossible by construction. While a WRITABLE live view exists, the affected object (or field, where the view is field-scoped) is conservatively invalidated each frame — a live view never silently receives weaker semantics to buy speed. Ranged editing APIs (edit_points(range, ...)-class) exist as the precise-dirty opt-in.

(3) THE RENDER MIRRORS (Rev 4, mandatory): lazy, revisioned struct-of-arrays (or AoSoA sized to the SIMD tier) mirrors of animated fields, materialized at most once per frame — the hot loops (field lerp, transforms, Lumen's IR sync) read mirrors, never the interleaved buffer; synchronization back through the view protocol happens only when a live view or API read demands it.

title: W2: QuadPath — the shared-anchor path model, formalized with exact fixtures first
description:
Implement Chisel's path model (§7.1, §1.2). VMobject paths are joined quadratic Béziers over a SHARED-ANCHOR layout: points = [a0, h0, a1, h1, a2, ...], length odd when nonempty, curve i = points[2i..2i+3], subpath break = a null curve whose anchor equals its handle. This invariant is API SURFACE — curve counts, partial reveals, alignment, and user code indexing points all depend on it — so it is implemented formally, with exact fixtures for empty / one-point / one-curve / closed / multi-subpath paths BEFORE any higher-level geometry lands (the fixture-first ordering is the W2 exit rule).

Also here: consider_points_equal tolerance and VectorizedPoint degeneracies preserved as API behavior; anchor modes (jagged / approx_smooth / true_smooth) and the smoothing solvers — banded solve for open paths, dense for closed (via fsci-linalg); arc primitives under ONE arc-density convention (the Reference has three inconsistent ones; ours is the unified rule, Behavior Note BN-09 — coordinate with the W7 geometry bead which consumes it); subdivision; per-vertex joint angles.

Design notes: object-space construction and the geometry APIs compute in f64 (§6.1); the QuadPath type is the shared vocabulary of Chisel, Marionette's point data, Scribe's glyph outlines, and Lumen's compiled paths — get the API right here and everything downstream composes.

Acceptance: invariant fixtures green (including adversarial: zero-length curves, coincident anchors, single-point subpaths); smoothing-solver tests against known closed forms; the arc-density rule documented with BN-09 drafted.

title: W5: Zero steady-state per-frame allocation in the certified engine (PG-6)
description:
PG-6 requires zero steady-state heap allocations per frame, over bump arenas and pooled buffers (§10.8, §17.2). The certified CPU engine (fm-ig3) does not meet it yet, and the three places are known:

1. FrameJob::new builds a Vec<Draw> per frame, and each Draw owns a Vec<JoinWedge> and an Option<GradientField> (which owns two Vecs). For a text-heavy scene that is thousands of small allocations per frame.
2. render_into collects a Vec<(usize, &mut [u8])> of bands per frame.
3. Each worker allocates its Worker scratch (acc, cov, RowScratch) once per render_into call rather than once per pool.

None of these can change a bit — they are all storage, and the arithmetic is unchanged — so this is purely the §17 'eliminate work' rung and it is safe to do behind the existing goldens (crates/fmn-conformance/goldens/certified_engine.certified.lock will catch any accident).

Shape: a per-frame bump arena owned by the caller, threaded into FrameJob::new, plus a Worker pool keyed on tile width. Wants to land with or after fm-3df, which owns the ExecutionPlan that would size the pools.

The GLYPH-RECYCLING seam is set_submobjects_from_number: when the digit count is unchanged it does sm.become(smt) in place rather than rebuilding, which is what makes a ticking counter not re-typeset every frame — W5IR's interning is the mechanism. Layout is arrange(RIGHT, buff=digit_buff, aligned_edge=DOWN) with digit_buff = digit_buff_per_font_unit * font_size. set_value restores edge_to_fix position and style. Integer is num_decimal_places=0 with get_value rounding to int.

MATRIX FAMILY — Matrix, DecimalMatrix, IntegerMatrix, TexMatrix, MobjectMatrix (matrix.py). Element grid via x_step=(max_width+h_buff)*RIGHT, y_step=(max_height+v_buff)*DOWN, elem.move_to(i*y_step + j*x_step, aligned_corner) — VMobject::moved_to_aligned already exists for this, landed by fm-y69. Brackets come from fmd-math's extensible-delimiter engine: typeset the Reference's own \\left[\\begin{array}{c}...\\end{array}\\right] with the row count, then set_height(rows.height + v_buff) and next_to(rows, LEFT/RIGHT, h_buff). Scope: express the render IR's highest-ROI stage — stroke signed-distance evaluation + AA resolve (the dominant cost of typical 2D scenes, per-pixel independent) — as frankentorch kernels on Metal, running end-to-end into an actual Studio-preview frame on Apple silicon: IR upload through ft shared buffers (unified memory makes the handoff nearly free), kernel dispatch, composite, present. WHAT LANDED. spikes/g0-8-accelerator (non-member, ADR-0003 dev tier, own committed Cargo.lock, 36 tests green on linux-x86-64 AND macos-aarch64): the prototype compiled render IR (§10.8 subset — SegmentTable/PathTable/StyleTable/TileGrid/CSR per-tile command lists, plus the Metal-shaped FlatIr derivation), the CPU reference engine, the MSL kernel, the §16.3 equivalence measurement, and a preview scene built to exercise curvature, the Line primitive hint, joins, round caps, arc-length width tapers, translucent painter-order overlap and a sub-pixel hairline. Report: docs/g0/G0-8-accelerator-ratification.md. Renders: docs/g0/g0-8-renders/.

THE MEASUREMENT (Apple M4 Pro, 960x540, tile 16, 30 paths / 164 segments / 2040 tiles):
  CPU f32 vs CPU f64 (arithmetic floor): max_u8 152, 200/2073600 differing (0.0096%), ssim 0.999949
  Metal vs CPU f64, MathMode::Safe:      max_u8 152, 201/2073600 differing (0.0097%), ssim 0.999949
  Metal vs CPU f64, MathMode::Fast:      max_u8 184, 235/2073600 differing (0.0113%), ssim 0.999790
Read rows 1 and 2 together: under safe math the Metal engine's ENTIRE divergence from the reference is what f32 does to the algorithm — the GPU contributes one differing component in 2,073,600. That is a controlled experiment, not an inference: sdf::distance_to_quadratic_f32 is a literal f32 transcription run on the CPU, so the annex's numerical behaviour is testable in CI on a machine with no GPU.

THE FINDING THAT WAS NOT IN THIS REPO. frankentorch had no route to a GPU for a consumer's own kernel — only sgemm and the fused NN ops behind fixed entry points — so D-22's "ft is the only GPU gateway" and "the annex runs its own kernels" were flatly contradictory, with standing pressure on the D1 closure to admit a second, far larger GPU dependency. Closed upstream as ft-kernel-metal::compute (UPSTREAM_LEDGER row 8): compile caller-supplied MSL, unified-memory buffers, dispatch, readback, all unsafe contained in ft, no new dependency, stubbed off macOS. The spike kept #![forbid(unsafe_code)]. Landed as a local frankentorch commit; push + SUITE.lock pin bump + class=ffi rows are fm-xsz's §2.9 steps 3-5, so the spike consumes it BY PATH and says so in its Cargo.toml.

THREE DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED, all of which W5 would otherwise have inherited:
  F7 Rust's signum(0.0)=1.0 vs MSL's sign(0.0f)=0.0f collapsed the stable-quadratic pairing to a double root at zero on the GPU alone. Both engines now write the predicate longhand; regression test added.
  F8 An absolute 1e-12 degeneracy threshold is a bug only the f64 engine cannot see: at screen scale a near-straight curve's leading cubic coefficient lands ~1e-8 in f32, so the shader entered the cubic branch and divided by noise. Thresholds are now relative to coefficient scale and sized per engine precision. Two robustness changes rode along.
  F9 Metal compiles fast-math BY DEFAULT. Measured: it doubles rms error and adds 17% more differing components for no measurable time saving. The upstream gateway now defaults to MathMode::Safe — a deliberate reversal of the platform default, because half the §16.3 budget was being spent on a compiler flag nobody had chosen.

F10, THE FINDING WITH THE LONGEST REACH, IS NOT ABOUT THE ANNEX. The 200 surviving components sit at two symmetric spots on one curve — a Lissajous's turning points, where the distance function is near-degenerate and the general quadratic solve is ill-conditioned. 0.0096% at ssim 0.99995 is comfortably inside any budget §16.3 will write for a standard-only annex. But fm-4wt's FAST CPU ENGINE is licensed to use mixed precision under §6.1, and this is the quantified warning: f32 in the stroke SDF costs visible error at curvature extrema on a mainstream curve at ordinary widths. Keep the distance solve in f64, or reformulate and re-measure with cpu::Precision::AnnexF32, which exists for exactly that and needs no GPU.

ALSO SURFACED, AND FIXED: the governed-closure checker keyed allowlist rows by NAME while its own schema and its dedup key say (name, version). The G0-5 spike's PyO3 graph pins syn 2; this spike's Metal graph pins syn 3 through foreign-types-macros, and neither can move — so one non-shipped spike's transitive constraint would have vetoed another's. ADR-0008 rules rows are keyed by (name, version), with both halves pinned by tests: an unlisted VERSION still fails, and two listed versions coexist. 16 new class=dev rows plus a path row for ft-kernel-metal.

D-22 stands unamended; every constraint held (standard-only, never certified, PG-A only, backend identity journaled in AnnexReport, ft the only gateway, no wgpu).

FILED: fm-orn, the analytic-fill GPU mapping spike, which the report's §5 names as the one deferred item needing its own spike before W5 commits to a fill layout — fills are per-SCANLINE with an ordered area accumulation, not per-pixel independent, so nothing about the stroke result transfers for free. title: W5/W10: Behavior Note + Appendix C entry for the Reference's x0.95/x1.06 fill round-trip (0.70% overshoot)
description:
G0-2 (fm-k77, finding L3 and the follow-ups section) measured a systematic defect in the Reference's fill compositing that we do NOT inherit, and it should be recorded so the difference is never mistaken for a colour bug in our renderer.

THE DEFECT: quadratic_bezier/fill/frag.glsl:32 scales fill alpha by 0.95 before the signed-alpha winding blend (to bound the -a/(1-a) singularity at a=1), and shader_wrapper.py:489 un-scales the resolved texture by 1.06. The exact inverse of 0.95 is 1.0526315789...; 1.06 x 0.95 = 1.007, a 0.70% OVERSHOOT applied to rgb AND alpha of every fill in every frame the Reference has ever rendered.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE: our analytic fill has no winding-blend scaling at all, so there is nothing to un-scale. Any side-by-side of a filled shape will therefore show our fill ~0.7% darker/less opaque than the Reference's, uniformly. That is us being right, but a reviewer comparing pixels without knowing this will read it as a colour regression.

DELIVERABLE: an Appendix C row (Reference-defect register) and a line in BN-04, both citing shader_wrapper.py:489 and fill/frag.glsl:32. Evidence is in docs/g0/G0-2-look-study-ratification.md section 8.
close_reason:
DONE. Two Appendix C rows and a BN section, all evidence-backed.

C-12 — the 0.70% fill overshoot. quadratic_bezier/fill/frag.glsl:32 scales fill alpha by 0.95 before the signed-alpha winding blend (bounding the -a/(1-a) singularity at a=1) and shader_wrapper.py:489 un-scales the resolved texture by 1.06. The exact inverse of 0.95 is 1.05263..., so the round trip is 1.06 x 0.95 = 1.007: a 0.70% overshoot applied to rgb AND alpha of every filled shape in every frame the Reference has ever rendered. Our analytic fill has no winding-blend scaling, so there is nothing to un-scale — meaning a side-by-side shows our fills uniformly ~0.7% darker and less opaque. Written up as a full section in BN-04 (the colour note, where a compositing difference belongs) with the trace, and cross-referenced from BN-06's fill note so a reviewer measuring a filled panel does not read a systematic 0.7% as a regression in our colour pipeline.

C-13 — the swapped joint constants, added while here because it is the same class of finding and it turned up in fm-oac's work an hour earlier. stroke/geom.glsl:110-122: BEVEL_JOINT (code 2) sets miter_factor=0, giving shift = -tan(θ/2), the POINTED corner; MITER_JOINT (code 3) sets miter_factor=1, giving +cot(θ/2), the blunt one. The names are swapped relative to the geometry the shader produces, corroborated by G0-2's captured apex widths (auto 4 px, bevel 6 px, miter 9 px — miter visibly blunter). There is also no miter_limit constant anywhere. Ruling recorded in the row: our names mean what they draw, with auto's measured de facto limit of sqrt(10) adopted as the real one (ADR-0012, BN-06-strokes.md).

Appendix C had eleven rulings; it now has thirteen. Both rows carry file:line citations and their ruling, matching the register's existing shape.

title: W8: fmn-cache — the content-addressed store
description:
Implement the persistent cache (§14.4): content-addressed on fmn-hash — atomic writes (write-temp + rename, never partial visibility), cross-process locks (two fmn invocations share a cache safely), per-entry checksums verified on read, versioned namespaces (a schema/version bump invalidates cleanly without clearing unrelated namespaces), corruption recovery (a bad entry is evicted and recomputed, never trusted, never fatal), traversal protection (keys never map to paths outside the cache root), defined eviction (LRU-class with pinning for in-use entries), size ceilings (config-visible).

Serves three consumers with one discipline: TYPESET RESULTS (fmd-math + text layout, keyed on string + preamble-pack hash + font hashes + engine version — W6TEX's contract; the dominant win, PG-7's <100µs cached path); FETCHED ASSETS (through the AssetFetcher capability — cached by content hash with the fetch policy recorded); THE REPLAY JOURNAL's storage (§13.4 — journal segments and checkpoint snapshots live under a cache namespace with pinning while a session is live).

Determinism interaction: a cache is an OPTIMIZATION, never an oracle — certified renders must produce identical output with a cold or warm cache (the key includes everything semantic, so a hit is definitionally equivalent; test it), and --clear-cache (the Reference flag, kept) must be safe at any moment.

Acceptance: atomicity tests (kill -9 mid-write leaves a consistent store); cross-process lock test (two writers, no corruption); corruption-injection tests (flipped bytes detected, evicted, recomputed); eviction/ceiling tests with pinning; cold-vs-warm equivalence test on a typeset-heavy scene; traversal fuzz on keys.
close_reason: The content-addressed store is real: crates/fmn-cache/{lib,key,entry,store}.rs over the fs/clock capabilities — no ambient I/O anywhere. Addresses are SHA-256 of canonical key material (KeyBuilder over fmn-hash serial: fixed field order, framed fields, canonicalized floats, domain separation, self-golden address lock) or of content itself (blobs self-certify). Entries ride the checksummed serial envelope recording kind+address, so flipped bytes, truncation, garbage, AND a valid envelope at the wrong path all classify corrupt → evicted, miss, never fatal (every-byte-flip test). Atomic writes via write-temp+rename; cross-process safety by construction for put/get (content-addressed idempotence) plus an advisory per-namespace maintenance lock with wall-clock staleness breaking (fresh→skip, stale/garbage→break; non-blocking, FakeClock-scripted). Versioned namespaces ns/<name>/v<N> with auto-purge of stale versions, unrelated namespaces untouched. LRU-class eviction on a logical access sequence (never wall time) with shared PinSets, config-visible ceilings, Manual policy for the journal ns; advisory index is merge-flushed and disk-truth-reconciled (lost/corrupt index degrades LRU, never correctness). Traversal protection: validated names + digest-hex-only paths, adversarial+LCG fuzz asserts the shape. Cold-vs-warm equivalence + read-only-cache tests pin the never-fatal contract; get_or_compute swallows cache trouble, surfaces only compute errors. clear() (--clear-cache) safe at any moment, format-stamped store with precise FormatUnsupported refusal. FileSystem capability grew create_new (atomic-content via hard-link)/remove_file/remove_dir_all; torture tests (2 store openings, 7 threads, real StdFs) caught+fixed a genuine pre-existing write_atomic temp-name collision (pid-only unique → pid+seq). 58 tests green (14 unit + 35 deterministic acceptance + 2 host torture ×5 stable + doctest + 6 platform), full gate green, ubs criticals all false-positive (test panics, advisory-token pattern matches). Scene-level cold/warm equivalence on a typeset-heavy scene lands with fm-7dw (consumer). Fuzz-harness follow-up filed as fm-tdp (rides fm-ntp infra).

title: W5: Adaptive coverage anti-aliasing — classify tiles, supersample only complex edges, fuse the resolve
description:
Implement Rev 4's AA scheme (§10.4, D-21). Frames render at native output resolution; tiles are CLASSIFIED (via W5IR/W5BIN metadata) as empty, fully-covered, simple-edge, or complex-edge: interiors fill as vectorized spans; analytic coverage is evaluated only near edges; 2x/4x edge supersampling applies ONLY to complex-edge cells (thin overlapping strokes, dense self-intersections, high-frequency 3D silhouettes); and the resolve is FUSED into the coverage pass so the supersampled buffer never makes a second trip through memory. Full-frame SSAA spent most of its work on pixels that were empty or fully covered; the adaptive scheme spends it where the picture is — this matters most on bandwidth-limited parts (§17.6: Apple silicon's wall is bandwidth, not FLOPs).

Contract discipline: in `standard`, the classification thresholds are a QUALITY knob (§4) — but the escalation defaults are FIXED in G0-2's look study so default output reads as "the same feel, cleaner." In `certified`, the canonical analytic path runs everywhere and classification is a scheduling choice that CANNOT change bits (§10.5) — assert this by construction: the certified engine's per-pixel result must be independent of tile class. A forced-SSAA knob remains for A/B comparison and debugging.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FROM fm-ig3 (2026-07-26) — the certified engine is landed and it deliberately does NOT classify.

§10.4 is explicit that 'certified runs the canonical analytic path everywhere — classification there is a scheduling choice that cannot change bits'. The engine does exactly that: every partial tile evaluates analytic coverage, and the only classification it honours is bin.rs's existing CLASS_INTERIOR, which is a correctness mechanism (exactly 1.0, the precondition for byte-exact occlusion pruning) rather than an AA policy.

So your adaptive scheme is additive and standard-mode, and the engine gives you two footholds:

1. FrameJob::fill_pass already picks one of three coverage sources in a documented order — classified interior, hinted kernel, general machinery. A complex-edge escalation is a fourth arm at the same site.
2. the_engine_matches_a_brute_force_reference is the test that will hold you honest: it renders the same frame with no binning, no interior class and no slab rejection and compares bytes. Anything you add that claims to be an optimization can be measured against it directly; anything that changes the picture has to be a declared standard-mode divergence with its own visual-equivalence budget (§16.3), not a quiet default.

Also worth knowing: the AA band's reach is now in the binner. bin::screen_aabb grows a stroked instance's AABB by half its widest width plus anti_alias_width (§10.3's per-draw width expansion, which was specified and never implemented — a stroke used to lose w/2 + aa pixels wherever its hull ended on a tile boundary). If your escalation widens the region a command can touch, it has to widen that expansion too.

comments.text:
ADDENDUM from fm-ig3's review (2026-07-27) — one number that bears on your escalation thresholds.

The cap/join corpus was drawing at 3.6 px and ALL FOUR joint settings rendered inside the ~1.5 px AA band — the golden was locking a picture no joint setting could move. That is the same regime your complex-edge classifier has to reason about: below roughly two AA bands of stroke width, the joint geometry is entirely inside the antialiasing and the distinctions §10.3 makes are sub-pixel.

Two consequences: (a) a corpus or gallery panel meant to show join behaviour needs width above that threshold or it shows nothing — the fixture now draws at 8.4 px; (b) if your escalation is keyed on edge complexity, thin overlapping strokes at that width are exactly where the analytic path is already delivering the right answer and supersampling would buy nothing. §10.4 names 'thin overlapping strokes' as an escalation trigger; the measurement suggests the trigger wants a width term, not just a count.

title: W5: The compiled render IR — retained tables, independent revisions, primitive hints, glyph instancing
description:
Implement Lumen's retained core (§10.8, D-20). Between Marionette's authoritative state and the execution engines sits a compiled, backend-neutral render IR: PathTable, SegmentTable, StyleTable, InstanceTable, ImageTable, and per-tile command lists — synchronized LAZILY from the RecordBuffer under §8.2's mirror rule, with backend-specific layouts derived from it (SoA/AoSoA sized to SIMD lanes on CPU; device arrays for the annex).

INDEPENDENT REVISIONS per renderable resource — topology, geometry, transform, style, visibility/order, image, camera-projection — and the distinctions pay directly: a color change does not regenerate curve coefficients; a translation does not recompute an object-space arc-length table; a camera move does not re-decode font outlines. Each COMPILED PATH retains: y-monotone quadratic splits (at vertical-tangent parameters), screen-independent coefficients, object- and screen-space bounds, the arc-length LUT (shared artifact with W2ARC), conservative stroke slabs, fill winding metadata, its primitive hint, previous tile coverage, and old + new dirty bounds.

PRIMITIVE HINTS route semantic shapes off the general quadratic solver: line/polyline → capsule-distance kernel; circle/arc → direct arc kernel; rectangle/rounded-rect → specialized coverage; dot → radial kernel; image → sampler kernel; nearly-linear quadratic → line fast path under an explicit screen-space error bound; glyph → cached path instance. Mutation through set_points or a writable live view invalidates the hint back to the general path — correctness never depends on a hint.

GLYPH/SHAPE INTERNING: an outline compiles once (content-addressed with the §11.3 span machinery and fmn-cache) and each occurrence is an INSTANCE (transform, color, clip, order) — for text-heavy mathematical scenes this deletes the bulk of geometry duplication and binning work; the same mechanism serves dots, arrow tips, repeated graph nodes, copied decorations.

G0-8's mapping report feeds this design (device-layout implications discovered there land here, not at W9-time).

Acceptance: revision-independence tests (each mutation class touches exactly its revision); lazy-sync tests (untouched resources never recompile); hint-invalidation tests; instancing dedup test (N copies of a glyph ⇒ 1 compiled path + N instances); IR golden snapshots for fixture scenes.
design:
INHERITED FROM G0-8b (fm-orn), docs/g0/G0-8b-analytic-fill-ratification.md — four layout verdicts, all cheap now and expensive to retrofit:

F11 THE FILL NEEDS ITS OWN GEOMETRY TABLE. Axis-monotone pieces (split at BOTH dy/dt=0 and dx/dt=0 — the plan named only one; §10.2 is trued up) are a DERIVED table keyed by the geometry revision, NOT a reshaped SegmentTable. Strokes read whole segments and their normalized arc-length spans (s0,s1); splitting invalidates those spans and gives the nearest-point search more work for the same answer. Bound: one segment yields at most 3 pieces, so a device allocator can size at 3*segments with no second pass. Device form: flat f32 at stride 6 (no arc-length span — §10.2 never asks where along the path a pixel is).

F12 THE STYLETABLE IS STAGE-SPECIFIC. Fills read rgba/rgba_end/gradient_axis (stride 12); strokes read rgba/width_start/width_end/aa_width (stride 8). Keep ONE interned host style table (dedup is semantics, §8.5 BatchKey bitwise) and derive a per-stage device row. Shared dedup index, unshared layout — a union row wastes a third of every entry or reintroduces the mixed-type access F1 forbids.

F13 THE COMMAND LIST NEEDS A FLAG WORD, AND OCCLUSION PRUNING DOES NOT WORK WITHOUT IT. Per-tile runs should carry (path_index, flags), not path_index — 4 bytes per command. §10.4's interior/edge class is a property of a (path, tile) PAIR, so flags are parallel to draws, not to tiles. The interior class must SHORT-CIRCUIT the accumulation and write exactly 1: an accumulated interior coverage is 1-epsilon, so an opaque cover lets the layer beneath show through by an ulp, and dropping the hidden command then changes the frame. Measured: 21.8% of commands interior, 16.5% pruned, frames byte-identical.

F14 THE TILE CARRY IS FREE AND CHANGES NO BINNING. Each row needs the winding deposited left of the tile, in closed form (one root solve per piece), so the fill iterates EVERY piece of a path, not only those meeting the tile. Slab-keyed binning is still sufficient: a path enclosing any pixel of a tile has hull bounds containing it. No shadow binning, no clip geometry.

Executable reference: spikes/g0-8-accelerator/src/analytic_fill.rs (the algorithm, generic over f32/f64) and shaders/analytic_fill.metal (both dispatch shapes).
close_reason:
All five acceptance criteria met, in crates/fmn-render (48 tests): revision-independence (each mutation class touches exactly its axes), lazy-sync (an unchanged renderable's points are never read — SyncStats counts the work NOT done), hint-invalidation (consumed from Marionette's revision comparison, all four write channels tested), instancing dedup (8 copies of an outline => 1 compiled path, 2 segments, 8 instances), and an IR golden snapshot bit-locked through fmn-hash's canonical envelope.

LANDED: revision.rs (the seven axes, Dependency), hint.rs (kernel routing + §10.8's nearly-linear fast path under a screen-space bound), table.rs (object-space segments, styles interned by bits matching BatchKey, shapes interned by content digest with position excluded, instances), plan.rs (the retained plan and its lazy sync), snapshot.rs (canonical encoding + the golden).

CARRIED FORWARD, each recorded on its owner: per-tile command lists -> fm-tg6; previous tile coverage + old/new dirty bounds -> fm-0l8; the backend-derived flat layouts -> the engines that derive them (F1 says one derivation per backend; fm-xsz carries the Metal one); ImageTable + the image axis producer -> fm-nve (blocked on an image mobject existing); the transform revision channel -> fm-7if.

TWO BUGS THE TESTS CAUGHT, both invisible: the joint type folded into the style key via f64::to_bits() as u32, which takes the low 32 bits — all zero for small integers — so all four joint types interned as one style; and the test that should have caught it used 2.0 + f32::EPSILON as a one-ulp value, which rounds straight back at 2.0.

title: W4: Composition & timeline algebra — AnimationGroup/Succession/LaggedStart + the declarative Timeline
description:
Implement animation composition (§9.4): AnimationGroup / Succession / LaggedStart / LaggedStartMap over (start, end) interval math — group run_time derivation, lag_ratio spreading across members, nested composition (groups of groups with independent rate_funcs), squish_rate_func and time_span flowing through the single normalized-alpha pipeline (W4CONTRACT owns the pipeline; this bead exercises its composition surface hard). Interval semantics are the Reference's: members map their (start,end) sub-intervals onto parent alpha; a member's rate_func applies inside its window.

THE DECLARATIVE TIMELINE: keyframes, labels, seek — compiling to the SAME primitives (an authored Timeline is sugar over composed animations on the rational clock, never a second engine). This is the substrate for Studio scrubbing (§13.5) and the WASM tier-2 serialized-timeline player (§10.7): a Timeline must serialize (fmn-hash canonical format) with enough fidelity that the player replays it without scene code. Seek semantics: seeking to time t reconstructs state deterministically — for pure segments via snapshot + interpolate-at-alpha; across stateful segments via the nearest checkpoint + replay (coordinate with §13.4's journal; the Timeline records segment boundaries).

Acceptance: interval-math fixtures vs the Reference (nested groups, lag interactions, unequal member run_times); normalized-alpha composition tests shared with W4CONTRACT; Timeline round-trip (author → serialize → load → replay ⇒ identical frame states); seek determinism tests (seek(t) ≡ play-through-to(t) for pure content).

AnimationGroup/Succession/LaggedStart/LaggedStartMap over one interval model (build_timings = the Reference's build_animations_with_timings); two Reference defects fixed as C-10 (group rate_func/time_span inert; ours runs the one normalized-alpha pipeline, rate curve defaults to linear so the ordinary group is unchanged) and C-11 (Succession's equal-share alpha + dropped members; ours honors member run_times and walks). BN-11 written, Appendix C trued up in the same commit. Declarative Timeline: compile() derives the schedule with no stage, labels resolve to frames, render() drives the ordinary primitives, seek() = nearest checkpoint + replay + (pure) reconstruct_pure_frame; TimelinePlan serializes canonically as FMNA/5 with content addressing. Acceptance met: interval fixtures vs the Reference (1008 alpha cases, 48 timing cases, 168 Succession cases incl. 31 divergent), nested groups with independent rate_funcs, seek(t) == play-through-to(t) at f32::to_bits identity for pure AND stateful content, plan round-trip + corrupt-bytes refusal. comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
AUDIT ADDENDUM — testing & logging doctrine (binding on every bead in this epic):

Every task bead in this epic lands with its tests as PART OF ITS SCOPE — a bead without its tests is not done:
1. COMPREHENSIVE UNIT TESTS, colocated in-crate, covering the bead's stated acceptance criteria INCLUDING negative and edge cases (degenerate inputs, resource-budget violations, version-mismatch refusals, error-path assertions — not just happy paths).
2. E2E REGISTRATION: any bead landing user-visible behavior (a mobject, an animation, a CLI flag, an output format, a Studio surface) registers at least one scripted end-to-end scenario with the Gauntlet e2e harness (fm-fjq) — driven through the real surfaces (CLI / Rust API / fmn-python / Studio HTTP), asserting outputs (bit-locked hashes on certified paths; structural assertions elsewhere), exit codes, and emitted-file inventory.
3. DETAILED STRUCTURED LOGGING: behavior flows through the owned tracing layer (§17.1/§18 — scene→play→frame→phase→tile spans, stage timings, counters, decision points: engine selection, cache hits, purity classifications, barriers). Where correct behavior is invisible in the output ("the preflight ran before frame 0", "wait() frames hit the tile cache"), the e2e scenario ASSERTS ON THE LOGS. On failure, the harness auto-bundles a deterministic repro (scene + input closure + logs + journal tail).
4. GATES BEFORE CLOSE: scripts/check.sh green (fmt, check, clippy -D warnings, test) + ubs clean on changed files, per AGENTS.md. Determinism-relevant beads additionally run their {1,4,16}-thread sweep before close.

title: W8: The ordered asynchronous emitter — sequence-numbered frames, preallocated rings, never a stall
description:
Implement Reel's orchestration core (§14.1, D-19): sequence-numbered frames from the pipeline (§17.4) and from frame-parallel pure segments (§9.5) publish IN FRAME-INDEX ORDER through a preallocated ring of frame slots — Lumen never stalls on a sink, and no sink ever observes an out-of-order or torn frame.

Mechanics: a bounded ring sized by the RAM-derived, config-visible in-flight budget (PG-6: each in-flight 4K RGBA frame ≈ 33MB — the budget is real memory); workers deposit completed frames by index; the emitter drains the contiguous prefix to sinks (file writers, the ffmpeg pipe, the Studio stream, the y4m/PNG-sequence writers); backpressure propagates to the pipeline when the ring fills (bounded, deadlock-free: the ring never blocks a frame that the drain is waiting on — slot reservation happens at frame dispatch); the hot path never allocates, resizes, or synchronously flushes a frame-sized buffer (§14.3's rule).

Ordering is a determinism obligation, not a UX nicety (§10.5 e): frame-index-ordered emission is one of the parallelism contract's six clauses — the frame-parallel equivalence tests (W4PURITY, PG-5) depend on this component being airtight. Multi-sink: a render may feed video + PNG sequence + preview simultaneously; each sink observes the same ordered stream; a slow sink applies backpressure rather than dropping (drops are an explicit per-sink policy, only for preview-class sinks).

Acceptance: out-of-order deposit tests (adversarial completion orders ⇒ in-order emission, always); backpressure test (slow sink throttles pipeline without deadlock); torn-frame impossibility test (a slot is never visible to sinks mid-write — API review + concurrency test under the thread sweep); multi-sink consistency test; ring-budget accounting test vs the configured in-flight limit.
close_reason: Bounded preallocated ordered emitter, multi-sink backpressure/drop policy, direct Lumen integration, concurrency acceptance suite, and full green workspace gate landed.

title: W5: The certified CPU engine — canonical raster arithmetic, the definition of the bits
description:
Implement the certified execution engine (§10.5, §6.1, §6.6, D-18; consumes G0-6's OQ-1 decision): the engine whose output IS the definition of correct bits for self-goldens, PG-5, and --reproducible.

Arithmetic: per G0-6's ruling — either floating-point with fmn-dmath transcendentals, fixed-order reductions, FMA off; or canonical fixed-point screen coordinates + integer coverage accumulation at defined precision with explicit rounding. Either way: NO fast-math, NO FMA on certified paths, reductions in fixed order and LANE-COUNT-INDEPENDENT (no horizontal sums whose association varies with vector width — the trap that silently breaks bit identity across SIMD build tiers); within the certified engine THE SCALAR PATH IS THE DEFINITION and every SIMD tier must match it bit-for-bit; degenerate/badly-conditioned cases route to the precision-exception path in every mode.

The parallelism contract, enforced here structurally (§10.5 a–f): frame bits are a pure function of (begin snapshot, alpha, frame-indexed RNG, input closure); write-disjoint tiles, fixed composite order; frame-index-ordered emission; engine/backend identity journaled into the input closure (§16.7).

Verification hooks: PG-5's thread-count sweep ({1,4,16} per commit, {32,96}+ weekly) runs THIS engine's output through the self-golden rig; the certified matrix cross-platform check (W1WCI's runners) compares frame hashes across linux-x86-64/linux-aarch64/macos-aarch64. The engine-equivalence suite (W10) holds every OTHER engine to this one's reference frames.

Acceptance: bit-identity at {1,4,16} threads on the primitive corpus; cross-platform bit-identity on the certified matrix for the G0-6 frame plus a growing corpus; scalar-vs-SIMD-tier bit-identity harness in place (tiers land in W5FAST but the harness is certified-side); the input-closure journaling path tested.
close_reason:
DONE. The certified CPU engine is landed, the certified matrix is measured on its own corpus, and ADR-0010's load-bearing property is now enforced rather than assumed.

WHAT LANDED
- crates/fmn-render/src/engine.rs — FrameJob: a serial front-end deriving per-instance draw state once, and a parallel back-end that slices the frame into bands with chunks_mut so §10.5(b)'s write-disjointness is enforced by the borrow checker. A multi-threaded rasterizer under #![forbid(unsafe_code)] with no escape hatch anywhere. Raw frame is linear-light Rgba16F; canonical PNG is one table lookup away.
- EngineIdentity + journal() — §10.5(f) and C7/C10, canonically serialized. EngineKind::certifiable is where 'certified requires the certified CPU engine' stops being prose.
- tests/certified_arithmetic.rs — ADR-0010's two mechanically checkable properties as permanent gates, one-line exemption list, with a self-test because a scanner that finds nothing is indistinguishable from one that is broken.
- tests/certified_engine.rs — the raw-frame corpus under Scope::Certified, PG-5's {1,4,16} sweep, and the tier harness.
- ADR-0013 (accumulation order) and ADR-0014 (fmn-dmath at the DAG root), with the plan trued up in the same commits — including ADR-0010's own true-up, which its commit never made.

ACCEPTANCE, ITEM BY ITEM
1. Bit-identity at {1,4,16} threads on the corpus — DONE, per commit, and additionally measured natively on a 14-core M4 Pro.
2. Cross-platform bit-identity on the certified matrix — DONE AND MEASURED, not merely claimed by scope. All three legs pass one Scope::Certified lock: linux-x86-64 (glibc, native), linux-aarch64 (musl, qemu-user, cross-compiled), macos-aarch64 (Darwin, native, M4 Pro). The corpus is stronger evidence than G0-6's single frame: gradient fills, a winding hole, all four joint settings including two miter-limit escapes, round caps at three widths, an arc-length taper, both hinted fill routes, an inner border, a backstroke, a sub-AA hairline. 631 further tests green on macOS.
3. Scalar-vs-tier harness in place — DONE. Tier::ALL has one entry today and the test says so plainly rather than implying coverage it lacks; fm-4wt's first tier becomes real coverage by adding a variant and dispatching on identity.tier.
4. Input-closure journaling path tested — DONE.

ADR-0010'S FOUR PROPERTIES: 1 and 2 are permanent CI gates; 3 is ADR-0013's ruling; 4 is structural (nothing weaker than + - * / sqrt).

THE TWO ITEMS HANDED HERE BY fm-oac AND fm-5oi: discharged. caps_and_joins.v1 and fills.v1 are rasterized, looked at, and bit-locked. The accumulation-order open question is ADR-0013.

THREE DEFECTS FOUND, ALL BY THE BRUTE-FORCE REFERENCE TEST OR THE GUARD
- bin::screen_aabb applied no per-draw width expansion, so every stroke was binned to its centreline hull and lost w/2 + aa pixels wherever its outline ended on a tile boundary. §10.3 specified the expansion; nothing implemented it, and nothing could notice until a rasterizer existed.
- The same function returned an un-normalized AABB, so a negative ScreenMap::scale — the natural spelling of a y-flip — binned the entire scene out of existence, silently.
- BN-04's 'decode to linear light at the render boundary' had no implementation. The record buffer holds sRGB, Style documents linear, and nothing between them decoded. Now done once per interned style row through fmn_frame::transfer::srgb_decode.

AND ONE FINDING ABOUT THE EVIDENCE ITSELF: the funnel guard found sixteen live libm call sites, two of them inside the very frame G0-6 hashed (rate::wiggle's sin and rate::exponential_decay's exp, which compute alpha and therefore move points, not last bits). G0-6's digests stand — but its argument was stronger than the code supported. Fifteen of the sixteen were unreachable from the funnel because fmn-core, fmn-mobject and fmn-library had no edge to fmn-dmath, and fmn-core could not have one without a cycle. That edge turned out to be vestigial (fmn-dmath uses nothing from fmn-core), so ADR-0014 inverts it.

ALSO: self_goldens.rs's two artifacts were measured identical on all three legs and graduated from per-platform locks to one certified lock, which is what that file said should happen once G0-6 landed. self_goldens.linux-x86_64.lock is superseded and no longer read — left in place, not removed.

FILED: fm-e9h (zero steady-state per-frame allocation, PG-6 — the Vec<Draw>, the band list, the per-worker scratch; all storage, none able to move a bit) and fm-qtd (canonical PNG panels from the corpus for Look Gallery review).

HANDOFFS POSTED: fm-4wt, fm-uql, fm-0gy, fm-3df, fm-gmr.

GATES: scripts/check.sh green — 1131 tests, fmt, clippy -D warnings, crate-DAG (22 crates, all edges downward), ubs 0 critical.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
G0-6 (fm-zn9) resolved OQ-1 on 2026-07-25 — ADR-0010. This unblocks you, and it also hands you four acceptance criteria.

THE DECISION: floating-point suffices for the certified path. §10.5's canonical fixed-point raster boundary is RETIRED, NOT DEFERRED — it should not reappear in a W5 review as an unresolved option, and no precision or rounding constants enter the input closure.

THE EVIDENCE: one frame exercising gradient fills, a winding hole, strokes with joins and arc-length tapers, per-vertex atan2 joint angles that reach pixels, the Reference's true_dot glow with its pow falloff, rate functions driving the geometry, and alpha compositing — hashed byte-identically on linux-x86_64 (glibc, native), linux-aarch64 (musl, qemu-user) and macos-aarch64 (Darwin, M4 Pro). All 18 digests: the f64 frame, the f32 frame, and each of 16 fmn-dmath functions. The three legs vary ISA, libc and OS independently, so agreement is not one comparison repeated. Raw data docs/g0/g0-6-hashes/; methodology docs/g0/G0-6-determinism-ratification.md.

THE RESULT IS ONLY AS DURABLE AS FOUR PROPERTIES, WHICH ARE NOW YOUR ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
  1. fmn-dmath owns EVERY transcendental on the certified path. This is the load-bearing one — three platforms with three different libms agreed precisely because the libm is not in the loop.
  2. No FMA contraction (§10.5d). Verified in aarch64 object code; guarded in source by determinism::fma_guard.
  3. Fixed-order reductions (§10.5c). Trivially true today because the prototype is scalar; it stops being trivial the moment the SIMD tiers land (that risk is noted on fm-4wt).
  4. IEEE-754 basic operations only. Nothing weaker on the certified path.

THE CERTIFIED MATRIX IS FROZEN into docs/INPUT_CLOSURE.md §5: linux-x86-64, linux-aarch64, macos-aarch64 certified; windows-x86-64 functional-CI only, its bit-certification still OQ-6. Adding a platform is an ADR, not a CI-config change.

ONE CAVEAT TO CARRY, NOT TO FORGET: the linux-aarch64 leg ran under qemu-user, because no aarch64 Linux hardware is reachable. QEMU's softfloat is IEEE-754 correct for the basic ops and nothing certified uses anything weaker, so it is valid evidence about the ARITHMETIC — but not about an aarch64 Linux MACHINE. fm-sol replaces it with real hardware if any becomes available.

SELF-GOLDEN ALREADY IN PLACE: the frame's f64 and f32 digests are bit-locked as single cross-platform constants in the spike's tests, so the property fails on whichever machine breaks it rather than waiting for someone to re-run the sweep. That is the Scope::Certified shape docs/INPUT_CLOSURE.md §6 now points at.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FROM fm-5oi (2026-07-26) — the analytic fill is landed and green (crates/fmn-render/src/fill.rs), so this bead's fill half is unblocked. Three things it hands you that bear on 'the definition of the bits':

1. The core is generic over a Real trait with f64 and f32 instantiations from ONE expression tree, so the certified/fast split is a type parameter rather than two transcriptions. The f32 instantiation is already exercised as 'the annex's arithmetic without the annex's hardware' (measured divergence < 1e-5 of coverage on a 15px-radius disc).
2. RowScratch::interior_row returns bit-exactly 1.0, written as a fill of the literal rather than a clamp of an accumulation. That is the precondition that makes occlusion pruning byte-identical (G0-8b F13) — do not replace it with a clamp.
3. Everything transcendental in the fill routes through fmn-dmath: the disc kernel's antiderivative uses fmn_dmath::atan2 (NOT asin — asin has infinite derivative at +/-1 and cost 1.4e-7 of area at r=6, and pixels sit a hair under r at every disc's extremes), and fmn_geom::distance uses the scalar funnel for cbrt/acos/cos. sqrt is used directly, since IEEE 754 requires it correctly rounded.

Open question this bead owns and the fill did not resolve: whether the certified path fixes the accumulation ORDER across pieces. fill_row accumulates pieces in table order and then prefix-sums the row, which is deterministic for a given plan — but the plan's piece order is a property of the sync, so PG-5's thread-count sweep will want that pinned explicitly rather than inherited.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
ADDENDUM from fm-oac (2026-07-26) — strokes are landed too (crates/fmn-render/src/stroke.rs), so both §10.2 and §10.3 are now waiting on this bead. Three things bear on it:

1. TWO ACCEPTANCE ITEMS FROM fm-oac LAND HERE, not there. §10.3's acceptance asks for 'cap/join golden fixtures (every combination, including miter-limit escapes to bevel)'. The GEOMETRY of every combination is tested in stroke.rs — round cap circularity over twelve directions, the join arc with no notch and no gap, bevel trimming, miter extending, the miter-limit escape on a reversal — but a bit-locked GOLDEN is a rasterized frame, and there is no engine to rasterize one. The same is true of the fill. Wire both corpora into fmn-conformance's golden rig when the engine exists; that is this bead's, and fm-oac was closed saying so rather than sitting open on it.

2. THE STRUCTURE IS ANNEX-SHAPED ALREADY. stroke_coverage is per-pixel independent with no accumulator and no scan — the one-thread-per-pixel shape G0-8 proved on Metal — and the fill offers the same shape via coverage_at_cell alongside its scanline form. §10.3 asked for 'scalar-complete first; the structure must not preclude lanes', and nothing here does: the hot loop is a min over segments of one nearest-point solve.

3. THE ARITHMETIC IS ALREADY FUNNELLED. Everything transcendental goes through fmn-dmath: the fill's disc kernel via atan2, fmn_geom::distance via the scalar funnel for cbrt/acos/cos. sqrt is used directly (IEEE 754 requires it correctly rounded). What this bead still owns is the ORDER: the fill accumulates pieces in table order then prefix-sums the row, and the stroke takes a min over segments in table order. Both are deterministic for a given plan, but the plan's order is a property of the sync — PG-5's sweeps will want that pinned explicitly rather than inherited.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FRESH-EYES REVIEW (2026-07-27) — four defects found in the work closed under this bead, all fixed, plus two corpus weaknesses. Recorded here because the bead is closed and these are its consequences.

1. THE DRAW LIST WAS COMPACTED WHILE BINNING INDEXES BY INSTANCE. FrameJob skipped instances with no visible pass; Binning's command lists hold instance indices. From the first skipped instance onward, every command paired with the wrong shape and style — a scene whose first object is invisible drew its second object's geometry in its third object's colour and dropped the last. 1075 of 12544 pixels. I had written the comment explaining that the two indices diverge and then indexed by the wrong one.

2. compile_shape DETECTED SUBPATH BREAKS BY ZERO LENGTH. fmn-geom's convention (QuadPath::subpath_end_indices, and the Reference's) is a handle sitting on the previous anchor. The two coincide only when a subpath begins where the last ended, so an annulus with distinct radii and EVERY GLYPH COUNTER compiled as one subpath — §10.2's named failure, 'fill as one ring with a chord through it' — and the break survived as a drawn segment, so a stroked annulus grew a radial spoke. This one predates fm-ig3 (fm-gw7's compile_shape) and would have hit W6 hard the moment text landed.

3. THE FUNNEL GUARD WAS BLIND AFTER LINE 6 OF bezier.rs. It stopped at the first #[cfg(test)]; that file's line 6 is a #[cfg(test)] use, hiding 173 lines of production geometry while reporting clean. Now skips only the item the attribute introduces (47k lines read, floor raised 20k->40k), and its self-test covers this plus a // inside a string literal.

4. A HINTED FILL KERNEL WOULD HAVE FILLED A MULTI-SUBPATH SHAPE'S HOLE. Prophylactic — no constructor tags such a shape today — but §10.8 says correctness never depends on a hint.

Plus: encode_frame guessed 4 bytes/px for non-Rgba16F (a planar buffer would have hashed luma and dropped chroma); the journal wrote PixelFormat as a discriminant, so reordering fmn-frame's enum would have moved every manifest digest ever issued; render_into did not check the binning was built for its viewport.

TWO CORPUS WEAKNESSES, WHICH MATTER MORE THAN THEY LOOK:
- The cap/join grid drew at 3.6 px, where all four joint settings sit inside the AA band — the golden was locking a picture no joint could move. Widened to 8.4 px, and the test now proves the joints reach pixels and asserts ADR-0012 at frame level (Auto == NoJoint byte-for-byte; Bevel and Miter each differ).
- At 60 px/unit every Circle was inside HINT_BUDGET_PX, so §10.2's general machinery was exercised by the annuli alone. Added a self-intersecting pentagram: its centre has winding 2, so it fills under nonzero and would be a hole under even-odd — a discriminator for the rule, not just a workout for the evaluator.

ALSO CORRECTED: interning_order_does_not_move_a_pixel proved nothing. RenderPlan::sync interns in painter order, so on a FRESH plan the two orders cannot diverge — they diverge only on a RETAINED plan when an object is inserted behind ones already compiled, which is the normal path. Replaced with a retained-vs-fresh comparison that asserts the divergence as a precondition. ADR-0013's Context and Consequences are trued up.

All three certified legs re-verified against the final tree (14 certified tests each, one shared lock). Gates green: 1135 tests, fmt, clippy -D warnings, crate-DAG, ubs 0 real criticals.

The superseded self_goldens.linux-x86_64.lock was removed with the owner's written authorization.

title: W10: The performance rig — PG-1..PG-8 + PG-A on pinned profiles, with scaling annex
description:
Implement §17.2's gate machinery: dedicated PINNED bare-metal profiles (8-core x86-64 Linux; Apple-silicon macOS), multiple repetitions, median + robust dispersion, ALERT vs BLOCKING thresholds, versioned baselines.

THE GATES: PG-1 end-to-end (OpeningManimExample-class 1080p vs the Python Reference under the PINNED benchmark definition from W1PROF — ≤0.5x at G2, ≤0.35x at G4); PG-2 rasterizer (≥300 Mpx/s fill-equivalent, ≥120 Mpx/s stroke at 8 threads on canonical workloads with stated path/segment/overdraw parameters); PG-3 throughput (≥60fps 1080p preview median primitive scene; ≥30fps 4K export typical 2D); PG-4 latency (cold CLI → first frame <150ms; edit-to-frame <1s); PG-5 determinism (bit-identical frames {1,4,16} per commit — frame-parallel and pipelined schedules INCLUDED — {32,96}+ weekly, certified matrix under --reproducible); PG-6 memory (≤1.5GB peak on the 4K 3D gallery under the RAM-derived in-flight budget; zero leaks over 1h soak; ZERO steady-state per-frame heap allocations on the primitive corpus); PG-7 typesetting (<3ms cold / <100µs cached median formula; 10k-glyph layout <20ms); PG-8 binding tax by class (from W10TAX's budgets).

SCALING PROFILES (published, then ratcheted): parallel efficiency at {1,8,32,96} threads for raster-bound and frame-parallel workloads, per release, alert-first graduating to blocking after two releases of baseline. PG-A: annex engines on their own pinned profiles (Apple Max-class; RTX-4090-class), gating ANNEX changes only — the CPU engine stands alone so acceleration can never mask a core regression (R21).

Rig telemetry beyond fps (§17.2): bytes up/back per frame, reuse and tile-cache hit rates, dirty-tile percentage, allocations per frame, team utilization, cross-NUMA steals, GPU occupancy, encode queue depth; scene classes static/locally-dirty/full-screen/dense-stroke/text-heavy/high-overdraw/3D; latency probes + 10-minute thermal runs; outputs raw/PNG/software-video/hardware-video.

Acceptance: every gate has a bench binary, committed baseline, variance budget, and flamegraph-on-regression artifact; blocking wired per gate's schedule (G2/G4 thresholds staged); the scaling annex publishes per release; a demonstrated regression drill (inject slowdown → gate blocks).
