This keeps G2's PG enforcement off the fmn-python critical path, matching §20.3's gate criteria.

title: W10: The Parity Ledger + Behavior Notes — symbol-granular, semantics-tiered, user-facing
description:
Implement the two user-facing truth registers:

THE PARITY LEDGER (§16.1): rows are SYMBOLS AND BEHAVIORS — module · symbol · kind (class/method/property/function/constant/CLI flag/config key) · wildcard-exported? · signature/defaults · semantic status: SAME | IMPROVED (Behavior-Note link) | TIERED (out-of-tier ledger link, §16.6) | EXCLUDED (e.g. custom GLSL) · tests · notes. Covers the utility-function surface (the wildcard-import namespace with no authoritative __all__ — §1.6), the CLI, and config keys. Generated FROM the W10SCHEMA plus per-symbol status annotations; regenerates the coverage badge; CI FAILS ON REGRESSION (a symbol dropping status is a build break with a required written amendment).

THE BEHAVIOR NOTES (§16.8, D-05): the user-facing register of deliberate differences from classic manim — one evidence-backed entry each, written as MIGRATION GUIDANCE, not apologia. Seed set: BN-01 single RNG; BN-02 rational clock; BN-03 true arc length; BN-04 color (linear-light + familiar gradients); BN-05 native typesetting metrics; BN-06 renderer (analytic coverage, round caps, arclength width); BN-07 Reference bugs fixed (Appendix C rulings C-1..C-9); BN-08 de-TeX'd classes; BN-09 one arc-density rule. Individual notes are drafted in their owning beads; THIS bead owns the register's format, review bar (each note: what changed, why, what you'll observe, how to adapt), publication (docs artifact), and completeness check (every IMPROVED Ledger row links a note; CI-verified).

THE OUT-OF-TIER LEDGER (§16.6): the honest fringe — complex-script shaping, CFF, variable fonts, exotic mesh/media formats, arbitrary GLSL — each with rationale and a REVISIT TRIGGER.

Acceptance: Ledger generation + badge in CI with regression blocking; the notes register published with the seed set complete and cross-linked; out-of-tier ledger with triggers; a completeness CI check (no IMPROVED without a note; no TIERED without an out-of-tier row).

title: W6: fmd-math tier 2 — the long-tail construct program, scheduled by corpus rank
description:
The post-G2 continuation of the coverage ratchet (§11.5, G5 criterion: "the ratchet continuing past its G2 floor into tier-2"): implement the LONG-TAIL constructs — \substack, uncommon decorations, exotic environments, and whatever else G0-4's harvest ranked below the tier-1 cut — in DESCENDING OCCURRENCE ORDER (the harvest's ranked table is the schedule; re-rank as the corpus-pending list from W10CORPUS adds real-scene evidence).

Working rules inherited from tier 1: each construct lands with (a) layout per the published TeX rules (Appendix-G parameters where applicable) over the calibrated metrics; (b) span-map provenance (W6SPAN's invariant: every glyph/rule carries source spans); (c) Gallery review against LaTeX renders for visually-nontrivial constructs; (d) the ratchet baseline UPDATED in the same change (coverage strictly increases — W6RATCHET's monotone rule); (e) its precise unsupported-error REMOVED and the error-audit inventory updated. Until a construct lands, its named error and tracking link remain the contract (never silence, never garbage).

Corpus-pending discipline (§15.3): scenes in VIDEO_CORPUS.lock marked pending-with-named-constructs get UNBLOCKED as their constructs land — each tier-2 construct's completion note lists which corpus scenes it unblocks, and the G4a harness re-runs them (the ratchet's real-world half advancing in lockstep).

This bead is deliberately open-ended: treat it as the tier-2 EPIC-of-record — file per-construct child beads as they are scheduled, each with the (a)-(e) checklist, so `br` reflects the actual sprint plan R1's escalation path calls for ("gate amended publicly with a construct-sprint plan" if G2 coverage misses).

Acceptance (per increment): construct green under (a)-(e); ratchet dashboard reflects the increase; unblocked corpus scenes pass. Bead closes only when the harvest's tier-2 list is exhausted or remaining constructs are formally moved to the out-of-tier ledger with revisit triggers (§16.6).

title: W4: dependency-gated animation classes — geometry-backed indication, numbers, string transforms
description:
The tail of the 80-class animation catalog (fm-cye) whose Reference constructors need mobject-library geometry, composition operators, or W6 span maps — every underlying MECHANISM already exists in fmn-anim; these are constructors + wiring only.

Geometry-backed indication (needs fm-oab: Dot/Circle/Line/SurroundingRectangle/Underline): FocusOn (Transform between Dots with an updater-tracked target), CircleIndicate, Flash (lines + ShowCreationThenDestruction per line, grouped), FlashAround/FlashUnder (VShowPassingFlash over a surrounding path), AnimationOnSurroundingRectangle + ShowPassingFlashAround/ShowCreationThenDestructionAround/ShowCreationThenFadeAround, Broadcast (specialized.py: LaggedStart of Restores over styled circles).

Composition-backed (needs fm-hfe AnimationGroup/Succession/LaggedStart): the grouped forms of Flash/Broadcast/AnimationOnSurroundingRectangle above, ShowCreationThenFadeOut (Succession), FlashyFadeIn (AnimationGroup), and wrapping transform_matching_parts' returned Vec into the real TransformMatchingParts group (run_time=2, lag_ratio=0) with clean_up_from_scene semantics (scene removes pieces, adds target — coordinate with fm-5xm).

Numbers (needs fm-y69 DecimalNumber): ChangingDecimal, ChangeDecimalToValue, CountInFrom — UpdateFromAlphaFunc-shaped over set_value.

Strings (needs fm-70s span maps): AddTextWordByWord (build_groups word boundaries), TransformMatchingStrings/TransformMatchingTex (matching_blocks over symbol substrings; the fsci assignment matcher enters at string_mobject's shape matching per D-09 — NOT in transform_matching_parts, confirmed against the pinned tree).

Acceptance: each class constructible with Reference-default parameters, doc-mapped to its reference file:line, effect signatures declared, tests per family.

title: GATE G5 — Distribution & Leapfrogs: shipped, browsable, accelerated, extended
description:
Convergence gate G5 (plan §20.3). Criteria:

(1) W11 SHIPPED: per-tier binaries with selection UX, wheels with the namespace policy, npm/WASM, font/license bundles, reproducible releases (all four W11 beads). (2) The WASM timeline player (tier 2) and the browser Studio direction demonstrated (W11WASM building on W5WASM + W4TIMELINE). (3) Graph/DataFrame/Markdown mobjects landed at enhanced-tier quality (W7DATA lineage). (4) The fmd-math ratchet CONTINUING past its G2 floor into tier-2 constructs (the ratchet is a permanent public metric, not a gate-passing artifact). (5) The Accelerator Annex BROADENED: the CUDA production backend from its ledger spike (OQ-10's outcome), wider platform tuning per §17.6's playbooks, the autotune corpus grown. (6) The exploratory tier OPENED (differentiable-animation research, SME/AMX investigations — explicitly research, never product-gated).

This gate also inherits any deferred obligations with public notes: the annex-preview requirement if G3 exercised its fallback (OQ-12), Windows bit-certification if OQ-6 resolved positive, tier-2 construct sprints scheduled by corpus rank.

title: W3: Family tree, positional API, bounding boxes, uniforms
description:
Implement the structural/positional surface (§8.4, §1.1): the full positional API — next_to, arrange, arrange_in_grid, to_edge, to_corner, align_to, shift, move_to, center, scale, stretch, set_width/height/depth, match_* — locked by structural fixtures against the Reference (loose f32 tolerances per §16.4, since we compute in f64); bounding boxes with dirty-flag propagation through the family tree (invalidate on point mutation via the RecordBuffer dirty channel, on submobject add/remove, on transform); the cached family flattening with correct invalidation.

Uniforms (§1.1, §8.4): the COMPLETE per-object uniform inventory as typed state — including the four clip-plane slots, stroke_behind, depth-test flag, is_fixed_in_frame (a float mix, per the kept camera model), per-kind AA widths, shading triple (reflectiveness, gloss, shadow) — because scene code reads and writes mobject.uniforms directly (API surface), and Lumen's StyleTable synchronizes from it.

Design care: positional operations are defined against bounding boxes in the Reference; ours must match its box conventions (about_point/about_edge semantics, buff application, stretch vs scale) exactly enough that fixture arrays coincide. Where the Reference's box is subtly wrong (stale caches), ours is correct — any user-visible divergence gets a Behavior Note.

Acceptance: positional fixture corpus green (generated from the pinned Reference across representative shapes/nesting); bbox invalidation property tests (mutation through any channel dirties ancestors exactly once); uniform read/write round-trip via the future Python bridge surface (engine-side test now).
close_reason: The structural/positional surface landed (§8.4, §1.1). Bounding boxes: BoundingBox [min,mid,max] value type with critical-point selection (np.sign semantics — -0.0 selects mid, not min); Stage::get_bounding_box lazily recomputed and keyed by a subtree SIGNATURE (FNV over every family member's point-field revision + identity + len), so a point write (revision bump), a raw RecordBuffer write, a resize, or a structural attach/detach all invalidate automatically through ANY channel with no explicit dirty-flag bookkeeping — the D-20 lazy-revisioned-mirror pattern. materializations counter is the laziness hook. Positional API on Stage (recursing over family exactly like the Reference's Mobject methods over get_family): shift, scale/scale_about, stretch/stretch_about, center, to_edge/to_corner (align_on_border), next_to, move_to, align_to, set_coord/set_x/y/z, rescale_to_fit, set_width/height/depth (+stretch), stretch_to_fit_*, match_width/height/depth/coord/x/y/z, arrange, arrange_in_grid; plus the full critical-point getters (get_center/edge_center/corner/left/right/top/bottom/zenith/nadir, get_coord/x/y/z, length_over_dim/get_width/height/depth, get_start/end). apply_points_function core with about_point/about_edge pivot resolution matching the Reference. Uniforms: complete typed inventory (is_fixed_in_frame as a float MIX not bool, shading triple, four clip-plane slots, anti_alias_width, joint_type enum<->code, flat_stroke, scale_stroke_with_zoom, stroke_behind, depth_test, use_winding_fill) on Entry with read/write accessors + family-recursing setters; carried through copy_family/snapshot/restore. Appendix C rulings: C-2 fixed (get_scale_stroke_with_zoom reads the CORRECT uniform, not flat_stroke) + BN-07 drafted; C-7 (use_winding_fill accepted as an explicit no-op, changes no output bits). Acceptance met: positional fixture corpus green — 26 scenarios generated by scripts/gen_positional_fixtures.py (Reference formulas transcribed from mobject.py into NumPy f64, independent of the Rust engine) rebuilt through the Stage and checked point-for-point + root bbox at loose f32 tol (§16.4); bbox invalidation property tests (lazy: N reads=1 materialization; point-write channel, positional op, leaf-mutation-dirties-ancestor-exactly-once, structural attach/detach); uniform read/write round-trip + recursing-setter family reach; C-2/BN-07 and C-7 tested at both the Uniforms and Stage levels. Gates: fmt --check clean; check --all-targets; clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo test green (fmn-mobject: +26-scenario corpus + 8 bbox/uniform property tests + 8 new unit tests; 62 workspace suites, 0 failures); ubs library src panic-free (remaining 3 criticals are test-only panic!/unwrap fixture-integrity guards, same accepted stance as fm-6h6). Points read from the RecordBuffer point field; QuadPath-specific point semantics still land in W7. Follow-ups: fm-ncq (copy semantics to the letter) and fm-yra (updaters/.animate) build on this.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: AUDIT ADDENDUM — Appendix C rulings owned here: C-2 — the Reference's get_scale_stroke_with_zoom() reads the WRONG uniform (flat_stroke); ours reads the correct scale_stroke_with_zoom uniform (fixed, Behavior-Noted under BN-07). C-7 — use_winding_fill is a documented NO-OP in the Reference (the earclip path is dead in the shipped fill); we ACCEPT the API for compatibility as an explicit no-op (our analytic fill never needed it) — the uniform inventory must include it, accepting writes, affecting nothing, with a doc note. Both get unit tests asserting the ruling (C-2: correct uniform read; C-7: setting it changes no output bits on a fixture scene).

title: W3: The render-order model — z_index, batching partitions, ordering-trace fixtures
description:
Implement the Reference's ACTUAL render-order semantics (§8.5, §1.5): top-level sort by z_index with STABLE scene order for ties; adjacent compatible-item batching; depth-test and fixed-in-frame partitions — kept as semantics, because what draws over what is meaning, not pixels. Lumen consumes this as its draw-order model (§10.1); painter's order for transparent content descends from it (§10.4, §10.8's exact-painter-order command runs).

Deliverable is a specification-with-tests, engine-side: given a scene graph (with shared submobjects, multiple parents, mixed z_index, stroke_behind, depth-tested 3D content, fixed-in-frame overlays), produce the deterministic draw sequence. ORDERING-TRACE FIXTURES pin the tricky cases: a submobject shared by two parents (drawn when? once or twice?), z_index on a child vs parent, stroke_behind interleaving (fill/stroke split ordering), add/remove/bring_to_front/bring_to_back effects on stable order, and the depth-test partition boundary (painter order within non-depth-tested; per-tile depth among depth-tested).

Generate the fixture expectations from the pinned Reference's batching code by INSPECTION (its semantics, not its pixel output), recording each ruling with a source citation — this is the kind of archaeology that must be done once, in one bead, not rediscovered per renderer bug.

Acceptance: the ordering-trace corpus green; property test (stable under no-op mutations; insertion order preserved among equal keys); the written ordering spec committed beside the fixtures (Lumen's W5 beads cite it as normative).
close_reason: Render-order model landed (§8.5). docs/RENDER_ORDER.md is the normative spec: 12 rulings, each cited into the pinned Reference (scene.py:300/327/338/360/371/389/394, mobject.py:435/1238/2056, shader_wrapper.py:117/277/354, utils/family_ops.py:23, utils/iterables.py:48). Implementation: fmn_mobject::order (BatchKey = ProgramKind + the uniform inventory, bitwise on floats; DrawPlan with per-item group/batch/root/passes; Stage::draw_plan is a pure function of scene state) plus the scene-list ops brought to the Reference's exact semantics (add = remove+append+stable-sort by (z_index,position); bring_to_front = add; bring_to_back = remove+prepend with NO sort, deliberately beating z_index until the next add; remove = recursive ungrouping; replace = splice-if-member; set_z_index writes the family and never re-sorts). z_index is per-object data threaded through the detached Mobject, the VMobject builder, copies, become, and snapshots — durable schema to minor 1.2 by append (§6.7). Two D5 divergences documented: a diamond child draws once (our family dedups; the Reference's get_family would draw it twice and double-composite alpha), and a child's z_index orders nothing (stated rather than rediscovered). Acceptance: 23-test ordering-trace corpus green (shared submobject one-per-root, diamond, child-vs-parent z_index, stroke_behind pass order, every shader-id uniform splitting a batch, the group-boundary batch rule, add/remove/front/back/replace traces, no-op-mutation stability, snapshot round-trip); self-goldens verified NOT drifted (the stage golden writes its own STAGE_SCHEMA document, not the persist form). 866 workspace tests, scripts/check.sh green.

title: G0-2: Renderer look study — calibrate the analytic renderer against captured Reference imagery
description:
Executed calibration study fixing Lumen's aesthetic parameters BEFORE W5 scales (§20.1 spike 2 → §10, §6.3). The product contract is "correct AND beautiful, judged as at-least-as-good" — this spike turns "the same feel, cleaner" from aspiration into a measured statement.

Scope: render the calibration set with the prototype analytic renderer — fills with per-vertex gradients, self-intersecting paths, every joint/cap combination, glow dots, 3D lighting spheres/surfaces, text samples — side-by-side against one-time captured Reference imagery (no certified Pango/llvmpipe capture environment is maintained; capture once, keep forever). Fix, by decision recorded in the plan: (a) the adaptive-AA defaults and tile-escalation thresholds (§10.4), (b) the AA profile and the ~1.5px weight, (c) the smooth "auto" join tuning and miter-limit default (§10.3), (d) gradient behavior — confirming the kept interpolate_color sqrt(lerp(c1^2,c2^2,a)) form and RMS average_color composite correctly in linear light (§6.3), (e) the finalize_color lighting match — (reflectiveness, gloss, shadow), light at (-10,10,10), dark_shift 0.2 (§1.5, Appendix B), (f) the cubic→quad converter tolerance default so curve fidelity visibly exceeds the Reference's (§7.2).

Why: the Reference's look constants are the aesthetic DNA of 3Blue1Brown and are KEPT deliberately (D-04); but they were tuned for a GPU pipeline full of workarounds (signed-alpha fills, x1.06 composite un-mangle, polyline ribbon strokes). Porting the constants onto honest mathematics shifts their visual effect; only side-by-side calibration can close that loop.

Acceptance: the calibration gallery checked in (small, public, permissively-licensed primitives); a parameters document with every chosen constant + rationale; risk R2's standing mitigation (Gallery review as gate input) stood up.
close_reason:
The G0-2 look study is executed and ratified: docs/g0/G0-2-look-study-ratification.md, with the rendered evidence in docs/g0/g0-2-renders/ and the measurements reproducible via scripts/g0_2_measure.py. Unblocks fm-5oi, fm-oac, fm-6cf, fm-3g6, fm-o3j.

METHOD — two independent lines of evidence, kept separate so they could disagree: the Reference's GLSL/Python read as source (every constant carries file:line), and measurements of the fm-o3i captures. Where they agreed the number is settled; where they disagreed, the disagreement WAS the finding.

DECISIONS FIXED (the bead's (a)-(f), plus glow):
(b) AA = smoothstep over a 1.5 px band. Measured: band 1.560 px, RMS 0.0031 — under one 8-bit level across the whole profile. 10-90 width 0.99 px.
(c) Round joins from the distance field; auto crossover smoothstep(-0.8,-0.9,cos t); effective miter limit 3.1623 half-widths, DERIVED (the Reference has no miter_limit constant).
(d) interpolate_color is EXACTLY sqrt(lerp(c1^2,c2^2,a)) — 0.000000 error — and average_color is exactly RMS. Composite in linear light; the kept form is a gamma-2 stand-in differing by at most 9.4/255, peaking at a~0.2 and exact at both endpoints. That table is BN-04's evidence.
(e) add_light kept verbatim; Surface shading (0.3,0.2,0.4); light (-10,10,10).
(f) cubic->quad tolerance 0.1 px, justified by measurement: the Reference's fixed 2-quad approximation deviates up to 7.71 px at 1080p — over 5x the entire AA band. 0.1 px is 77x tighter.
glow: (1-r/R)^2 exactly, confirmed twice (source glow_factor=2.0; measured exponent 1.986, competing models 10x worse).
(a) is the one decision measurement CANNOT fix: the Reference has no escalation concept, it supersamples every fill unconditionally. So the criterion and the default are fixed here (analytic coverage, no supersampling) and fm-gmr is named owner of record for the numeric threshold.

THREE FINDINGS THAT CHANGE WHAT GETS BUILT:
1. THE FILL AA IS 2.3 BITS. quadratic_bezier/fill/frag.glsl has no AA term at all — a hard discard plus a 2x supersampled f16 target, box-resolved. Predicted 5 coverage levels; measured on a bare fill edge (stroke_width=0, so nothing covers the boundary): 4 distinct intermediate levels at 0.2471/0.4981/0.7452/0.7567. Against the stroke's continuous smoothstep this is the concrete at-least-as-good claim for §10.2, and it is why (a) defaults to NO supersampling — we would be paying 4x to lose precision.
2. bevel AND miter ARE NAMED BACKWARDS. miter_factor=0 (BEVEL_JOINT, code 2) yields -tan(t/2), the pointed corner; miter_factor=1 (MITER_JOINT, code 3) yields +cot(t/2), the blunt one. Corroborated independently from the captures: at the zig-zag's turn cos t = 0.154 > -0.8 so auto must equal bevel, and the measured apex widths are auto 4 px, bevel 6 px, miter 9 px. Ports must key on the NUMERIC CODES; ours already does.
3. dark_shift IS NOT A LIGHTING PARAMETER. The bead (and plan §10.4, now trued up) listed 'dark_shift 0.2' alongside reflectiveness/gloss/shadow. At the pin its only occurrence is textured_surface/frag.glsl:16, a light/dark TEXTURE crossfade that finalize_color never sees. Struck, so the port does not manufacture a parameter that never existed.

THE MEASUREMENT I GOT WRONG FIRST, AND WHY IT MATTERS (L2). Per-scanline 10-90 ramps on the square gave 1.07 px on the vertical edge and 1.59 px on the horizontal one — an anisotropy the shader cannot produce, since pixels are square. The cause: an axis-aligned edge lands at ONE sub-pixel phase, so the 'ramp' measured was the phase, not the profile. A circular boundary sweeps every phase; binning ~7,800 near-boundary pixels by exact signed distance to a least-squares circle (residual 0.041 px) recovered the true profile. Two other first-pass numbers were also artefacts — the glow profile had run into the neighbouring dot, and the gradient sample had landed in the gap between the square and the circle, returning the background as the 'midpoint'. All three looked plausible. The rule that caught them: a measurement contradicting the source is a bug in the measurement until proven otherwise.

THE SIDE-BY-SIDE (4 of 6 panels; lighting_3d and text_sample need 3D and Scribe, filed as fm-gfn): self_intersections is at-least-as-good and shows why — the Reference's star core renders LIGHTER than its limbs because winding 2 composites the fill twice through the signed-alpha trick, while ours is one uniform colour. joints_and_caps is different-but-fine: four Reference corners collapse to one round join, with no notch at any vertex. glow is at-least-as-good. gradient_fills is OPEN and is fm-5oi's input, not a settled result — the Reference shows a hard diagonal fan seam (per-vertex interpolation across the triangle fan from base_point), ours is smooth, but ours is a defined stand-in and §10.2's real interior field is unbuilt.

PLAN TRUED UP: §10.4 and Appendix B corrected on dark_shift; §10.4 now records the per-vertex Gouraud lighting as a §12 question.
FILED: fm-fte (Appendix C + BN-04 entry for the x0.95/x1.06 round-trip, a 0.70% systematic overshoot we do not inherit — worth recording so our correct fills are not read as a colour regression), fm-gfn (the two remaining gallery panels).
GATES: scripts/check.sh all green (22 crates, DAG OK); spike fmt/clippy clean, 75 tests pass; ubs Critical 0 (the 55 scene.rs warnings are pre-existing whole-file inventory — my delta is 4 unwraps on hardcoded path builders, the file's own idiom); ruff clean.

title: W6: fmd-math extensions — extensible delimiters, environments, macros, preamble packs
description:
Complete fmd-math's tier-1 surface (§11.4):

EXTENSIBLE DELIMITERS + WIDE ACCENTS: assembled from CM's extension glyphs (repeatable middle segments + caps) per G0-3's ratified strategy (OQ-2), with DRAWN-PATH CONSTRUCTION as the universal fallback so NO requested size can fail — a \left( around a 12-row matrix gets a correct paren, always. \left...\right sizing math (delimiter covers content height per TeX's rules), \big/\Big/\bigg/\Bigg fixed sizes.

ENVIRONMENTS: the matrix family (matrix/pmatrix/bmatrix/vmatrix/Vmatrix), cases, array with column specs, align*-class multi-line with alignment points — column measurement, alignment, inter-row spacing per the published rules. (W7's Matrix mobject consumes the delimiter engine directly — §11.6.)

USER MACROS + PREAMBLE PACKS: \newcommand-style non-recursive substitution macros (with argument support, recursion refused with a named error); named PREAMBLE PACKS — macro/symbol bundles replacing tex_templates.yml — registered through fmn-config's registry (W1CONF), with a compatibility mapping for the common Reference templates. Pack identity participates in cache keys and the input closure (a pack change re-typesets, correctly).

Acceptance: delimiter-assembly golden paths at many sizes including past-glyph-inventory sizes (fallback engages); environment fixtures (alignment correctness, matrix spacing) vs published rules + LaTeX-visual Gallery review; macro expansion tests (arguments, nesting, recursion refusal); pack round-trip (define → use → cache-key changes on edit); tier-2 constructs from the harvest error with correct names.
close_reason: fmd-math's tier-1 surface is complete, landed upstream as franken_markdown 4e5066c and consumed here at the bumped pin. DELIMITERS: the ADR-0005 drawn-path mainline in full — parametric quadratic constructions (new drawn.rs) for parens+surd (ported from the proven G0-3 spike) and brackets/braces/bars/angles/floor/ceil/slashes, engaging past the 1.25x uniform-scale ceiling AND serving outright when a face has no authored glyph, so no requested size can fail (six-deep-fraction tests across all eight families); provenance spans survive the mechanism switch; \big/\Big/\bigg/\Bigg hit their fixed 0.85/1.15/1.45/1.75em targets monotonically. (Bead text predates ADR-0005: glyph assembly was REJECTED there — CM Unicode maps no extension pieces — and the ratified drawn mainline is what landed.) STRETCHY: \widehat/\widetilde/\overbrace/\underbrace/\overrightarrow/\overleftarrow as drawn bands spanning their bases; braces take scripts as centered limits (\mathop semantics, tested). ENVIRONMENTS: grid engine with shared column measurement, per-column alignment, baselineskip/lineskip row stacking (+\jot for align), \vcenter axis centering; matrix family wraps the rule-19 delimiter engine (bare matrix stays bare — caught+fixed a nulldelimiterspace leak), smallmatrix tightens, cases gets one stretched brace + left columns, array honors l/c/r/| (vertical rules drawn; @/p{} etc. precise refusals), align/align*/aligned close the r,l pair around the alignment point (equal-x '=' test) with \minalignsep between pairs. MACROS+PACKS: token-level expansion before the grammar (new macros.rs) — packs fmd-math/pack/{default,basic,empty} matching fmn-config's registry content_ids exactly, inline \newcommand/\renewcommand under LaTeX shadowing rules, args keep true source spans while body material carries the call-site span (isolate/t2c work through macros — span-map test), recursion refused by name (direct+mutual), budgets (65536 tokens/depth 32) kill bombs cleanly, MacroSet::canonical_bytes is the deterministic cache-key ingredient (pack edit => bytes change => re-typeset). COVERAGE: private-corpus PARSE+LAYOUT rose 98.188->98.921% unique / 98.916->99.379% occurrence-weighted; ratchet re-run (RATCHET_UPDATE=1) regenerated baseline/trend/dashboard, trend records the advance at the new pin; only five math-alphanumeric chars remain layout-pending (upstream fonts bead). Upstream: 1908 workspace tests, clippy clean, policy/wasm-core/determinism gates green, two layout goldens re-blessed deliberately (drawn parens replace over-scaled glyphs — adjudicated). Here: pin bumped in SUITE.lock+Cargo.toml (one-commit ritual), UPSTREAM_LEDGER row 2 updated, fmn-tex pin-surface test updated to the crossed frontier, full gate green (fm-rvm-family boundary flake retried green x4). Unblocks fm-7dw (Scribe II), fm-y69 (de-TeX'd natives), fm-j5t scheduling; G2's blocker set shrinks by one.

title: W5: The CUDA annex production backend — via frankentorch, per the §17.6 playbook (post-ledger-spike)
description:
Implement the annex's second engine (§17.5, §17.6, §10.7, D-22; gated on OQ-10's ledger-spike outcome from G0-8): CUDA via frankentorch — ft is the ONLY GPU gateway; no wgpu, no direct CUDA bindings.

The §17.6 NVIDIA playbook, implemented: keep the scene RESIDENT — path headers, quadratic segments, styles, instances, image descriptors, macrotile bins, and fine-tile command lists live on-device (24GB is ample for persistent scene state + several 4K surfaces); upload ONLY DELTAS (changed transforms, styles, geometry ranges, ordering metadata — W5IR's revision taxonomy is exactly the delta vocabulary). Batch by pipeline class (solid fills, strokes, gradients, images, 3D triangles) WITHIN painter-order command runs; one block or cooperative block group per tile; raster and composite in stable command order; DETERMINISTIC count/prefix/scatter binning — never one-kernel-per-mobject, never unordered atomic appends. A small pinned-memory ring + multiple non-default streams overlap delta upload, rasterization, NV12 readback, and host-side ffmpeg submission; shared memory stages command/segment chunks ONLY where it provably removes repeated global reads (occupancy costs are real). Don't over-engineer the bus: 4K@30 readback is ~1GB/s RGBA / ~0.4GB/s NV12 against ~25GB/s PCIe gen4 x16 — plain pinned readback is fine; zero-copy is an Apple luxury. NVENC rides the §14.3 boundary. Tensor/RT cores are the WRONG tools here (branchy geometric coverage, ordered compositing, memory movement) — ordinary CUDA execution, good binning, persistent layout.

Hard boundaries (identical to Metal, R21): standard-only, never certified; PG-A profiles (RTX-4090-class pinned machine) gate ANNEX changes only; backend identity journaled; engine-equivalence budget vs certified frames; annex work pauses when core PG-1..PG-3 regress.

Acceptance: the corpus rendering through CUDA within the engine-equivalence budget; delta-upload instrumentation (bytes/frame recorded, resident-state verified across frames); binning determinism test (same scene ⇒ same command lists across runs); PG-A rig numbers on the pinned CUDA profile; graceful absence (no CUDA ⇒ CPU/other engines, no error).

title: EPIC W4 — Choreo: the animation engine (fmn-anim)
description:
Workstream W4 (plan §9, §20.2): the animation calculus. Depends on W3.

Contents: the Animation contract — constructor surface field-for-field, begin/interpolate/finish lifecycle, get_sub_alpha lag semantics, prepare_animation accepting Animation | _AnimationBuilder only (§9.1); the RationalFrameClock — i64 frame index over fps, drift-free, emitting the Reference's exact nominal sample sequence (arange(0,run_time,1/fps)+1/fps semantics: no alpha-zero progression frame, begin()'s separate zero-interpolate, upward duration rounding, final_alpha_value) (§9.2); the six-step frame order kept exactly — animation update_mobjects(dt) → interpolate(alpha) → time advance → scene updaters over post-interpolation state → capture → emit — with the Rev-4 FramePacket freeze at capture making everything downstream pipeline-legal (§9.3); the five mechanism families and the 80 animation classes as parameterizations, the align_data path under a 1000-pair structural fixture corpus, AnimationGroup/Succession/LaggedStart interval math, squish_rate_func/time_span through one normalized-alpha pipeline, and the declarative Timeline (§9.4); the segment-purity classifier enabling embarrassingly-parallel frame rendering for pure segments, conservative by construction — any unrecognized effect demotes to stateful (§9.5, R20).

Why the order is sacred: always_redraw-style scenes semantically depend on scene updaters observing post-interpolation state. This is semantics, not implementation detail.

Exit: all W4 task beads closed; the update-order corpus green; adaptive/variable frame sampling permanently refused (D-18).

comments.text:
AUDIT ADDENDUM — testing & logging doctrine (binding on every bead in this epic):

Every task bead in this epic lands with its tests as PART OF ITS SCOPE — a bead without its tests is not done:
1. COMPREHENSIVE UNIT TESTS, colocated in-crate, covering the bead's stated acceptance criteria INCLUDING negative and edge cases (degenerate inputs, resource-budget violations, version-mismatch refusals, error-path assertions — not just happy paths).
2. E2E REGISTRATION: any bead landing user-visible behavior (a mobject, an animation, a CLI flag, an output format, a Studio surface) registers at least one scripted end-to-end scenario with the Gauntlet e2e harness (fm-fjq) — driven through the real surfaces (CLI / Rust API / fmn-python / Studio HTTP), asserting outputs (bit-locked hashes on certified paths; structural assertions elsewhere), exit codes, and emitted-file inventory.
3. DETAILED STRUCTURED LOGGING: behavior flows through the owned tracing layer (§17.1/§18 — scene→play→frame→phase→tile spans, stage timings, counters, decision points: engine selection, cache hits, purity classifications, barriers). Where correct behavior is invisible in the output ("the preflight ran before frame 0", "wait() frames hit the tile cache"), the e2e scenario ASSERTS ON THE LOGS. On failure, the harness auto-bundles a deterministic repro (scene + input closure + logs + journal tail).
4. GATES BEFORE CLOSE: scripts/check.sh green (fmt, check, clippy -D warnings, test) + ubs clean on changed files, per AGENTS.md. Determinism-relevant beads additionally run their {1,4,16}-thread sweep before close.

title: W5: WASM tier 1 — the frame renderer in the browser
description:
Implement WASM tier 1 (§10.7): the frame renderer compiled to wasm32 — single-threaded by default; threads only under atomics + cross-origin isolation — rendering scenes to canvas/ImageData in the browser. Tier 2 (the serialized-timeline player consuming W4TIMELINE's format) is a G5 deliverable; this bead makes tier 1 real and keeps the workspace honestly wasm-clean.

Scope: the wasm feature axis through fmn-core/geom/mobject/anim/render/frame (fmn-platform provides wasm capability implementations: virtual fs, performance.now clock, no process capability — the ffmpeg boundary is structurally absent and native outputs are the only sinks); wasm-bindgen surface (pre-authorized under D1) exposing scene construction + frame rendering; size discipline (feature-gate fonts/assets; measure and record the artifact size — R19's CI-measured budgets).

Depends on G0-7's wasm-target audit (which closure members compile; which need shims at fmn-platform — R15's mitigation). Determinism note: wasm is not in the certified matrix, but standard-mode determinism (same seed ⇒ same output on the same build) must hold — fmn-dmath already gives wasm the same transcendentals, which is most of the battle.

Acceptance: a browser demo rendering a primitive-corpus scene to canvas; wasm32 CI build + headless test (node/wasmtime) for the core crates; artifact-size budget recorded; single-thread determinism test (two renders, same bytes).

title: W7: Surface CubicBezier conversion failures instead of truncating the built path
description: CubicBezier::build in crates/fmn-library/src/poly.rs discards QuadPath::add_cubic_bezier_curve_to's Result. Invalid/non-finite controls or an unrepresentable tolerance request can therefore yield a VMobject containing only the start anchor, silently changing a cubic into a point. Define the constructor/build error contract coherently across the Rust builder and From/TryFrom surface; do not panic or silently fall back to a coarser curve. Acceptance: failure is typed and observable, valid builds remain unchanged, non-finite/pathological controls have regression coverage, and conversion errors cannot publish a partial VMobject.

title: W1: The single RNG — PCG64DXSM with named substreams and keyed per-frame forks
description:
Implement fmn-core's one-RNG rule (§6.5, D-06). The Reference carries TWO seeded legacy streams (CPython random + NumPy legacy RandomState); with output parity dropped, both are irrelevant — FrankenManim standardizes on fnp-random's PCG64DXSM, already bit-exact against NumPy for explicit seeds.

Requirements: (a) a single seeded root stream exposed via fmn-core; OS entropy when unseeded; (b) NAMED SUBSTREAMS derived per subsystem (layout jitter, stream-line seeding, sampling, shuffle...) so features don't perturb each other's sequences — adding a new consumer must never shift an existing consumer's draws; (c) snapshot/restore of full stream state into SceneState and the replay journal; (d) KEYED PER-FRAME FORKS (Rev 4, load-bearing for §9.5): a frame's stream state derives from (substream id, frame index) — NEVER from sequential pulls consumed in scheduler completion order. This is the property that makes frame-parallel rendering replay-identical BY CONSTRUCTION, and the reason per-thread completion-order RNG is on §10.5's permanent refusal list (D-18); (e) render-affecting map iteration uses ordered maps only — audit helper + lint note.

Testing: substream independence tests (adding draws on stream A leaves stream B's sequence untouched); fork determinism tests (fork(sub, k) identical regardless of call order/thread); snapshot/restore round-trip; NumPy seed-parity vectors via fnp.

Draft Behavior Note BN-01: seeded scenes reproduce within FrankenManim, not across engines.

Acceptance: all above tests green; the fork API documented for Choreo (§9.5) and StreamLines (§12.4) consumers.
close_reason: One-RNG rule landed in fmn-core/src/rng.rs: PCG64DXSM + SeedSequence, bit-exact to NumPy (81 parity vectors from scripts/gen_rng_vectors.py: seedseq words, draws, doubles, substream + fork spawn keys — all green). RngRoot -> named Substreams (canonical name encoding mirrored in the generator) -> keyed per-frame forks (pure function of (substream, frame); call-order/thread invariant by construction, D-18). Snapshot/restore round-trips full state. OrderedMap alias + doc as the ordered-iteration audit hook. BN-01 drafted. Subtlety pinned by vectors: NumPy seeds PCG64DXSM via the FULL 128-bit multiplier srandom, runtime steps use the DXSM cheap multiplier. Owned temporarily per SUITE.lock gap: migration to fnp-random filed as fm-ai1 (blocked on fm-g2c). Gate-hygiene note: clippy piped through tail masks exit codes — caught and fixed here; future sweeps use pipefail.

title: W11: Release binaries — per-SIMD-tier artifacts, selection UX, install script
description:
Package the engine (§17.3, §20.2 W11): release binaries per platform x SIMD build tier — portable / x86-64-v3 (AVX2) / x86-64-v4 (AVX-512) / aarch64+NEON — with install/launch tier SELECTION UX (the installer or first-run picks the right tier from HardwareTopology; a wrong-tier launch fails cleanly with guidance, never SIGILL); the curl|bash install script (scripts/install.sh — platform detect, tier detect, signed artifact fetch, checksum verify, PATH setup); signed releases with checksums; reproducible release builds (the release pipeline pins the toolchain per SUITE.lock and records provenance — the determinism doctrine applied to our own artifacts).

Size/time budgets (R19): embedded fonts + Studio UI assets are the size drivers — feature-gated where tiering allows, CI-MEASURED budgets on binary size and compile time with alert thresholds (a font-bundle or asset regression is visible, not silent).

Tier matrix discipline (R22): tiers capped at the four named; per-commit CI builds the two pinned profiles, the full matrix builds weekly; if CI budgets breach, a tier drops to weekly-only by recorded decision.

Acceptance: artifacts for all platform/tier combinations build in release CI; the install script tested on clean containers/VMs per platform (fresh-machine render works end-to-end with zero preinstalled deps — the leapfrog #1 demo, minus optional ffmpeg); tier-selection tests incl. the wrong-tier failure path; checksum/signature verification in the script; size/time budget reports in CI.

title: W6: The public coverage ratchet — occurrence-weighted fmd-math coverage as a headline metric
description:
Implement the coverage ratchet (§11.5, §18; R1's public mitigation). With no LaTeX fallback, coverage DISCIPLINE replaces fallback discipline — and it must be public, precise, and monotone.

Mechanics: against G0-4's frozen corpus (the ratchet's denominator), compute per-construct and aggregate coverage — OCCURRENCE-WEIGHTED (what fraction of real-world formula mass typesets) and UNIQUE-STRING (what fraction of distinct formulas), with PARSE-vs-LAYOUT success split out (a string that parses but mislays counts as layout-fail, not success). Wire as: (a) a CI job producing the numbers per commit; (b) a RATCHET RULE — coverage may never decrease (a regression is a build break; deliberate tier changes require updating a committed baseline with a written note); (c) the public dashboard artifact (§18: a first-class DX artifact — badge + per-construct table + trend, generated into the repo/docs), naming which T2 constructs are pending with their tracked issue links, honoring the licensing rule from G0-4 (publish numbers and construct names, never the 3b1b-authored strings).

Also here: the per-construct named-error audit — every construct in the harvest that is NOT tier-1 must produce its precise unsupported error with tier + tracking link (test the error text against the harvest inventory, so no construct ever fails silently).

Acceptance: ratchet CI green with committed baseline; a deliberate-regression negative test (removing a construct fails CI); dashboard artifact generated and rendered; error-audit test over the full harvest construct list; G2's coverage checkpoint criteria (R1: coverage misses gate → public amendment with construct-sprint plan) documented as the escalation path.
close_reason: The ratchet is live: docs/ratchet/{baseline.tsv,trend.tsv,dashboard.md} + fmn-conformance::ratchet + tests/coverage_ratchet.rs. Headline numbers (frozen G0-4 denominator, 9269 strings / 17711 occurrences): PARSE 99.577% occurrence-weighted / 99.266% unique; PARSE+LAYOUT 98.916% / 98.188%, per-construct pending tables with tracked links (fm-j5t / fm-kg9 / the upstream fonts bead), trend by pin rev, escalation path (R1 public-amendment rule) and §15.3 licensing documented on the dashboard. CI teeth via pin-coupling: coverage is a pure function of (frozen corpus, fmd-math pin), so the always-on test requires baseline.tsv to name the current SUITE.lock franken_markdown rev — a pin bump without a ratchet re-run fails CI even without the private corpus; corpus-bearing runs recompute all four counts, fail on any decrease (deliberate-regression negative test at the comparator: unit-tested), and bless with RATCHET_UPDATE=1 regenerating all three artifacts atomically. The per-construct named-error audit runs always-on: all 29 T2 command/env constructs from the harvest table produce their precise tier-tagged error naming fm-j5t (probed in both modes); char: rows are layout-plane. Full gate green (one fm-rvm flake retry).

title: W3: fnp-backed zero-copy NumPy round-trip for RecordBuffer
description: fm-cus landed the data plane with byte-layout tests locking the interleaved schema to numpy's structured-dtype packing (crates/fmn-mobject/tests/data_plane.rs), but the LIVE zero-copy round-trip through franken_numpy's structured-record engine (mobject.data as an fnp structured view over the RecordBuffer's current storage generation) needs fnp consumable, which arrives with SUITE.lock (fm-g2c). When it lands: export a RecordView-backed fnp structured array, assert zero-copy aliasing (writes both ways), the V3 detach on resize, and dtype equality with the Reference dtypes. title: W3: Copy semantics — manim's rules, to the letter
description:
Implement Mobject.copy() to the Reference's exact contract (§8.3) — user code depends on these rules, so they are API semantics, not pixel trivia: recursive copy of submobjects and ndarray attributes; updater CALLABLES kept by reference (not cloned); family-internal attribute references REMAPPED (if self.arrow is also self.submobjects[2], the copy's attribute points at the copy's submobject, not the original's); selected links cleared (parents; scene backrefs) per the Reference's rules.

Also here: the interaction with the arena (copying allocates fresh handles; generation bookkeeping), with the RecordBuffer (deep field copy; live views on the ORIGINAL unaffected; the copy starts with no views), and with target/saved-state machinery (generate_target, save_state / Restore use copies — get the reference topology right or Restore breaks).

The binding tier (fmn-python, W10) layers Python-level copy.copy / copy.deepcopy / pickle onto this engine contract — design the engine-side hooks now (a stable copy-map from old handle → new handle that the Python layer can walk for __dict__ remapping).

Acceptance: fixture tests generated from the Reference's copy behavior on representative object graphs (shared submobjects, attribute aliases, updaters, nested groups); remap-correctness property test (no copy ever references an original's family member); Restore round-trip test; documented rules for which attribute categories copy deep / by-reference / cleared.
close_reason: Copy semantics landed to the letter (§8.3): CopyMap — stable old→new handle map in family (DFS) order from copy_family_mapped, the engine hook fmn-python walks for __dict__ alias remapping (the Reference's family.index rule; order preservation + alias remap verified against a verbatim transcription of mobject.py copy()). Cleared-link rules structural: parents/scene-membership/target/saved_state cleared on every copied member (the stash_mobject_pointers list, exactly). generate_target/save_state/restore_mobject with the Reference's exact cross-link topology (target.saved_state and saved_state.target are SHARED links, order-sensitive — fixtured in both orders). become_mobject (become is a Rust 2024 reserved keyword) over already-aligned families: schema-checked data plane via RecordBuffer::assign_from through the copy-on-resize path (revisions bump past old — bbox signatures/mirrors resync; views detach V6), uniforms+tracker copy, match_updaters root-only; FamilyShapeMismatch names the fm-cye align_family seam. Corpus: gen_copy_fixtures.py transcribes copy()/generate_target/save_state/restore onto mock objects — 21 graph cases, 146 facts, all true; tests/copy_semantics.rs replays them (15 tests) incl. the no-alias-back property over the random corpus, diamond sharing per the ratified G0-1/D-11 family model (Reference would duplicate — documented), live-view isolation, snapshot round-trip of the new links. Accepted ubs findings: test-only panic! guards on malformed fixtures (established idiom, per fm-3xk close). Gates: fmt, check, clippy -D warnings, 364 workspace tests green, crate-DAG OK.

title: W2: space_ops + Rotation conventions — scipy semantics fixed, tested at singularities
description:
Implement space_ops signature-for-signature and the quaternion/Euler conventions module (§7.5, §2.2). The Reference's space_ops follows scipy Rotation's conventions — quaternion sign, composition order, as_euler("zxz") extraction, gimbal behavior — and users' camera code assumes them. We fix these conventions AS DOCUMENTED SEMANTICS (they are meaning, not implementation detail), implemented over fnp-linalg / fsci, tested explicitly at the hard points: gimbal-lock configurations, quaternion double-cover sign choices, near-identity and near-pi rotations, axis-angle degeneracies.

Scope: rotation_matrix, quaternions (mult, conjugate, from/to axis-angle), Euler conversions with the "zxz" behavior pinned, angle_between_vectors, normalize, cross/dot conveniences, z_to_vector, rotation_about_z fast paths, get_unit_normal (Appendix B: kept), 2D↔3D point promotion rules, complex↔R2 helpers — the full call-site inventory from the Reference's space_ops module, verified against Appendix A consumers.

Determinism note: everything here is f64 semantic math (§6.1); transcendentals route through the fmn-dmath seam so certified renders get bit-stable Euler/axis conversions (CameraFrame animations are transcendental-dense).

Acceptance: convention fixtures generated from scipy on the pinned Reference environment (loose f32 tolerance per §16.4); singularity tests with DEFINED outputs (no NaN escapes); property tests (composition associativity within tolerance, double-cover q ≡ -q, round-trip Euler→quat→Euler within branch conventions); doc page stating the conventions normatively.
close_reason: space_ops and the rotation conventions landed (§7.5, §2.2). SURFACE: crates/fmn-geom/src/space_ops.rs is manimlib/utils/space_ops.py ported signature for signature — cross/cross2d/dot/get_norm/norm_squared/get_dist/normalize(+_or fallback)/normalize_rows/poly_line_length/center_of_mass/midpoint/promote_point; quaternion_mult/conjugate/from_angle_axis/angle_axis_from_quaternion/rotation_matrix(_transpose)(_from_quaternion)/rotation_about_z/rotation_between_vectors/z_to_vector/rotate_vector(_2d)/angle_of_vector/angle_between_vectors/get_unit_normal/project_along_vector; find_intersection/line_intersection/line_intersects_path/get_closest_point_on_line/get_winding_number/tri_area/is_inside_triangle/compass_directions/thick_diagonal/complex_to_r3/r3_to_complex/complex_func_to_r3_func. The only member NOT ported is earclip_triangulation — that is triangulation, not space ops, and belongs to fm-81u (noted in the module doc). CONVENTIONS: crates/fmn-geom/src/rotation.rs reimplements scipy Rotation exactly rather than choosing its own — quaternion [x,y,z,w] scalar-last, from_rotvec/as_rotvec including BOTH small-angle series (so near-identity camera drags keep full relative precision), the double-cover normalization (|angle| <= pi), compose_quat's order (q applied first; M(pq)=M(p)M(q)), as_matrix's element layout, and a faithful port of scipy's quaternion-direct Euler decomposition for ARBITRARY sequences (lowercase extrinsic / uppercase intrinsic, symmetric and Tait-Bryan families, the +-pi wrap, and the 1e-7 gimbal window with its by-index degenerate assignment). TWO DELIBERATE DIFFERENCES, both refusals of silence: gimbal lock is DATA (EulerAngles::gimbal_lock) not a UserWarning, because CameraFrame has to branch on it; and every scipy raise / numpy NaN becomes a typed None or a defined value (zero-norm quaternion, identity axis-angle, parallel line_intersection, empty center_of_mass). REFACTOR: vec.rs is now only the numpy-array plumbing (add/sub/scale/lerp/mul_point_mat/transpose/np_isclose_all/Mat3); everything the Reference defines in space_ops moved to the public module and ~36 call sites across arclength/bezier/cubic/quadpath/smoothing were rehomed. rotation_matrix now goes through the quaternion exactly as the Reference does, so it is scipy-exact rather than Rodrigues-equivalent. FIXTURES: scripts/gen_space_ops_fixtures.py imports the pinned Reference's real space_ops module (stubbing only mapbox_earcut/tqdm/colour and the constants six, none of which space_ops computes with) and records 457 cases; tests/space_ops_parity.rs re-runs every one at 1e-12 absolute, with angles compared modulo 2pi since the +-pi branch cut is a representation choice. Cases cover cardinal+general+non-unit+degenerate axes x 9 angle regimes (0, 1e-12, pi/2, pi-1e-9, pi, pi+0.4, 3*TAU+1.1), all six Euler sequences x 13 rotations incl. both gimbal poles and just-outside-the-window, and every planar helper's degenerate branch. PROPERTIES (tests/rotation_properties.rs, 16 tests): composition associativity, q === -q double cover (same matrix, same Euler angles), Euler round-trip within the branch conventions, second-angle family ranges ([0,pi] symmetric / [-pi/2,pi/2] Tait-Bryan), gimbal lock exactly at the pole and not outside it, near-identity precision bounded by the series remainder, near-pi stability incl. the axis flip past pi, orthonormality + det=+1, and a NaN sweep over 25 degenerate input pairs across every op. DOC: docs/ROTATION_CONVENTIONS.md states all of it normatively (storage, axis-angle, composition order, matrices, sequences/ranges/gimbal, the degeneracy table, numerics, and what is deliberately absent). fnp-linalg/fsci were deliberately NOT pulled in: every operation here is a 3-vector or 3x3 closed form with no solve, so a linalg dependency would buy nothing and would need a new DAG edge; the actual solve paths in this crate are already tracked by fm-go7. GATES: scripts/check.sh green end to end (fmt, check --all-targets, clippy --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test, crate-DAG); fmn-geom 104 tests across 7 binaries, 0 failures; ubs criticals 0 on all three library sources (the 7 on the test files are the fixture-integrity panic!/unwrap guards, same accepted stance as fm-6h6/fm-jru). Consumers unblocked: fm-oab (geometry lineage needs compass_directions/find_intersection/angle_of_vector/rotate_vector/rotation_matrix_transpose), fm-0gy (camera/3D, the Euler surface), fm-2u6.

title: G0-3: fmd-math architecture spike — parse-and-layout proof over the hard constructs
description:
Compile-tested spike proving the shape of the math-layout engine BEFORE the fmd-math crate's API freezes (§20.1 spike 3 → §11.4; resolves OQ-2). This is the program's critical-path risk R1 (Critical severity: no LaTeX fallback exists, deliberately) — the spike exists to fail fast if the architecture is wrong.

Scope — parse AND lay out, with correct output paths: \frac (nested), sub/superscripts (including simultaneous sub+sup with correct kerning), radicals with indices, a \left( ... \right) delimiter pair at three sizes, a big operator with limits (\sum in display and text style), and a small matrix environment. This forces every load-bearing architectural question: (a) the atom-classification + inter-atom spacing engine shape (the eight TeX atom classes, the spacing table, style propagation display/text/script/scriptscript with \mathchoice-class behavior); (b) the math-metrics synthesis method for bundled Computer Modern — axis height, x-height, quad, sup/sub shifts, radical parameters, fraction gaps, hand-calibrated in the spirit of OpenType MATH (CM's TFM-era metrics must be reconstructed for our sfnt parsing); (c) the extensible-delimiter strategy — CM extension-glyph assembly vs drawn-path construction vs hybrid (OQ-2), with drawn paths as the universal fallback so NO requested size can fail.

Depends on fmd-font being far enough along to decode CM glyph outlines (the fmd-font factoring task) — coordinate cross-repo via the upstream ledger.

Acceptance: rendered output paths for all spike constructs, visually reviewed against LaTeX renders of the same input; a written architecture decision resolving OQ-2; the fmd-math public-API sketch frozen at spike shape until G2 (R8 pivot rule); explicit go/no-go on the Appendix-G parameter approach.
close_reason: G0-3 ratified (docs/g0/G0-3-fmd-math-ratification.md). spikes/g0-3-fmd-math: parser with spans + precise named unsupported-errors (the ratchet shape), the eight atom classes + full inter-atom spacing table with Bin degradation + script suppression, exact D/T/S/SS style propagation with cramping, and the Appendix-G constructions (rule-15 fractions, rule-18 scripts incl. 4-theta clearance + 4/5-x-height lift, rule-11 radicals with indices, rule-19 left/right, rules 13/13a big-op limits, vcentered matrix). 18 tests green; visual gallery committed (docs/g0/g0-3-renders) and reviewed. Verdicts: Appendix-G approach GO (published TFM fontdimens validated against fmd-font-decoded CM geometry: x-height +0.13%, axis exact); OQ-2 resolved by ADR-0005 (drawn-path mainline: natural -> <=1.25x scale -> parametric drawn; assembly rejected, CM Unicode ships no extension repertoire); multi-face layout structural (big ops resolve via Noto). API sketch frozen until G2 (R8). 568 workspace tests green. UBS criticals adjudicated false positives (test-module panics; 'token' name heuristic).

title: Reconcile the Behavior Note register with plan §16.8
description:
DOCUMENTATION DEFECT, found while drafting BN-08 for fm-y69. The plan's §16.8 register and the files in docs/behavior_notes/ disagree about two numbers, and the files disagree with each other.

§16.8 seeds the register as: BN-01 single RNG, BN-02 rational clock, BN-03 true arc length, BN-04 color, BN-05 native typesetting, BN-06 renderer, BN-07 Reference bugs fixed (Appendix C rulings), BN-08 de-TeX'd classes (§11.6), BN-09 one arc-density rule, BN-11 composition timing.

On disk:
  BN-07-stroke-uniform-fixes.md      } TWO files share BN-07. Both are
  BN-07-updater-and-group-fixes.md   } plausibly "Reference bugs fixed",
                                       which is one register entry.
  BN-08-animation-contract.md          Occupies BN-08, which §16.8 assigns
                                       to the de-TeX'd classes. The
                                       animation contract is not in the
                                       §16.8 seed list at all.
  BN-10-skip-mode-updater-time.md      Also not in the §16.8 seed list;
                                       BN-10 is unassigned there, so this
                                       one is an addition rather than a
                                       collision.
  (no BN-06)                           The renderer note is unwritten.

fm-y69 wrote BN-08-de-texed-natives.md per the plan (which is normative — GOVERNANCE.md: "Where they seem to disagree, the plan wins and this file gets fixed"), so BN-08 now has two files. That was the deliberate lesser evil: renumbering someone else's published note is a documentation act with its own review, and RULE 1 forbids deleting files without permission.

What this bead has to decide and record:
1. Whether BN-07's two files merge into one note or the register grows an entry to cover the second.
2. Which number the animation contract takes (it is real content, just not where §16.8 put it).
3. Whether §16.8's seed list is amended to include the notes that grew beyond it (BN-10, the animation contract) — an ADR if it amends the plan, which it likely does.
4. Whether BN-06 (renderer) stays reserved for W5 or is renumbered.

Then rename the files to match, in one commit, with the plan trued up in the same commit per GOVERNANCE §3's true-up rule. ASK THE PROGRAM OWNER BEFORE DELETING OR RENAMING ANY EXISTING NOTE — these are published, user-facing migration guidance and the register is cited from the README.

Acceptance: one file per register entry; the register in §16.8 matches the directory exactly; a test or check script asserting that (the ratchet's pin-coupling test is the pattern — an always-on assertion that the documented set and the on-disk set agree costs little and stops this recurring).
close_reason:
Reconciled. The register is now an authoritative index with numbering rules, §16.8 is trued up, and the one genuine collision is gone.

WHAT THE INVESTIGATION FOUND, which changed two of the four answers this bead posed:

1. THE TWO BN-07 FILES ARE NOT A COLLISION. §16.8 defines BN-07 as "Reference bugs fixed (Appendix C rulings)" — one register entry over a topic, and Appendix C carries eleven rulings owned by different workstreams. BN-07-stroke-uniform-fixes covers C-2/C-7 (W3, uniform inventory); BN-07-updater-and-group-fixes covers C-5/C-6 (W3, dynamic behaviour). Forcing them into one document would mean every workstream that touches Appendix C rewrites the same file. Ruled a FAMILY and blessed as such (ADR-0009 rule 2). No files touched.

2. THE BN-08 COLLISION WAS REAL AND CLEAN TO FIX. Grep first, rename second: NOTHING outside BN-08-animation-contract.md cited its number. Every BN-08 in docs/api/ledger.tsv (3 cells), API_OVERLAY.tsv (3 rows) and crates/** (brace.rs, matchers.rs, fmn-library/lib.rs) points at the de-TeX'd natives. So the rename cost one heading and one filename, and required no ledger regeneration and no code edit. BN-08-animation-contract.md -> BN-12-animation-contract.md, with a dated renumbering callout in the file. The de-TeX'd note keeps BN-08, matching the normative §16.8 line; renumbering IT instead would have contradicted the plan to preserve a number nobody referenced.

3. BN-10 AND THE ANIMATION CONTRACT GROWING PAST THE SEED LIST IS CORRECT BEHAVIOUR, not drift. A workstream that finds a deliberate divergence should write it a note rather than file it nowhere. The defect was that no rule said so, which is what let all of this happen quietly.

4. BN-06 STAYS RESERVED for the renderer (W5). Filling a reserved slot with unrelated content is how registers rot; an empty row states "the renderer's note is a W5 deliverable" more usefully than silence.

LANDED: docs/behavior_notes/README.md — the authoritative register, twelve rows, with the four numbering rules (one number per note, never reused, never renumbered once cited; a number may name a family where the plan's own entry does; reserved numbers stay reserved; Draft -> Final on gate passage) and the regeneration command for the ledger's evidence cells. ADR-0009 records the ruling and the rename authorization. Plan §16.8 amended IN THE SAME COMMIT per GOVERNANCE §3 — its prose now points at the register index and keeps the seed list as the register's first rows, so a future note needs no plan edit and no ADR.

AUTHORIZATION FOR THE RENAME (AGENTS.md RULE 1 + the irreversible-actions protocol): the program owner was asked, given three options, and selected "Rename to BN-12" explicitly. Command: `git mv docs/behavior_notes/BN-08-animation-contract.md docs/behavior_notes/BN-12-animation-contract.md`, executed 2026-07-25T16:18:01Z. No other file was moved or deleted.

GATES: scripts/check.sh green (937 tests). No dangling BN references — verified by grep across crates/, docs/api/ and API_OVERLAY.tsv after the rename.

title: W5: The ImageTable and the image revision axis — blocked on an image mobject existing
description:
§10.8 lists ImageTable among the IR's tables and 'image' among the seven revision axes. Neither has a producer in the tree: there is no ImageMobject, and nothing writes raster content to a renderable.

fm-gw7 therefore built the axis (fmn_render::revision::Axis::Image) and left it as an INPUT — Revisions::with_image(rev) — rather than deriving a plausible zero from a Stage that cannot know. G0-8's report assessed the device side: an ImageTable needs MTLTexture and a sampler, which the frankentorch gateway does not expose, so it is 'a genuine upstream extension, not a layout question'.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS: the ImageTable itself (descriptor rows: extent, format, colour space, sampler state, content digest), the image revision's producer, and interning by content digest through fmn-cache — the same mechanism ShapeTable already uses for outlines, which is why this is small once there is something to put in it.

BLOCKED ON: an image mobject (§12's ImageMobject / the Reference's ImageMobject + Texture path). File the dependency when that bead exists.

ALSO NEEDED FOR THE ANNEX: the ft gateway must grow texture + sampler support before the annex can sample one (G0-8 §5). That is an upstream ledger item, not this bead.

title: W5: Bound perspective vector strokes without viewport-wide tile fanout
description: Replace ThreeDJob's fail-closed full-viewport bounds for every visible perspective stroke with a conservative analytic or rational-slab bound for the projected offset field. The result must never clip legal flat or camera-facing stroke fragments, including asymmetric perspective widths, variable width, joins, caps, user-plane cuts, and curves approaching the near plane. Preserve painter order and certified pixels exactly; this is work elimination only. Acceptance: (1) adversarial containment tests compare derived bounds against dense/brute-force legal fragments for flat and billboard strokes, joins/caps, variable widths, and near-plane cases; (2) cold renders before/after are byte-identical across the vector corpus and threads {1,4,16}; (3) a tile-work counter proves a small perspective stroke no longer touches every viewport tile; (4) no sampled-only maximum is accepted without an error bound or fail-closed fallback; (5) scripts/check.sh and UBS are green. Follow-up discovered while closing fm-diu.

title: Execute the one-time Reference imagery capture on a GL-capable machine
description: Run scripts/capture_reference_imagery.py (landed with fm-xb3) on a machine with the Reference's full GL import closure (moderngl + OpenGL context or EGL/OSMesa headless + manimpango). The harness renders the six-scene G0-2 calibration set (gradient fills, self-intersecting star, all joint types, glow, 3D lighting, Pango text) and writes gallery/reference_captures/*.png + PROVENANCE.json (python/GL/package identity, Reference commit, per-image sha256). Then update the two tables in docs/look_gallery/CAPTURE_INVENTORY.md (statuses to 'captured', capture machine + date) and commit — the PNG bytes stay out of git per the §15.3 fixture policy. Capture ONCE; the environment is recorded, never maintained (D-16). Blocks fm-k77 (the G0-2 look study needs the captured imagery). Note: the scene definitions may need small adjustments against the real Reference API at capture time — they are written but could not be executed in the dev environment (no GL).
close_reason:
Captured on sensedemobox 2026-07-25. All six G0-2 calibration stills + PROVENANCE.json are in gallery/reference_captures/ (gitignored per §15.3); the committed record is docs/look_gallery/CAPTURE_INVENTORY.md. fm-k77 is unblocked.

THE PREMISE WAS WRONG, IN OUR FAVOUR. The bead and the inventory both said the dev environment cannot do this ('requires a real OpenGL context'). It can: Mesa llvmpipe gives a conformant GL 4.5 core profile with no GPU, and Xvfb satisfies both the Reference's pyglet shadow window and moderngl's default backend in one step. No second machine was needed. The exact recipe is recorded in the script docstring. This is consistent with D-16 rather than a stretch of it — the inventory's own doctrine names llvmpipe ('no certified Pango/llvmpipe environment in CI, ever'), and these captures are never compared bit-for-bit; the Reference draws through its own GLSL, so a conformant GL implementation reproduces its look and software rasterization costs only speed.

TWO HARNESS DEFECTS THE CAPTURE EXPOSED, both fixed before the set was accepted:

1. THE BLANK-CAPTURE BUG — the serious one. The harness called scene.camera.get_image(), which only READS the framebuffer; nothing ever drew into it. The first run produced six byte-identical fully-transparent 1920x1080 PNGs and reported six successful captures. Every surface signal was healthy: valid PNGs, right size, right format, no error, exit 0. The only tell was that all six sha256s matched. Fixed by the explicit draw (scene.update_frame(force_draw=True) then scene.get_image()), and — more importantly — made unrepresentable by a new check_liveness() that refuses to publish a set in which any frame is a single flat color or any two frames are pixel-identical, with the whole set now written all-or-nothing per the docstring's stated contract. Both guards are verified to fire (exit 2) and to pass a healthy set. Left unguarded, this would have calibrated G0-2 — the spike that fixes Lumen's aesthetic constants — against six blank images, and nothing downstream would have noticed.

2. joints_and_caps WAS CLIPPED. Four 2.4-unit rows overflowed the 8-unit frame, cutting 'auto' and 'no_joint' off-screen in the one scene whose purpose is showing every joint type. The stack is now fitted to frame height; all four types and labels are visible and visibly different (the no_joint notch, the miter point).

Also fixed a pre-existing unbounded subprocess (ubs warning) in ref_commit(). Gates: ubs exit 0, ruff check + format clean, capture re-runs to identical hashes.

WHAT THE IMAGERY ALREADY SHOWS: self_intersections renders the star's overlap core LIGHTER than its limbs — the Reference's signed-alpha additive fill artifact, exactly the mechanism Appendix B replaces with honest nonzero-winding coverage. fm-k77's side-by-side has its first concrete 'at-least-as-good' claim waiting for it.

title: GATE G1 — Core 2D: the engine end-to-end without text
description:
Convergence gate G1 (plan §20.3) — an integration CHECKPOINT, not a scope reduction. Criteria, verbatim from the plan and mechanically checkable:

(1) Path-invariant + kernel fixtures green (W2's QuadPath, converter, arclength). (2) Core Mobject/VMobject functionality (W3's arena, RecordBuffer, family, ordering, updaters). (3) Transform family, partial reveals, fades, updaters, trackers running on the rational clock (W4). (4) The analytic renderer with G0-2's look-study calibration applied (W5 fill/strokes/adaptive-AA/certified engine). (5) THE PRIMITIVE CORPUS: ~25 scenes, OURS, public, bit-locked as self-goldens, THREAD-COUNT-INVARIANT ({1,4,16} per PG-5's per-commit sweep), and Look-Gallery-approved against Reference imagery. (6) Native PNG/y4m output (no ffmpeg needed to pass this gate).

The gate closes when every dependency bead is closed AND a gate-review session records: self-golden lock state, the Gallery verdict sheet for the primitive corpus, and the thread-sweep evidence. If the Gallery verdict includes any 'regression' entries, the gate stays open (R2: look regressions block the gate that introduced them).

title: GATE G3 — Depth & Motion: 3D, interactivity, the Studio, the annex preview
description:
Convergence gate G3 (plan §20.3). Criteria:

(1) 3D surfaces with the KEPT lighting model; CameraFrame on the fixed Rotation conventions; depth, transparency, clip planes (W53D). (2) Dot clouds, images, textures (W53D/W73D + codecs). (3) Vector fields + StreamLines on the tuned integrator (W73D). (4) Events + InteractiveScene (W9EVENTS). (5) The Studio baseline: supervisor/worker, PNG stream, scrubbing, TUI (W9SUPER/W9STUDIO). (6) THE ANNEX SERVING STUDIO PREVIEW on supported Apple-silicon hardware (W5METAL) — with the DECLARED FALLBACK ruled in Rev 4 (OQ-12): if the annex misses, G3 passes on CPU preview meeting PG-3, and the annex requirement moves to G5 with a public note. Core gates stay CPU-only either way, so acceleration can never mask a core miss (R21). (7) PG-3 (throughput) blocking; PG-A active for annex changes.

title: W5/W3: carry primitive hints through shape-preserving transforms
description: Today any point write demotes an entry's ShapeTag hint to General (crates/fmn-mobject/src/shape.rs) — conservative and never wrong, but a shifted Circle loses its arc kernel, and shift/move_to/next_to are the commonest operations in every scene. Make the shape-preserving positional ops (shift, scale_about with a uniform factor, rotate about z for tags that are rotation-invariant, move_to/center/align_to/next_to which are shifts underneath) transform the tag's geometric payload and re-stamp its point revision instead of letting it stale. Non-preserving ops (stretch, apply_points_function, match_points, alignment, raw writes, live views) must keep demoting. Acceptance: a per-op table test asserting preserved vs demoted for every positional method; a property test that a preserved tag still describes the points (rebuild from the tag, compare at f32 tolerance); the existing fm-oab hint tests stay green.

title: W7: The geometry lineage — Arc/Line/Arrow/polygon families under one arc-density rule
description:
Implement the geometry classes of Appendix A (§12.1): the Arc lineage (Arc, ArcBetweenPoints, CurvedArrow/CurvedDoubleArrow, Circle, Dot/SmallDot, Ellipse, AnnularSector, Sector, Annulus) under ONE clean arc-density rule — the Reference has THREE mutually inconsistent conventions for how many curves an arc of given angle gets; ours is one documented rule (Behavior Note BN-09, drafted in W2PATH, applied here); the Line lineage (Line, DashedLine, TangentLine, Elbow, Arrow, StrokeArrow, Vector) with the TIP-ATTACHMENT ALGEBRA placing by TRUE arc length (W2ARC — tips sit at the actual end of the actual curve, dashes distribute by true length); CubicBezier (through W2CUBIC's converter); Polygon/Polyline/RegularPolygon/Triangle; ArrowTip; Rectangle/Square/RoundedRectangle; TipableVMobject as the shared tip machinery.

Compatibility method: constructors are LOCKED BY STRUCTURAL FIXTURES against the Reference where formulas intentionally coincide — point counts, layouts, dimensions (loose f32 per §16.4) — generated from the pinned Reference by the W1GAUNT extraction scripts. Where our rule deliberately differs (arc density, true-length dash placement), fixtures assert OUR documented behavior and the Behavior Note covers migration.

Primitive hints (§10.8): these constructors are exactly the shapes Lumen's hint system fast-paths — Circle/Arc/Rectangle/Dot constructors must tag their paths with the semantic hint so W5IR routes them off the general solver (and mutation clears the tag, tested).

Acceptance: structural fixture corpus green across the lineage; tip-placement tests on curved paths (true-length positions); dash-distribution tests; hint-tagging tests per constructor; BN-09 finalized with examples.
close_reason: The geometry lineage landed in fmn-library (§12.1), which was an empty crate at the start of this bead. THREE COMMITS: b1168d6 (the Marionette surface it needed), a964631 (the lineage), 2aa86a7 (the fixture corpus). SHAPE TAGS (§10.8): fmn-mobject/src/shape.rs — ShapeTag is durable class config AND a geometric payload, kept apart: Stage::shape always readable (Line's path_arc outlives transforms, as the Reference's does), Stage::primitive_hint returns the tag only while the point-field revision still matches, so EVERY write channel demotes the hint by construction (positional op, raw buffer write, live view, set_points — all four tested). Copies re-stamp against the cloned buffer and a stale tag copies as stale; snapshot/restore round-trip; the snapshot format carries it at schema minor 1.1 with an unknown discriminant a typed refusal. Mobject grew uniforms+shape so builders can set them before entering the arena. positional.rs grew get_points/set_points (order-preserving, joint angles refreshed)/get_start_and_end/put_start_and_end_on, with the Reference's closed-loop raise as StageError::DegenerateEndpoints. LIBRARY: VMobject (the detached builder + the transform helpers the Reference's constructors use) + Style/VStyle (the colour surface as record data, color-sets-both and colour/opacity-independent kept) + VGroup/VectorizedPoint/CurvesAsSubmobjects/DashedVMobject/VHighlight + Arc/ArcBetweenPoints/CurvedArrow/CurvedDoubleArrow/Circle/Dot/SmallDot/Ellipse/AnnularSector/Sector/Annulus + Line/DashedLine/TangentLine/Elbow/Arrow/StrokeArrow/Vector + CubicBezier/Polygon/Polyline/RegularPolygon/Triangle/ArrowTip/Rectangle/Square/RoundedRectangle + ScreenRectangle/FullScreenRectangle/FullScreenFadeRectangle. BN-09 FINAL: one density rule everywhere, with a worked-example table showing the common counts are unchanged (Circle 33 points, quarter Arc 9) and only the self-inconsistent Reference paths move. BN-03 CONSUMED: tips place by the TRUE tangent and the shaft is trimmed by TRUE LENGTH rather than rescaled toward its chord (a trimmed arc keeps its curvature — tested); Line buffers, DashedLine spacing, and TangentLine proportions all measure along the curve; C-3 closed (get_arc_length is the arc length for every path_arc, not only positive). FIXTURES: 30 cases from the Reference's formulas at 1e-9, plus density-rule and shared-anchor-invariant sweeps over the same corpus. BUG FOUND AND FIXED IN fmn-geom: the closed-form quadratic arc length returned exactly ZERO for a near-straight curve (handle at the midpoint to within rounding — what scaling a short segment up produces, e.g. TangentLine); the general antiderivative's two ~1e16 terms cancelled completely. Now the near-straight case is detected relatively and integrated in a factored form that cancels the small divisor symbolically, with branch and continuity regression tests. GATES: scripts/check.sh green (fmt, check, clippy -D warnings, test, crate-DAG); fmn-library 63 tests, fmn-mobject 12 binaries, fmn-geom 106; ubs 0 criticals on library sources (the one critical is a panic! inside a #[cfg(test)] assertion, the accepted stance from fm-6h6/fm-jru).
