title: W5: Strokes — true curve-distance, round caps, principled joins, arclength width
description:
Implement the stroke rasterizer (§10.3): exact/high-accuracy signed distance to the quadratic within conservative slabs (slabs retained per compiled path, W5IR); ROUND CAPS on open ends (the Reference's butt caps were a ribbon-pipeline artifact; round is the deliberate choice, Behavior-Noted with BN-06); round/bevel/miter joins with a real miter limit plus the smooth "auto" join tuned in G0-2's look study; width and color interpolated by ARC LENGTH (via the shared LUT), not parameter space — a stroke whose width varies does so uniformly along the curve, as the eye expects; flat_stroke vs camera-facing 3D stroke construction both supported (the uniform flows from W3FAMILY's inventory); the smoothstep AA profile at the calibrated ~1.5px weight.

Every one of these is visibly better than the ≤32-segment polyline ribbons it replaces — which is the point (§1.5 ↷). The quality bar is judged in the Look Gallery against Reference imagery: same feel, cleaner.

Numerical care: distance-to-quadratic is a cubic root-find — use the stable closed-form/iterative hybrid with the degenerate cases (colinear control points, cusp-adjacent) routed to the precision-exception path (§6.1); certified mode runs the canonical arithmetic (W5CERT decides representation per G0-6).

Performance shape: stroke SDF + AA resolve is the dominant cost of typical 2D scenes (per the plan's annex ROI ranking) — structure the kernel for the SIMD hot list (§17.3: stroke-SDF slabs are named) and for the annex offload (G0-8 proved this exact stage on Metal). Scalar-complete first; the structure must not preclude lanes.

Acceptance: distance-accuracy oracle tests vs brute-force sampling; cap/join golden fixtures (every combination, including miter-limit escapes to bevel); arclength-width metamorphic test (reparameterized curve ⇒ identical stroke); degenerate-case corpus; Look Gallery review of the stroke calibration set.
close_reason:
DONE. §10.3's strokes are landed in crates/fmn-render/src/stroke.rs (~380 lines + 18 inline tests), on the nearest-point primitive this bead's own work put in Chisel (crates/fmn-geom/src/distance.rs, landed under fm-5oi).

THE STAGE IS ONE EXPRESSION: the signed excess min over segments of (distance − half_width(s)), through G0-2's measured AA profile. Three of the four deliverables fall out of it rather than being built:
- ROUND CAPS. The distance to an open end is radial, so the level set is a semicircle with nobody asking for one. Asserted by sweeping twelve directions at the half-width and requiring equal coverage in each — a butt cap reads zero immediately past the endpoint.
- ROUND JOINS. Two segments sharing an anchor contribute two fields whose minimum IS a round join. G0-2 L6's finding, now asserted rather than quoted: sweeping the join arc at the half-width, every sample sits exactly on the silhouette (so it is a circular arc, not a mitre or a cut), and one pixel inside there is no gap.
- WIDTH AND COLOUR BY ARC LENGTH, over the shared §7.3 layer. The excess is formed PER SEGMENT before the minimum, which makes a variable-width stroke a union of variable-radius tubes rather than one tube of averaged radius. That ordering is the whole reason §10.3's metamorphic law holds: a de Casteljau split of every curve — same curve, different point array, different parameterization — moves the stroke by < 1e-6 on a steep 100→800 width ramp. Computing min(distance) first and looking up a width afterwards would use one segment's width at another segment's nearest point, and there is a test that pins the silhouette at three arc positions to catch that.

THE JOINS (ADR-0012, resolving what G0-2 L6 explicitly left to this bead). The Reference's constants are SWAPPED relative to its own shader: BEVEL_JOINT sets miter_factor=0, i.e. shift = -tan(θ/2), the POINTED corner, and MITER_JOINT sets +cot(θ/2), the blunt one — corroborated independently by the captured apex widths (auto 4 px, bevel 6 px, miter 9 px, with miter visibly blunter). Ruling:
- Auto and NoJoint render the round join. NoJoint's notch is a ribbon artifact and D-05 grants no obligation to reproduce one; a distance field cannot carve a gap unless told to, and it is not told.
- Bevel cuts flat, Miter comes to a point. OUR NAMES MEAN WHAT THEY DRAW. Numeric codes still load unchanged (source compatibility), but propagating a misnamed constant into a second engine forever is not compatibility. BN-06-strokes.md carries the migration guidance: a scene that set joint_type explicitly and wants the Reference's corner swaps the two.
- MITER_LIMIT = sqrt(10) ≈ 3.1623 half-widths of miter length — L6's measured de facto value, since there is no miter_limit constant in the Reference to copy — past which a miter falls back to a bevel. Derived two ways in the test (1/sin(psi/2) with cos psi = 0.8, and the shader's own tan(71.565°)=3 route) and cross-checked against the wedge's own miter_ratio at the crossover angle.
- The overrides are EDITS to the round corner, confined to the wedge whose nearest path point is the anchor: a bevel's region is a subset, so it trims (max with the chord's half-plane); a miter's contains it near the tip, so it extends (min with the two offset half-planes). The consequence is structural rather than careful — join_wedges returns NOTHING for the round settings, so the round path is bit-identical whether the join machinery exists or not, asserted pixel-for-pixel, as is 'no joint setting changes the stroke's body'.
- Closed subpaths get their wrap corner (a closed triangle has three joins, not two), tangential joins get none (no wedge, and an ill-defined bisector if one were built), and joins form only within a subpath.

THE SLABS. §10.3 says 'within conservative slabs', and the finding is that there should be no slab TABLE: the IR already retains what a slab is made of (the control-polygon hull contains the curve), and the width-dependent expansion must not be retained because width is a STYLE property — two occurrences of one interned outline can carry different widths, so a retained slab would be invalidated by a restyle, exactly the coupling §10.8's revision axes exist to avoid. segment_slab computes it per draw from retained data; containment is verified by sweeping a window larger than the slab and requiring every covered pixel to be inside it.

CONSOLIDATION. aa_coverage and width_px now exist ONCE. §10.2's border_coverage and border_width_px delegate to them, because the Reference feeds fill_border_width into the stroke_width attribute — it is the same conversion and the same profile, not similar ones.

TWO TEST-ARITHMETIC CORRECTIONS, recorded because both looked like code failures: the join probes first ran at a 3 px half-width, where the bevel chord (0.707 hw), the round arc (1.0 hw) and the miter tip (1.414 hw) all sit inside the 1.5 px AA band, so every probe read a blend of two joins — they run at 10 px now, where the three silhouettes are further apart than the band. And the miter limit's predicted value used the TANGENT angle where the classical formula wants the INTERIOR angle: the Reference's cos_angle = -0.8 crossover means cos psi = +0.8, so 1/sin(psi/2) = sqrt(10) and not 1.054.

ACCEPTANCE: distance-accuracy oracle vs brute-force sampling — done in fmn-geom (20,001 samples over a corpus with a straight segment, a cusp, a near-straight and an out-of-plane curve, x 9 query points; the closed form is never worse). Arclength-width metamorphic test — done. Degenerate-case corpus — done (no segments, degenerate map, zero width drawing nothing rather than an AA hairline, a cusp whose distance roots collide). Cap/join combinations including the miter-limit escape — the GEOMETRY of every one is tested.

TWO ITEMS DELIBERATELY CARVED OUT AND RECORDED ON fm-ig3 RATHER THAN LEFT OPEN HERE:
(a) 'cap/join GOLDEN fixtures'. A bit-locked golden is a rasterized frame and there is no engine to rasterize one; the same is true of §10.2's fill corpus. Wiring both into fmn-conformance's golden rig is fm-ig3's, and it is written on that bead.
(b) 'Look Gallery review of the stroke calibration set'. Human review. The panel already exists (gallery/reference_captures/joints_and_caps.png, and G0-2's committed fmn-joints-and-caps.png) and now has three distinct rows to judge instead of four identical ones.

ONE DEFERRAL, recorded on fm-0gy: flat_stroke vs camera-facing are the SAME construction under the affine ScreenMap — a width in the object plane and one in screen pixels differ by exactly the scale — and diverge only once geometry leaves the view plane, which needs §10.4's camera. The uniform is read and honoured trivially today rather than half-implemented against a projection nobody has written.

STRUCTURE FOR LATER STAGES: stroke_coverage is per-pixel independent with no accumulator and no scan — the one-thread-per-pixel shape G0-8 proved on Metal — so §10.3's 'scalar-complete first; the structure must not preclude lanes' is honoured. Everything transcendental funnels through fmn-dmath.

GATES: 1,102 tests pass (147 in fmn-render, 72 in fmn-geom), cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings, crate-DAG check, ubs 0 critical. Plan §10.3 trued up and ADR-0012 + BN-06-strokes.md landed in the same commit; the Behavior Note register's last reserved slot is discharged.

comments.text:
FROM fm-5oi (2026-07-26) — YOUR DISTANCE PRIMITIVE IS ALREADY LANDED. crates/fmn-geom/src/distance.rs: nearest_on_quadratic(a0,h,a1,p) -> Nearest{t, point, distance}, distance_to_quadratic, and solve_cubic_real. It is in Chisel rather than in the renderer because D4 puts the geometry kernel there and because two consumers need the same answer — this bead's strokes and §10.2's fill_border_width. Consume it; do not write a second root-find.

What it already handles, with tests: the straight segment (C=0, so the cubic degenerates to linear), the cusp (handle beyond an endpoint, two roots colliding), the near-straight (the case an absolute epsilon gets wrong — the degeneracy test is relative to the polynomial's own scale), out-of-plane curves, and queries beyond either end (both endpoints are always candidates, because no interior root reports one). Brute-force validated at 20,001 samples over that corpus x 9 query points: the closed form is never worse.

Two things it does deliberately that you should not 'fix': the trigonometric branch clamps its acos argument (rounding pushes it outside [-1,1] exactly when the discriminant is near zero, which turns a triple root into NaN), and root polish is a FIXED three Newton steps rather than convergence-tested, because a loop that stops when it has converged stops at a different iteration on a different platform and §6.6 exists to prevent that. cbrt/acos/cos all route through fmn-geom's scalar funnel to fmn-dmath.

What it does NOT give you and you still own: signed distance (this is unsigned — the inside/outside test is yours), the conservative slabs W5IR retains, caps, joins, the miter limit, and the arc-length width/colour ramp. Note also that §10.2's fill already consumes the shared arc-length inversion via the new fmn_geom::arclength::t_at_arc_fraction (curve_and_t_at's inner solve, extracted) — use that for the width ramp rather than a private inversion.

Also relevant: G0-2's finding L6 says bevel and miter are named BACKWARDS relative to their geometry in the Reference, and that 'auto' has an implied miter limit of 3.1623 with no miter_limit constant to copy. That is in docs/g0/G0-2-look-study-ratification.md, not in the plan.

title: W5: WASM tier 2 — the serialized-timeline player (implementation)
description:
Implement the tier-2 WASM deliverable (§10.7, §13.5's browser endgame substrate, G5 criterion): the SERIALIZED-TIMELINE PLAYER — a browser artifact that consumes W4TIMELINE's canonical serialized format (keyframes, labels, segment boundaries, engine version) and plays it: decode → reconstruct compiled render state → render frames on the tier-1 renderer (W5WASM) → present to canvas, with scrub/seek via the Timeline's seek semantics (pure segments reconstruct from snapshot + alpha; the serialized form carries the snapshots/checkpoints it needs — define exactly what a self-contained timeline bundle includes: geometry snapshots, typeset paths (pre-typeset — fmd-math need not run in the player for tier 2), styles, camera tracks, audio track reference).

Design decisions to make and record: (a) the TIMELINE BUNDLE format — self-contained (embedded assets/snapshots) vs referencing (player fetches) — lean self-contained per the sovereignty doctrine; (b) version policy per §6.7 (the player REFUSES engine-version mismatches cleanly — W11WASM's packaging test depends on this); (c) what tier 2 does NOT include, stated honestly: no scene construction, no Python, no live typesetting — it is a PLAYER (the browser Studio's live-render endgame remains W9STUDIO's WASM direction at G5, distinct from this bead).

Feeds: W11WASM packages this artifact; W9STUDIO's share/export story ("export an interactive player bundle of this scene") is the user-facing payoff.

Acceptance: a corpus scene exported as a timeline bundle plays in a headless browser test bit-consistently (same bundle ⇒ same frame hashes, single-threaded); scrub/seek correctness vs the native engine's frames on pure segments; version-mismatch refusal test; bundle-size measurement recorded (R19); the bundle format documented in the §6.7 versioned-schema registry.
notes: fm-hfe landed the schedule half: TimelinePlan (FMNA/5) carries fps, per-segment kind/run_time/frame range, and labels, and content-addresses. What tier 2 still owes: per-frame CONTENT so a browser player replays with no scene code in the process — either serialized geometry keyframes or animation reconstruction off the fm-vn6 API schema. Timeline::seek's pure O(1) path (reconstruct_pure_frame) is the model for in-browser scrubbing.

title: G0-4: Corpus harvest — the TeX-string multiset from 3b1b/videos + Reference constructors
description:
Executed data-gathering task defining fmd-math's tier-1 scope empirically (§20.1 spike 4 → §11.5). With no LaTeX fallback, coverage discipline replaces fallback discipline: tier 1 must be scoped by MEASURED occurrence, not aspiration (R1 mitigation).

Scope: extract the TeX-string multiset from (a) the pinned 3b1b/videos tree and (b) the Reference's own constructors (Tex-backed classes, preset strings) — static extraction (regex/AST over the Python sources for Tex/TexText call sites and string constants) plus a one-time instrumented run where feasible. title: G0-8 follow-on: analytic-fill GPU mapping spike, before W5 commits to a fill layout
description:
G0-8 (fm-ekx) proved the stroke-SDF + AA-resolve stage maps onto Metal cleanly and produced the IR->GPU mapping report (docs/g0/G0-8-accelerator-ratification.md). Section 5 of that report names what the spike did NOT exercise, with an assessment. The one item that needs its own spike BEFORE fm-gw7 freezes a layout is the analytic fill (§10.2).

WHY IT IS DIFFERENT FROM STROKES: the stroke stage is per-pixel independent, which is why it mapped to one-thread-per-pixel with no synchronisation and no atomics. The fill is per-SCANLINE: y-monotone quadratic splits, exact segment intersections from the closed-form root, and SIGNED TRAPEZOIDAL AREA ACCUMULATION per cell. An accumulation whose ordering matters is exactly the shape that does not fall out of the stroke kernel's structure.

ASSESSED (not proven) in the G0-8 report: tractable, because the accumulation is per-tile and the tile is already a threadgroup, so the natural form is a threadgroup-local scanline reduction rather than a global one. Prove or refute that.

SCOPE: extend spikes/g0-8-accelerator with a fill stage over the same prototype IR — reuse RenderIr, the CSR command lists, the flat single-typed FlatIr derivation, and cpu::Precision::AnnexF32 so the arithmetic floor is measurable without a GPU exactly as it is for strokes. Deliver the same three-row equivalence table (CPU-f32 floor / Metal safe / Metal fast) and the same table-by-table layout verdicts.

CARRY FORWARD FROM G0-8, ALL STILL BINDING: one scalar type per buffer (F1); deterministic host-side count/prefix/scatter binning, never atomic appends (F2); precompute anything branchy and revision-keyed onto the host (F3); threadgroup sizes from pipeline introspection (F4); MathMode::Safe, because Metal's default fast math doubled rms error on the stroke stage (F9); and F10's warning that f32 conditioning is the real risk, not the GPU.

ALSO WORTH SETTLING HERE: occlusion pruning, which is a host-side mask over painter order and only pays where fills are (G0-8 §5 deliberately left it with this bead rather than assessing it against a stroke-only scene).

Annex constraints survive regardless of outcome: standard-mode only, never certified (D-18); excluded from core gates; PG-A only; frankentorch the only gateway.

ACCEPTANCE: a Metal-rendered filled frame from the prototype IR; the equivalence table; the layout verdicts fed into fm-gw7; go/defer on whether fills join the annex's first production duty or stay CPU-only for G3's preview.
close_reason: G0-8b ratified: §10.2's analytic fill maps onto Metal in two dispatch shapes, neither needing an atomic, a barrier, or threadgroup memory — G0-8's threadgroup-local-reduction hypothesis refuted in the favourable direction. Both land at the f32 arithmetic floor (max delta-8bit = 1, vs the stroke stage's 152) and are byte-identical to each other after 8-bit encoding. Verdict GO for fills in the annex's first production duty; recommended shape is per-pixel, on structure (F17: the dispatch shapes are not distinguishable on speed — a ~1.1 ms allocate+clear+readback floor dominates a 1.3-2.2 ms preview frame). Findings F11-F17 in docs/g0/G0-8b-analytic-fill-ratification.md; occlusion pruning implemented and measured (16.5% of commands removed, frames byte-identical). Plan §10.2/§10.8 trued up in the same commit.

title: W7: The Scribe bridge — TextLayout/Typeset to VMobject
description:
The seam nothing in fmn-library has crossed yet: fmn-text and fmn-tex are declared dependencies of fmn-library and are NOT used anywhere in its src/. There is no Text, MarkupText, Tex, or TexText mobject class in the workspace. fm-7dw's close note put this here on purpose: "Geometry/Stage wiring stays in the library tier per §19 (fmn-tex cannot name fmn-geom; fm-inr/fm-y69 build VMobjects from Typeset)."

Split out of fm-y69 on 2026-07-25 because it is the shared blocker of several beads, not a private detail of one. fm-y69's text-backed half needs it; so do fm-v4l (axis labels and tick numbers are native text), fm-3kr (the drawings shelf's former Tex members), and the whole G2 gate.

TWO MODULES.

(1) TEXT to VMOBJECT. fmn_text::layout_text(&FontBook, &TextRequest) -> TextLayout gives positioned glyphs; fmn_text::glyph_quadpath(&FontBook, &PlacedTextGlyph) -> QuadPath gives each glyph's outline already scaled and translated. The bridge builds one VMobject child per glyph and preserves the SUBMOBJECT-INDEX CONTRACT — TextLayout::submobject_slice(a, b) is the Text[a:b] surface and TextLayout::select(range) is the isolate= surface, and both must survive into the mobject family or every t2c/isolate scene silently breaks. Reference default style for text mobjects is stroke_width=0, fill_opacity=1.0, fill_border_width=0.5.

(2) MATH to VMOBJECT. Harder, and the design decision is real. fmn_tex::Typeset carries layout: fmd_math::Layout (glyphs, rules, paths) plus subs: Vec<Sub> — the span map. Three obstacles:
  - Typeset.layout.glyphs[i].face is an fmd_math::FaceId into fmd_math::FaceSet, a DIFFERENT face identity from fmn_text::FaceSel, so fmn_text::glyph_quadpath cannot render math glyphs.
  - fmd_math::paths::resolve_paths(engine, layout) resolves everything into flat contours but FLATTENS the submobject structure, destroying the per-Sub grouping the span map indexes. Not acceptable alone — TransformMatchingTex depends on that grouping.
  - fmn_tex::TexEngine holds its fmd_math::Engine in a private field with no accessor, and fmd_math's drawn/ module (the extensible-delimiter engine) is pub(crate) upstream.
  So: emit one VMobject per Sub, resolving glyphs via fmd_math::FaceSet::font(FaceId) + font.glyph_outline(gid), rules as rectangles, and PlacedPath contours directly (those arrive already positioned and need no face access at all). Either add TexEngine::math(&self) -> &fmd_math::Engine (one line, keeps §19 layering — fmn-library already depends on fmn-tex) or take fmd-math/fmd-font as direct deps of fmn-library. BOTH ARE PERMITTED: scripts/check_crate_dag.py only inspects deps whose name starts with "fmn-", and SUITE_ALLOWLIST.tsv already admits fmd-font and fmd-math as runtime class. Pick one and record why.

Use fmd_math::paths::canonical_dump / layout_dump (fixed six-decimal, deterministic) for goldens — the fmn-tex engine fingerprint already does.

Acceptance: Text and MarkupText builders over TextRequest with the full StyleMaps surface (t2c/t2f/t2g/t2s/t2w); a Tex/TexText builder over TexEngine; submobject-index fixtures proving Text[a:b] and isolate= select the right children; one VMobject per Sub for math with the span map intact; a golden per construction; negative cases (unmapped char, unsupported construct) surfacing as the named errors fmn-text/fmn-tex already produce rather than as silence or garbage.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FROM fm-ig3's review (2026-07-27) — a bug you would have hit head-on, fixed before you get there.

`compile_shape` detected subpath breaks by ZERO LENGTH, but fmn-geom's convention (and the Reference's) is A HANDLE SITTING ON THE PREVIOUS ANCHOR. The two coincide only when a subpath begins exactly where the previous one ended. Every glyph with a counter — o, a, e, b, d, g, p, q, 0, 4, 6, 8, 9, and most of the math alphabet — has an inner loop that starts somewhere else, so every one of them would have compiled as ONE subpath and filled, in §10.2's own words, 'as one ring with a chord through it'. The break also survived into the segment list, so a stroked glyph would have grown a spoke from its outer contour to its counter.

Fixed in crates/fmn-render/src/table.rs: it now asks `QuadPath::subpath_end_indices` rather than re-deriving the predicate, which also keeps the Reference's 1e-4 disambiguation tolerance in the one place that owns it. Regression test: `table::tests::a_subpath_that_begins_elsewhere_is_still_a_subpath`.

Worth knowing when the Scribe bridge starts turning fmd-font outlines into VMobjects: if you build a glyph's contours with `QuadPath::add_subpath`, the break is inserted for you and now survives compilation correctly. If you build point runs by hand, the marker is `p1 == p0` with `p2` genuinely distinct — not a null curve.

title: W10: Canonical PNG panels from the certified corpus, for Look Gallery review
description:
The certified engine's corpus (crates/fmn-conformance/tests/certified_engine.rs) locks raw frames, which is the right certified artifact but is not something a human can adjudicate. title: W8: flaky test — fmn-output boundary::sandbox_publishes_atomically_and_pins_the_environment fails intermittently under full-suite parallelism, passes in isolation
notes: Second racy test observed 2026-07-24: sandbox_timeout_kills_and_leaves_destination_untouched fails intermittently under load (assertion matches!(result, Err(JobTimedOut)) at boundary.rs:617 — the scripted job completes before the timeout fires). Both flakes are timing-sensitive sandbox tests; reproduce by looping 'cargo test -p fmn-output --test boundary' under parallel build load. Roughly 1-in-3 under contention, passes in isolation.
close_reason: Root cause: ETXTBSY (ExecutableFileBusy) on spawn, not timing. The suite writes a fake-ffmpeg script then execs it; a sibling test thread forking inside that window leaks a writable fd into its child, and the kernel refuses the exec. Explains every member of the family (sandbox_publishes_atomically, sandbox_timeout_kills, two_stage_mux, sandbox_refuses_oversized) and the profile (load-dependent, isolated reruns green). Fix: scratch() hands out a spawn-gate MutexGuard with the private dir, so any test that writes a tool and runs it excludes sibling forks for its whole body — enforced by the return type rather than by vigilance. Two assertions now print the result they got. Verified 44 hammer runs at 8/16 threads under extra parallel load, 0 failures (3/12 failed before).

title: W5: Refresh retained geometry and style under writable live views
description:
Root cause found during fm-ys2 fresh-eyes review. RenderPlan::sync reuses retained geometry/style solely from revision dependencies before checking live-view state, and marks Instance::volatile only for whole-buffer writable views. Direct writes through a zero-copy Python/NumPy view need not call RecordView::write and therefore need not bump revisions. A held field-scoped writable point/style view is not included in volatile at all. The result can be stale compiled geometry/style and even cache hits from stale pixels, violating plan §8.2: while a writable live view exists, the affected object or field is conservatively invalidated every frame.

Acceptance:
1. Whole-buffer writable views force fresh point and style observation every sync even when revisions do not move.
2. Field-scoped point views invalidate geometry/hints and poison affected tile keys; field-scoped style views rebuild style and poison affected tiles; unrelated field views do not needlessly recompile geometry.
3. Regression tests model mutation with no Stage/RecordView revision callback, matching a zero-copy external writer, and prove rendered output changes immediately rather than only after view drop.
4. Hint demotion remains fail-closed under every writable point-view lifetime.
5. scripts/check.sh and UBS gates pass.
notes: Implemented exact field-scoped writable-view invalidation across retained geometry/style, mirrors, bbox, primitive hints, copy/snapshot, binning, fill-kernel selection, plan identity, and tile-cache poisoning. Added a foreign-write bridge/conformance hook and regression proving frame bytes change while the field revision remains fixed. Evidence 2026-07-28: rch exec -- cargo test -p fmn-mobject -p fmn-render exited 0; rch exec -- scripts/check.sh exited 0 with fmt, all-target check, clippy -D warnings, all tests/doctests, and crate-DAG green. UBS 5.3.7 scanned all 13 changed Rust files; nonzero only for 10 audited false positives: 4 deliberate fixture-test panics, 3 ordinary render/cache comparisons misclassified as secret comparisons, and 3 srgb_decode calls misclassified as JWT decoding; no unsafe or actionable finding. Authoritative pre-stage Agent Mail conflict check: 13 paths clear, 0 conflicts.
close_reason: Implemented fail-closed writable-view invalidation with untracked foreign-write render proof; full workspace gate green and UBS findings audited as false positives.

title: W5: Make IR snapshots cover full hint and subpath semantics
description:
Root cause found during fm-ys2 fresh-eyes review. snapshot::encode claims to serialize every pixel-deciding IR field, but writes only shape.hint.name() and shape.arc_length.total(); it omits every primitive-hint payload, the per-curve arc-length table, and Shape::subpath_starts. Different circle/arc/rect parameters or fill subpath topology can therefore alias one self-golden digest even though specialized coverage or winding pixels differ. hint_names_are_distinct only proves variant names differ and cannot catch payload loss.

Acceptance:
1. Version the snapshot schema and canonically encode every Hint discriminant and payload, every subpath boundary, and any arc-length data actually consumed by rendering.
2. Add paired negative tests in which only hint payload, subpath boundaries, or per-curve arc-length data differ; each must move the digest.
3. Extend describe() so adjudication output names those semantic differences.
4. Adjudicate the fixture golden explicitly with the schema change.
5. scripts/check.sh and UBS gates pass.

title: W10: The full Gauntlet corpora — correctness oracles, Look Gallery, engine-equivalence, fuzzing campaign
description:
Scale W1GAUNT's rig into the full verification machine (§16.3-16.5):

CORRECTNESS ORACLES: analytic ground truths — arc length vs closed forms; boolean identities; winding invariants; TeX layout vs the published Appendix-G parameters; color-model round-trips — plus property/metamorphic tests RESTRICTED TO VALID LAWS (integer-pixel translation equivariance; stateless resampling; subdivision invariance) and the structural-fixture corpus against the Reference where formulas intentionally coincide (loose f32, §16.4).

SELF-GOLDENS at scale: geometry snapshots at lifecycle points + frame hashes for the primitive (~25 scenes, public) and feature corpora — bit-locked per platform, cross-platform under certified; THE merge blocker (D-16).

THE LOOK GALLERY: side-by-side FrankenManim vs captured Reference imagery, human-reviewed, with perceptual metrics (SSIM, edge-distance, local-error percentiles) as SMOKE ALARMS, never hard gates; verdict vocabulary at-least-as-good / different-but-fine (Behavior-Noted) / regression (fix); review workflow tooling (render pairs, record verdicts, track regressions to their introducing change).

THE ENGINE-EQUIVALENCE SUITE (Rev 4, §16.3): fast-CPU and annex engines vs certified-engine reference frames under the VERSIONED visual-equivalence budget (perceptual + max-error bounds) — BLOCKING for engine changes, informational elsewhere.

THE FUZZING CAMPAIGN (§16.5): SVG, TTF, YAML-subset, TeX strings, PNG/JPEG, the canonical deserializer — with RESOURCE-BUDGET assertions (error within budget; never hang; never overallocate); fmd-math fuzzing (arbitrary token streams error precisely, never garble); CI-scheduled continuous fuzz with corpus persistence.

Acceptance: all four planes running in CI with their blocking semantics wired correctly (goldens block always; equivalence blocks engine paths; Gallery informs; fuzz runs scheduled); the oracle corpus documented per §16.3's taxonomy; a demonstrated regression drill for each plane (inject → detect → block/report).
notes: fmn-hash exposes fmn_hash::fuzz_probe(&[u8]) -> bool as the deserializer fuzz entry point (never panics; drains typed reads under Lenient policy). Wire it into the W10 fuzzing campaign's target set. Landed with fm-6h6.

description: When fm-ntp stands up the cargo-fuzz infrastructure for fmn-codec parsers, add fmn-cache targets riding the same harness: (1) entry-envelope decode over arbitrary bytes (entry::decode must never panic — the in-crate flip/truncation tests cover structured corruption; the fuzz target covers unstructured hostility at scale), (2) namespace-name validation + key-material → object-path invariants (path always under root, components hex-only; the LCG-driven traversal test in tests/store.rs is the seed corpus). Both are pure functions over byte inputs — trivial fuzz targets once the infra exists.

title: W5: Two-level binning, per-tile command lists, painter-order-safe occlusion pruning
description:
Implement Lumen's spatial organization (§10.8): object bounds → ~128x128 MACROTILES → engine-sized fine tiles → stable per-tile command runs, with sizes tuned per platform by the ExecutionPlan (§17.4) — tuning changes speed, never semantics. Command lists keep STABLE draw indices derived from W3ORDER's deterministic draw sequence; transparent runs stay in EXACT painter order; (annex note for later: deterministic count/prefix/scatter or stable key sort, never unordered atomic appends — the CPU binning must be expressible that way too, so keep the algorithm order-stable by construction).

OCCLUSION PRUNING, painter-order-safe: a conservative back-to-front opaque-coverage mask per tile lets provably-hidden commands be skipped ONLY when the result is provably unchanged (full opaque cover by later-drawn content in the same tile, no blending interactions); depth-tested 3D adds a hierarchical per-tile depth summary. The rule is absolute: pruning is an optimization with a proof obligation per skip — when in doubt, draw.

Determinism obligations (§10.5): tiles are write-disjoint by construction (one owner per tile per pass); composite order is fixed; binning output is identical at any thread count (parallel binning must produce the same command lists as serial — stable partitioning, no completion-order dependence).

Acceptance: binning golden tests (fixture scenes ⇒ identical tile command lists at {1,4,16} threads); painter-order preservation tests through binning; occlusion-pruning equivalence tests (pruned vs unpruned frames bit-identical on an adversarial corpus: translucent stacks, opaque covers, depth-tested mixes); macrotile/fine-tile size-sweep test proving size choices don't change output bits.
notes: FROM fm-gw7: the per-tile command list is this bead's to build. What exists upstream of it: fmn_render::plan::RenderPlan produces the painter-ordered instance list (ShapeTable::instances(), each carrying shape/style/offset/order), which is the input a binner consumes. The CSR shape (u32 offsets + u32 draws, built by a deterministic host-side count -> prefix -> scatter) was proven end-to-end on Metal in G0-8 and is structurally what §10.8 mandates — see the earlier note on this bead for F13's flag word.
close_reason:
Landed in crates/fmn-render/src/bin.rs (64 tests in the crate). Two-level binning (object bounds -> macrotiles -> fine tiles), CSR command lists with F13's per-command class word, and painter-order-safe occlusion pruning.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Binning golden / thread-count invariance: build_partitioned(n) makes §10.5's obligation testable WITHOUT threads — a partition is a slice of the painter-ordered instance list, counts sum in partition order, and each instance scatters to a slot derived from that sum. Byte-identical offsets/draws/flags at n in {1,2,3,4,5,7,16,64}, including counts that do not divide the work evenly. Pruning is checked under the same sweep.
- Painter order through binning: every tile run ascends in instance index, which IS painter order because the instance list is.
- Occlusion-pruning equivalence: stated the way it can be checked before an engine exists — for every pixel, the VISIBLE SUFFIX (everything from the last opaque full-cover onward) is identical pruned vs unpruned. Adversarial corpus: translucent covers (prune nothing), concave covers (never claim to cover), covers that miss a tile, and the covering command itself never dropped.
- Size sweep: tile size is a scheduling choice. The invariant is NOT identical per-pixel lists — binning is conservative, so a coarser tile legitimately lists more — it is that every tiling delivers every RELEVANT command in painter order, agreeing with an unbinned ground truth. Checked at 5 tilings over a pixel grid.

FOUND AND FIXED A REAL BUG IN fm-gw7's TABLES: shape_digest excluded position (which is what makes interning find anything) but compile_shape stored ABSOLUTE points, so two copies of one outline shared geometry sitting at the first copy's position — the second binned on top of the first, and an opaque cover pruned a draw nowhere near it. Compiled outlines are now shape-local, hints are localized with them (Hint::translated), and ScreenMap::place REQUIRES the instance offset so the mistake is not expressible. The IR golden moved and was adjudicated in the same commit, which is the golden doing its job.

DEFERRED, with reasons: frame-level pruned-vs-unpruned bit-identity needs a rasterizer — the visible-suffix property above is the strongest available now, and G0-8b already proved frame bit-identity for this mechanism against the spike's own fill. Depth-tested 3D's hierarchical per-tile depth summary waits on depth existing (fm-2u6/G3). Tile sizes come from §17.4's ExecutionPlan, which is fm-3df; Tiling carries defaults and takes them as parameters, which is the shape it needs either way.

title: W6: fmn-text — shaping, markup, and layout over fmd-font (Scribe I)
description:
Implement the text plane (§11.2): native shaping — cmap→gids, kerning via kern + focused GPOS, bundled-face ligature sets OFF by default (matching the familiar manim look; opt-in flag) — greedy line breaking with manim's width semantics (Knuth–Plass as an option, never the silent default), and the manim markup tag set: <span>, <b>, <i>, <u>, <s>, <sub>, <sup>, <tt>, <big>, <small> with color attributes, plus the t2c/t2f/t2g/t2s/t2w maps, justification/indent/alignment/line-spacing at full constructor granularity.

Output contract: glyph runs as QuadPath outlines (via fmd-font's decoder) with W6SPAN's provenance attached, preserving StringMobject submobject-indexing conventions — Text[3:7] and isolate= must produce the same submobject structure users' scene code indexes (the compatibility surface here is structural, not pixel).

Font policy (D-08): the bundled default face renders identically on every machine; user TTFs by path; the family-name scan is a convenience tier that never silently substitutes (a missing font is a named capability-style error, not a fallback surprise). Default text face decision: the Reference defaults to Consolas via Pango — ours is the bundled default face, Behavior-Noted (BN-05 covers native-typesetting metric differences).

Markup parsing is untrusted-adjacent: bounded nesting/size, precise diagnostics, fuzz target (§16.5).

Acceptance: shaping fixtures (kern pairs, ligature on/off) for the bundled faces; line-breaking fixtures vs manim width semantics; markup-parse golden tests incl. malformed-input diagnostics; t2c-family application tests via span maps; submobject-indexing fixtures vs Reference conventions; Gallery review of text samples (BN-05 drafted).
close_reason: Scribe I implemented in crates/fmn-text: owned shaping (cmap→gids; kerning = legacy kern + GPOS kern feature parsed once per face — CM Unicode kerns via GPOS; bundled ligature sets OFF by default with opt-in, ligatures cover their char range per §11.3); greedy line breaking with manim width semantics + least-badness as an explicit option (property-tested never worse than greedy); align/justify/indent/line-spacing at constructor granularity; the manim markup tag set (b/i/u/s/tt/big/small/sub/sup/span with color-weight-style-underline-font_family attrs, entities) with bounded parsing and one-based line:col diagnostics; t2c/t2f/t2g/t2s/t2w by source-byte occurrence with containment semantics (t2c never perturbs kerning); D-08 font policy (FontBook: bundled CM default + CM Typewriter + Plex Sans, user faces from bytes, family lookup errors by name with the roster — never substitutes); TextLayout with per-glyph face/span/char_index/submobject ordinal matching Reference StringMobject conventions (non-space glyphs in order; Text[a:b] slice + isolate-style select); underline/strike decorations; QuadPath output via the proven transcription seam (positioned, translation-exact fixture). 28 tests: kern/ligature fixtures, wrap/align/justify/spacing fixtures, markup goldens + 8 malformed-diagnostic cases + depth bound, map application incl. gradients, submobject indexing, outline geometry, markup chaos suite. BN-05 drafted (native typesetting vs Pango/host fonts; Gallery review rides the capture program). Full gate green; flaky fmn-output test re-observed and evidence added to fm-rvm.

title: W7: Code + MarkdownMobject — fmd's highlighter and document engine as animatable content
description:
Implement the document-flavored mobjects (§11.7, Appendix A census; leapfrog #10):

CODE: the census class (text_mobject module) binding FMD'S SYNTAX HIGHLIGHTER (the pygments displacement — §1.7, §2.3: the highlighter ships in fmd and displaces pygments verbatim) over CM TYPEWRITER — language selection, style/theme mapping (owned themes; document which pygments style names map where), line numbers per the Reference's constructor surface, and the StringMobject indexing conventions so Code[…] slicing works like Text (via W6SPAN's provenance — the highlighter's token spans ARE source spans; wire them through rather than re-deriving).

Each element maps to a submobject subtree with source-span provenance so TransformMatchingStrings works ACROSS document edits — the killer demo (edit a slide, animate the diff).

title: W5: Wire the retained compositor to real pixels — pooled frame buffers, bump arenas, reuse-equivalence goldens
description:
fm-0l8 landed the retained compositor's KEY and its dirty-tile machinery in crates/fmn-render/src/cache.rs: §10.8's four-part key (command list, resource revisions, camera revision, output transform), poisoning for §8.2's writable live views, per-frame counters for §17.2, and an adversarial key-completeness suite (every mutation class invalidates: style, transform-both-old-and-new-bounds, order, camera, output transform, live view).

TileCache is GENERIC over its payload because there is no rasterizer in the tree. What remains is everything that needs pixels:

1. REUSE-EQUIVALENCE GOLDENS: cached vs cold frames bit-identical across an animation corpus with waits, static layers and moving objects. The key-completeness suite is the strongest form available without an engine; this is the form the bead asked for.
2. POOLED FRAME BUFFERS + BUMP ARENAS: 'per-frame allocation in bump arenas over pooled frame buffers — the zero-alloc steady state PG-6 measures (allocation count is a sharper regression tripwire than wall-clock)'. fmn_frame::FramePool already exists and is the thing to pool.
3. THE wait()-FRAME FAST PATH, MEASURED: the counters are wired (CacheStats::hit_rate, dirty_fraction) and a wait() frame already reports 100% hits — what is missing is measuring the RASTER WORK avoided, which needs raster work to exist.
4. STATIC LAYER RUNS CACHED AS UNITS: §10.8 asks for runs above/below animated content cached as a unit rather than per tile. Deferred deliberately: it is a coarser key over the same mechanism, and choosing its granularity without a rasterizer's cost model would be guessing.

BLOCKED ON: the first engine (fm-ig3, the certified CPU engine).

DO NOT re-derive the key. TileKey::build reads the binning and the plan precisely so a new input cannot be forgotten at one call site and remembered at another; TileCache::store takes the key plan_tile returned so a payload cannot be stored under a state it was not rendered from.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FROM fm-ig3 (2026-07-26) — the rasterizer TileCache<T> was waiting for exists now.

cache.rs said it plainly: 'the engines own pixels (§10.1), and there is no rasterizer in the tree yet; parameterizing means the cache mechanism is complete and tested now, and the payload type arrives with the engine that produces it'. The engine renders into a fmn_frame::FrameBuffer of PixelFormat::Rgba16F (linear light, straight alpha, output orientation), so T is a tile's slice of that.

Four things that bear on wiring it:

1. THE TILE FUNCTION IS ALREADY PURE. FrameJob::render_into slices the frame into bands with chunks_mut and hands them to a shared queue; a band's bytes are a function of (band index, plan, config) and nothing else. A cache that substitutes stored bytes for a tile is substituting for a pure function, which is what makes reuse byte-identical rather than nearly so.

2. OCCLUSION PRUNING IS ALREADY PROVEN BYTE-EXACT AGAINST THE ENGINE — occlusion_pruning_is_byte_exact renders the same scene with and without prune_occluded and compares bytes. That is G0-8b's F13 discharged with pixels rather than argued from interior_row's literal 1.0.

3. TileKey'S EXCLUSION OF THE INSTANCE INDEX AGREES WITH ADR-0013, and now on purpose. The key omits the instance index because 'an object inserted earlier shifts every later index without changing what this tile draws'; ADR-0013 rules that the engine's accumulation order is painter order and outline order, never an interned table's order. Same reasoning, two places, now cross-referenced.

4. WATCH THE STRIDE. engine::frame_digest hashes payload rows only, never the whole allocation, because a pooled buffer carries the previous frame's stride padding — hashing it would make a golden a function of pool history. A cached-and-restored tile payload must respect the same boundary; the_frame_digest_ignores_stride_padding is the shape of the test you want.

Also filed: fm-e9h (zero steady-state per-frame allocation, PG-6), which overlaps your bump-arena work and should probably land with it.

title: W7: Atlas — coordinate systems, axes, plotting (native text throughout)
description:
Implement the coordinate-system plane (§12.2): the CoordinateSystem protocol — c2p/p2c, input_to_graph_point, graphing with DISCONTINUITY handling (the Reference's recursive discontinuity search semantics), Riemann rectangles, get_area_under_graph — Axes/ThreeDAxes/NumberPlane/ComplexPlane/NumberLine with tick and number placement LOCKED BY GLYPH-SEQUENCE TESTS (all number labels are native DecimalNumber text now — W7DETEX/W6TEXT — so the test asserts the glyph sequence and positions, not pixels); UnitInterval/Slider; ParametricCurve with the Reference's t-range/epsilon semantics; FunctionGraph; ImplicitFunction over W2FIELD's isolines (min_depth/max_quads budget semantics honored).

title: EPIC W3 — Marionette: the mobject engine (fmn-mobject)
description:
Workstream W3 (plan §8, §20.2): the object model of the whole system. Depends on W1, co-designed with W2, and its core is ratified by G0 spike 1 (object-model & buffer-lifetime).

Contents: the Stage arena with generational Mob handles, rooted lifetimes, and CoW snapshots (§8.1); the RecordBuffer — interleaved f32 records matching the Reference dtypes (API surface for mobject.data and zero-copy NumPy structured views) with the specified view protocol (views pin buffers; copy-on-resize; mutation marks dirty; reallocation under a live view impossible by construction) and the Rev-4 mandatory lazy revisioned SoA/AoSoA render mirrors feeding Lumen's compiled render state (§8.2); manim's copy semantics implemented to the letter — recursive submobject/ndarray copy, updaters by reference, family-internal reference remapping (§8.3); the full family/positional API (next_to, arrange, to_edge, align_to...) locked by fixtures, bounding boxes with dirty propagation, the complete uniform inventory incl. four clip planes (§8.4); the Reference's render-order model kept as semantics with ordering-trace fixtures (§8.5); insertion-ordered dt/non-dt updaters with the Reference's add_updater(call=True) double-call bug FIXED, ValueTrackers, always_redraw, and the .animate builder's real rules (§8.6); arena snapshot serialization backing SceneState/undo/replay/fixtures (§8.7).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
AUDIT ADDENDUM — testing & logging doctrine (binding on every bead in this epic):

Every task bead in this epic lands with its tests as PART OF ITS SCOPE — a bead without its tests is not done:
1. COMPREHENSIVE UNIT TESTS, colocated in-crate, covering the bead's stated acceptance criteria INCLUDING negative and edge cases (degenerate inputs, resource-budget violations, version-mismatch refusals, error-path assertions — not just happy paths).
2. E2E REGISTRATION: any bead landing user-visible behavior (a mobject, an animation, a CLI flag, an output format, a Studio surface) registers at least one scripted end-to-end scenario with the Gauntlet e2e harness (fm-fjq) — driven through the real surfaces (CLI / Rust API / fmn-python / Studio HTTP), asserting outputs (bit-locked hashes on certified paths; structural assertions elsewhere), exit codes, and emitted-file inventory.
3. DETAILED STRUCTURED LOGGING: behavior flows through the owned tracing layer (§17.1/§18 — scene→play→frame→phase→tile spans, stage timings, counters, decision points: engine selection, cache hits, purity classifications, barriers). Where correct behavior is invisible in the output ("the preflight ran before frame 0", "wait() frames hit the tile cache"), the e2e scenario ASSERTS ON THE LOGS. On failure, the harness auto-bundles a deterministic repro (scene + input closure + logs + journal tail).
4. GATES BEFORE CLOSE: scripts/check.sh green (fmt, check, clippy -D warnings, test) + ubs clean on changed files, per AGENTS.md. Determinism-relevant beads additionally run their {1,4,16}-thread sweep before close.

title: W10: The one API schema — classes, methods, defaults, flags, config keys; codegen for both front doors
description:
Implement the single source of API truth (§16.2, D-05 adjacency): ONE machine-readable schema describing classes, methods, parameters, defaults, CLI flags, and config keys — from which are GENERATED: Rust config structs + builders (the kwargs displacement: Default structs + builder methods, §15.1), fmn-python signatures (argument names/defaults/keyword-ness matching the pinned manimlib surface), Parity Ledger rows (W10LEDGER consumes), CLI flag tables (W9CLI consumes), and docs. DRIFT BETWEEN FRONT DOORS IS A BUILD ERROR — the schema check runs in CI; a Rust builder or Python signature that disagrees with the schema fails the build.

Bootstrapping: extract the initial schema from the pinned Reference (signatures, defaults, keyword arguments) via the W1GAUNT extraction tooling; then the schema is AUTHORED (our canonical names per C-9's typo rulings — tickness_multiplier et al. get canonical names in the schema with exact-name aliases in fmn-python), reviewed, and versioned. Include the wildcard-export inventory (§1.6: from manimlib import * has no authoritative __all__ — the Ledger enumerates SYMBOLS, and the schema is where that enumeration lives).

Also here: fmn-config's struct migration to codegen (W1CONF hand-wrote; this bead swaps in generated types), and the CLI exit-code/flag-interaction table (W9CLI's normative source).

Acceptance: schema file + generators in CI; drift negative tests (mutate a generated signature → build fails); import-surface conformance harness comparing the schema's export list against the actual pinned wildcard namespace; C-9 alias tests; docs generation smoke test.
close_reason:
The one API schema landed (§16.2). Two committed layers — API_SCHEMA.tsv, extracted from the pinned Reference by scripts/gen_api_schema.py (2276 symbols, 4441 params, 34 flags, 149 config keys), and API_OVERLAY.tsv, authored (C-9 canonical names, §16.1 tiers, optional config keys, Rust bindings) — merged by fmn_conformance::schema, which is the only thing generators ever see.

Extraction is a static ast walk, not an import: the Reference cannot be imported here (colour/moderngl/pyglet/a GL context) and importing it would make the schema a function of the local environment. CPython's wildcard rules are modelled faithfully, including skipping the TYPE_CHECKING guard bodies that never execute at runtime. The walk lands on 257 classes — exactly Appendix A's independently verified census, now asserted as a test, so a Reference pin bump that moves the census says so.

Acceptance, item by item. Schema file + generators run under cargo test and therefore CI. Drift negative tests present: a mutated accessor AND a mutated config path, both generated in memory so they neither race the bless run nor depend on the artifact existing. Import-surface harness compares the enumerated export closure against the extractor's own count and asserts both that the numpy leak IS present and that TYPE_CHECKING-only names are NOT. C-9 alias tests assert every misspelled symbol has a canonical name, that the Reference spelling survives as the fmn-python alias, and that each ruling stays within two edits so an API redesign cannot ride in disguised as a typo fix. Docs generation is smoke-tested by the same byte-for-byte gate as everything else. fmn-config's migration to codegen is done: 99 hand-written lines replaced by generated.rs, with all 35 pre-existing config tests passing unchanged as the behaviour-preserving evidence.

Findings recorded in the commit: C-9's real extent is 26 symbols and 2 params, not the 3 the plan names (the listner misspelling is systematic across the whole event surface); the wildcard surface leaks 73 third-party/stdlib names; class-level attributes are public surface and 105 are now carried. Two modelling gaps found by the coverage check were fixed in the schema rather than papered over in the test — map-valued parent keys that are bound as a whole, and optional keys that by definition have no default line to extract.

NOT DONE, deliberately, and noted on fm-c53 with a how-to: the CLI exit-code and flag-interaction tables. §13.6 wants them pinned in the schema and the schema is now where they go, but neither is extractable (the Reference signals by exception, not exit code) and authoring them is a W9 design decision rather than a transcription. Inventing them here would have been fabricating a contract under cover of codegen.

2265 of 2276 symbols read unreviewed — the honest number for a surface nobody has adjudicated, and the one fm-iz4's Ledger ratchets down; docs/api/ledger.tsv is the substrate it consumes.

Gates: scripts/check.sh green (fmt, check, clippy -D warnings, test, crate-DAG); 915 tests passing, up from 889; no new crate, no new DAG edge, no new dependency. ubs reports 19 criticals, all one class — panic! inside test code, the same fixture-test idiom geometry_parity.rs and self_goldens.rs already use — adjudicated false positives.

title: W11: Python wheels — CPython x platform ABI matrix, the manimlib namespace policy
description:
Package the Python front door (§20.2 W11, §15): wheels for the CPython x platform ABI matrix (abi3 where PyO3's support allows — decide and document the minimum CPython), bundling the engine + fonts so pip install franken-manim → from manimlib import * works with ZERO system dependencies (the one-binary story, wheel edition).

THE NAMESPACE POLICY (decide deliberately, document publicly): the bridge presents the manimlib module surface (§15.2) — resolve how the wheel provides it (a manimlib shim package? an import hook? a namespace decision recorded with its conflict story vs upstream manim installs in the same environment — a user with both installed must get a predictable, documented outcome, not import roulette).

Wheel contents: the compiled fmn-python extension per tier policy (portable tier for wheels, or per-arch wheels with tier selection — decide against R22's matrix budget); bundled OFL fonts with license texts; the fmd-math packs; NO ffmpeg (system ffmpeg discovered per D2's optional posture).

Acceptance: wheels build in release CI for the declared matrix; a clean-venv smoke test per platform (pip install → render the Hello corpus scene → bytes verified); the namespace-conflict test matrix (with/without upstream manim present); wheel-size budget recorded; the ABI/namespace policy documents published.

title: W6: fmd-math core — TeX grammar, the atom/spacing engine, style propagation
description:
Implement fmd-math's core (§11.4; architecture per G0-3's ratified spike). The language surface as ACTUALLY used (per G0-4's harvest ranking): groups, sub/superscripts, \frac/\dfrac/\tfrac/\binom, radicals with indices, \left...\right and fixed-size delimiters, accents (\hat \vec \dot \tilde \bar \overline \underline \overbrace \underbrace with annotations), big operators with limits (\sum \int \prod ...), the operator-name set, Greek + the standard symbol vocabulary (CM + Noto Math coverage), \text{...} islands, spacing commands, \mathbb/\mathcal/\mathrm/\mathbf/\mathsf/\mathtt, colors, phantoms, \stackrel/\overset/\underset.

The LAYOUT ENGINE: TeX's published mathematics — the EIGHT ATOM CLASSES (Ord/Op/Bin/Rel/Open/Close/Punct/Inner) and the inter-atom spacing table; display/text/script/scriptscript styles with correct propagation (\mathchoice-class behavior: numerators shrink, limits move, spacing changes by style). This bead is the parser + atom classification + spacing + style machinery; placement mathematics (fractions/radicals/scripts per Appendix-G parameters) is the next bead — but the ENGINE SHAPE (box/glue/kern node model or the spike's ratified alternative) is fixed here and must serve both.

Error doctrine (§11.5, R1): an unsupported construct is a PRECISE, NAMED error ("\substack is not yet supported; tier T2, tracked at ...") — never silence, never garbage; arbitrary token streams must error cleanly, never hang or garble (fuzz target, §16.5).

Acceptance: parse golden tests over the harvest's tier-1 corpus (parse success/fail exactly as tiered); atom-classification fixtures vs TeX's rules; spacing-table tests (every atom-class pair, every style); style-propagation fixtures; the unsupported-error format standardized (the ratchet bead consumes it); fuzzer wired.
close_reason: Landed upstream (franken_markdown 4328835, its main) and consumed at the SUITE.lock pin. Delivered per acceptance: T1 grammar (incl. \over group-split, TexText contract with display math + missing-$ recovery, parse-level T1 environments, SingleStringTex fragment semantics); atom classification + Bin→Ord degradation fixtures; the TeXbook p.170 spacing table locked pair-by-pair in every style; D/T/S/SS×cramped style_walk fixtures; box/glue/kern node model + frozen Layout types fixed for fm-hk9; the unsupported-error format standardized and locked (ratchet unit); chaos fuzz suite wired (cargo-fuzz harness rides fm-ntp's program). Corpus parse goldens: all 9,269 strings match tiers exactly — 99.27% unique / 99.58% occurrence-weighted parse coverage (≥99.5% T1 bar). fmn-tex holds the pin to the committed tier table + frozen API. Both repos' full gates green.

title: W8: The negotiated ffmpeg boundary v2 — FFMPEG_PROTOCOL.md, sandbox, hardware encoders, fake-ffmpeg CI
description:
Implement the ONE external-tool boundary (§14.3, §3 D2, D-23). FFMPEG_PROTOCOL.md v2 replaces any fixed pipe with NEGOTIATION: fmn-frame renders in output orientation (no vflip, ever) and applies transfer natively (no obligatory eq); the sink negotiates pixel format (RGBA8/BGRA8 for alpha/compat, NV12 for ordinary 8-bit video, P010 for 10-bit/HDR, canonical RGBA for certified raw/PNG), orientation, transfer, primaries, range, row stride, and encoder. The arithmetic is the argument: 4K RGBA8 is 33.2MB/frame vs NV12's 12.4MB — 2.67x less pipe payload at 60fps.

THE SECURITY PROTOCOL (D2, complete): argv-only invocation (no shell), per-job private temp dirs, timeouts + process-tree cancellation (via fmn-platform's process capability), output-size limits, environment allowlist + locale pinning, atomic result publication, executable path AND content hash into provenance. ffmpeg is OPTIONAL: absence yields a capability error NAMING the native alternative — never silent substitution.

HARDWARE ENCODERS enter here and only here (§14.3): hevc_videotoolbox/ProRes on macOS, h264_nvenc/hevc_nvenc/AV1 on NVIDIA — a documented standard-mode knob (ffmpeg products are excluded from certification by construction, so hardware encode changes nothing about the determinism story); fmn doctor reports what the installed ffmpeg offers; selection explicit or auto; encoder identity in provenance.

Protocol retentions: GIF mode, the two-stage audio mux (video first; then -c:v copy -c:a aac -map ...), --subdivide outputs, insert files, --prerun counting. ALL testable against a FAKE-FFMPEG in CI (a scripted binary asserting argv/stdin contract and emitting canned outputs) — the protocol is CI-verified without real encoders.

Acceptance: fake-ffmpeg contract suite (every negotiation dimension, both mux stages, failure modes: timeout, oversized output, nonzero exit); sandbox tests (env allowlist, tree-kill on cancel); capability-error tests with ffmpeg absent; provenance fingerprint test; real-ffmpeg smoke test behind an env flag.
close_reason: Boundary v2 landed: FFMPEG_PROTOCOL.md + fmn-output negotiate/ffmpeg modules. Negotiation over wire format/rational fps/color/container/encoder with typed refusals; no-vflip/no-eq structural; D2 sandbox complete (argv-only via fmn-platform, private workdirs, env allowlist+locale pinning, timeout, log caps, artifact size verification, atomic rename publication, content-hash+version provenance); capability error names native alternatives; hardware encoders explicit-only, validated vs probed caps; two-stage mux with -c:v copy verified; concat/transcode/prerun retentions. 22 tests incl. fake-ffmpeg sandbox suite + real-ffmpeg smoke (verified vs ffmpeg 7.1.1). 528 workspace tests green.

title: W4: The RationalFrameClock — manim's exact sample points, drift-free
description:
Implement the clock (§9.2, D-07, BN-02): an i64 frame index over fps, computing time as exact rationals — emitting the SAME nominal sample sequence as the Reference's arange(0, run_time, 1/fps) + 1/fps semantics: no emitted alpha-zero progression frame (begin() interpolates at zero separately, outside the emission sequence); upward duration rounding (a run_time that is not a whole number of frames still covers its end); the final sample may exceed run_time (alpha clamps per the Reference's rule); finish() applies final_alpha_value. Scene code experiences manim's timing model without manim's float drift — hour-long renders accumulate zero error (Behavior Note BN-02).

Why rational: the Reference advances a float accumulator; at 30fps an hour of frames drifts visibly, and two runs disagree with themselves under different chunkings. Our clock is (frame_index, fps) — time derives, never accumulates. Every subsystem that needs "now" (updaters' dt, wait_until predicates, presenter holds, A/V sync in Reel) reads this clock; dt is exactly 1/fps as a rational, converted to f64 at the consumer boundary.

PERMANENT REFUSAL (D-18, §10.5): adaptive or variable frame sampling is refused forever — the sample points are semantics, and every scheduler freedom in §17 is defined relative to them. Encode this in the type: there is no API to emit off-grid samples.

Acceptance: sample-sequence fixtures vs the Reference formula across awkward run_times (0.1, 1/3, 2.9999, exact multiples); drift test (10^6 frames: exact equality with closed-form time); wait/wait_until/skip interaction tests; the no-off-grid-API property documented and asserted.
close_reason: RationalFrameClock landed in fmn-anim: RationalTime (frames/fps — off-grid time unrepresentable by construction, D-18 refusal encoded in the type), FrameSegment sampler with the Reference's exact emission semantics (no alpha-zero frame, upward duration rounding via exact-rational ceil on the received f64, alpha clamp, skip = whole segment), overflow-free exact comparisons vs f64 seconds. 9 acceptance tests: count fixtures cross-checked vs Python Fraction AND numpy arange (BN-02 divergence set: 0.1@30fps = 4 vs Python's 3, documented), coverage property over 20k durations ((n-1)/fps < rt <= n/fps exactly), million-frame drift test (bit-equal to closed form; float accumulator provably drifts), wait/wait_until/skip interaction, refused inputs (0 fps, NaN/inf, overlong). BN-02 drafted at docs/behavior_notes/BN-02-rational-clock.md.

title: W1: fmn-platform — capability traits (fs/process/clock/AssetFetcher) + HardwareTopology introspection
description:
Implement fmn-platform (§6, §17.4). Two halves:

(1) Capability traits: filesystem, process spawning (the ffmpeg boundary's substrate — argv-only, env allowlist, timeouts, process-tree cancellation live HERE as the one sanctioned subprocess mechanism), monotonic + wall clocks, and the host-provided AssetFetcher trait — the ONLY place network exists; no TLS in core (D2). Every capability is a trait object the engine receives, never an ambient global: this is what makes the deterministic lab, WASM tiers, and the Studio's isolated worker possible. Provide std implementations + test doubles (virtual fs, fake clock, scripted AssetFetcher).

(2) HardwareTopology introspection (Rev 4, §17.4): physical/logical cores, performance classes (P/E), cache groups and NUMA nodes/CCDs, SIMD tier detection (portable/v3/v4/NEON), annex device presence, available memory, encoder capabilities — processor-group-aware on Windows (systems above 64 logical processors span groups and explicit scheduling code must know it). This feeds fmn-runtime's ExecutionPlan derivation (W5 bead): engine, frames in flight, render-team count/threads, tile dimensions, SIMD tier, scratch sizes, output pixel format.

Platform notes to honor from §17.6: no core pinning on Apple silicon (no clean no-unsafe API; output is thread-count-independent so placement cannot affect bits anyway); QoS class mapping is a consumer concern but the topology must expose what it needs.

Acceptance: trait suite + test doubles; topology snapshots from at least linux-x86-64 and one aarch64 committed as fixtures; Windows processor-group handling unit-tested against synthetic topologies; doc comments making the capability doctrine explicit for every later crate.

Real linux-x86_64 snapshot committed (128L/64C/8xCCD); synthetic x86 SMT+CCD and aarch64 big.LITTLE sysfs fixtures; real aarch64 snapshot = fm-<new> (hardware). Capability doctrine documented at crate root. Also fixed pre-existing check_crate_dag failure (G0 spike crates now exempt, with a no-production-dep-on-spike check). Notes: process-tree cancellation is direct-child kill (no libc under forbid(unsafe); ffmpeg doesn't daemonize — revisit documented); UBS's one remaining critical is the scanner's Command::new heuristic on the capability's program parameter — mechanism-vs-policy by design, absolute-path contract enforced, fixed-tool allowlist lands at the W8 boundary.

title: W4: The six-step frame order + the FramePacket freeze
description:
Implement the frame loop's load-bearing order EXACTLY (§9.3, §1.4, D-19): (1) animation update_mobjects(dt) → (2) animation interpolate(alpha) → (3) time advances → (4) SCENE updaters run, observing post-interpolation state → (5) capture → (6) emit. always_redraw-style scenes semantically depend on step 4 seeing step 2's output; this order is a contract, not an implementation choice.

The UPDATE-ORDER CORPUS locks it: dt-updaters on animated mobjects; target-with-updater; suspend both ways (animation suspending target updaters; explicit suspend_updating); wait and wait_until; skip mode; final samples; unequal run_times in one play(); time_span re-windowing. Each corpus scene asserts observable state at specific frames — these are semantic regression tests, not pixel tests.

THE FRAMEPACKET (Rev 4's boundary at step 5, reordering nothing): capture freezes an immutable FramePacket — frame index and alpha, camera state, RNG substream states (via §6.5's keyed forks), and revisioned references into Lumen's compiled render state — after which the frame no longer depends on mutable scene state. Everything before the freeze is the serial front-end; everything after (IR sync, binning, raster, color conversion, emission) consumes ONLY the packet. This is what makes the §17.4 pipeline and §9.5 frame-parallelism legal. Design the packet as genuinely immutable (no interior mutability, revision handles not live pointers) and cheap (CoW snapshot references, not deep copies).

Acceptance: the update-order corpus green; FramePacket immutability enforced by construction (API review + a test that mutating scene state after capture cannot affect a held packet); packet-cost measurement (O(touched-state), suitable for 3-6 in flight per §17.4).
close_reason: Six-step frame order + FramePacket freeze landed (§9.3, D-19): play_segment/wait_segment in fmn-anim drive the load-bearing order exactly — per-animation update_mobjects(dt) interleaved with interpolate(t/run_time, raw-unclamped so the §9.4 pipeline clips unequal run_times), time advance (clock + Stage::update fixed to advance its float mirror BEFORE updaters, matching increment_time-then-update_mobjects), scene updaters over post-interpolation state, capture, emit. Skip = one big-dt step, no capture/emit; BN-10 corrects the Reference's skip-mode double-dt (finish pass is dt=0 in both modes, so skipped and played segments end in identical updater state — corpus-locked). Reference begin_animations (roots unrooted animated mobjects) and finish_animations (remover cleanup + dt=0 pass) kept. FramePacket: immutable by construction — frame index, segment frame, clamped alpha, exact RationalTime, Rc'd CoW snapshot (O(touched) verified via storage_id sharing), and DERIVED rng: keyed per-frame forks are pure fns of (seed, substream, frame_index) so the packet carries two words and rng_fork() reproduces any substream exactly (D-18 property). Camera state + IR revisions join at fm-gw7/fm-5xm (documented subset). 16-scene update-order corpus green: post-interpolation observation (always_redraw property), time-before-updaters, suspend matrix, copy ticking, skip-parity, unequal run_times, final-sample clamp, time_span re-window, wait/wait_until/skipped-wait, membership edges, packet isolation/cost/rng. 339 workspace tests; all gates green (ubs: 0 critical).

title: W2: True arc length under the original names — adaptive quadrature + inverse-arclength LUTs
description:
Implement the proportion/length layer correctly (§7.3, BN-03). The Reference's layer is chord-distance heuristics — three mutually inconsistent approximations, with quick_point_from_proportion assuming equal curve lengths. We keep the NAMES and fix the MATH (D-05).

Scope: (a) get_arc_length returns actual arc length via adaptive Gauss–Legendre quadrature (fsci quad) with a stated tolerance; (b) point_from_proportion and MoveAlongPath consume a per-revision inverse-arclength LUT — built lazily per path revision (coordinate with §10.8's compiled-path caches: the LUT is one of the retained per-path artifacts, invalidated by geometry revision only, NOT by transform/style changes), giving constant-speed motion, as every user always assumed it worked; (c) quick_point_from_proportion REMAINS as the documented fast approximation — heuristics survive beside true math as labeled options, never silent substitutes; (d) downstream consumers get length-true placement: dashes, arrow tips, and tracers place by true length (W7 consumes this).

Behavior Note BN-03: paths animate at slightly different (correct) pacing than the Python engine; document with a migration example (a MoveAlongPath whose apparent speed changes).

Acceptance: arc-length oracle tests against closed forms (circles, parabolic arcs, lines); LUT inverse-error property tests (point_from_proportion(L(t)/total) ≈ t within tolerance); LUT-revision invalidation tests (transform does NOT rebuild; geometry edit does); constant-speed metamorphic test (equal proportion steps ⇒ equal arc steps).
close_reason: Proportion/length layer landed in fmn-geom/src/arclength.rs. Design upgrade over the plan sketch: quadratic Bezier arc length has a CLOSED FORM (|B'| is the norm of a linear function), so no quadrature and no fsci dependency — exact to rounding, deterministic (ln via fmn-dmath), with exact branches for lines, points, and interior cusps. get_arc_length = true length; point_from_proportion = constant-speed via ArcLengthTable (Newton on exact partial lengths + bisection safeguard, fixed 24 iterations, convergence break); quick_point_from_proportion kept verbatim as the labeled heuristic; CachedArcLength implements the §10.8 geometry-revision-only keying (transform/style never rebuild — tested). Oracles: 20k-interval Simpson agreement 1e-9, analytic parabola sqrt(2)+asinh(1) at 1e-12, cusp exactly 1, line exact; inverse round-trip; constant-speed metamorphic on an uneven path incl. demonstration that the quick heuristic diverges. BN-03 drafted with the MoveAlongPath migration example. All gates green (58 suites), ubs 0 critical.

title: W5: The Metal annex engine — Studio preview production backend (via frankentorch)
description:
Implement the Accelerator Annex's first production engine (§10.7, §17.5, D-22; building directly on G0-8's proven kernels): Metal via frankentorch — the ONLY GPU gateway (no wgpu, ever: D1 audit catastrophe + duplicates ft) — serving Studio preview on Apple silicon, where unified memory makes the handoff nearly free and preview frames carry no bit promise.

Offload set, ranked by ROI (§10.7): stroke SDF + AA resolve (dominant 2D cost, per-pixel independent — G0-8's stage); SSAA resolve + transfer functions; DotCloud/glow splats (overdraw-heavy, additive); 3D surface tessellation with the kept lighting; large fill coverage. Platform playbook (§17.6): ft shared buffers for upload; tile-shader/threadgroup techniques keeping tile-local coverage and compositing on-chip (Apple TBDR rewards exactly this); memoryless attachments for pass-local results; threadgroup sizes from pipeline introspection, never CUDA habit; direct presentation for preview; GPU-side NV12/P010 conversion before any export readback (§14.3).

Hard boundaries (R21): standard-mode ONLY, never certified (D-18 refusal); annex binning uses deterministic count/prefix/scatter or stable key sort, never unordered atomic appends; excluded from core gates — PG-A profiles gate ANNEX changes only, so acceleration can never mask a core regression (annex work PAUSES whenever core PG-1..PG-3 regress); backend identity journaled into the input closure; held to the engine-equivalence visual budget vs certified frames.

Acceptance: Studio preview renders through the annex by default on supported hardware with the declared CPU fallback intact (G3's required-with-fallback rule, OQ-12); engine-equivalence suite green for the annex on the corpus; PG-A rig measuring fps, bytes up/back per frame, occupancy on the pinned Apple profile; fallback-path test (annex unavailable ⇒ CPU preview, no error).
notes:
G0-8b (fm-orn) verdict: FILLS ARE IN SCOPE for the Metal preview backend, not deferred to CPU-only. The fill kernels land at the f32 arithmetic floor (max delta-8bit = 1, vs the stroke stage's 152), use the same one-thread-per-pixel dispatch model as the stroke kernel, and add no new upstream requirement on frankentorch. Use FillShape::PerPixel and MathMode::Safe.

ALSO OWNED HERE (G0-8b finding F17): at preview resolution the boundary is the cost, not the kernel. An EMPTY scene on the same grid costs ~1.1 ms of the 1.3-2.2 ms frame — allocate an 8.3 MB device buffer, clear it, read it back. Two levers, both outside the kernel: (1) hold ONE surface for the engine's lifetime instead of buffer_zeroed per dispatch (the spike reallocates deliberately, because a spike should not cache); (2) §17.6's GPU-side NV12/P010 conversion before any export readback. For Studio preview, present rather than round-trip. A PG-A per-frame number is meaningless without the empty-scene floor beside it.
