title: W7: The de-TeX'd natives — Brace, Matrix delimiters, Checkmark/Exmark, DecimalNumber
description:
Implement §11.6/§12.3's de-TeXing — the Reference routes several NON-math classes through LaTeX because LaTeX was there; we make them native and better, removing the deepest early typesetting dependency from the library's critical path:

BRACE becomes a PARAMETRIC PATH GENERATOR — correct at any width (the Reference renders \underbrace{\qquad} and stretches it, distorting the curl at extreme widths; ours is a proper parametric family), with BraceLabel/BraceText composing with Scribe text; LineBrace orientation semantics preserved. MATRIX delimiters use fmd-math's extensible-delimiter engine DIRECTLY (W6MATHEXT) — Matrix/DecimalMatrix/IntegerMatrix/TexMatrix/MobjectMatrix lay out their element grids natively (row/col spacing, alignment per the Reference's conventions) with delimiters that scale correctly by construction. CHECKMARK/EXMARK draw from bundled glyphs (no pifont). DECIMALNUMBER/INTEGER are PURE NATIVE TEXT — one face, GLYPH-RECYCLING updates (a ticking counter re-uses glyph instances, W5IR's interning — no per-frame typesetting), correct formatting edge cases (negative zero, rounding mode, trailing zeros, unit suffixes, edge_to_fix semantics for ChangingDecimal).

Also here (§12.3): SurroundingRectangle/BackgroundRectangle/Cross/Underline; BulletedList/Title on Scribe; the interactive.py control mobjects (Button, Checkbox, sliders, ControlPanel...) as compositions bound to Proscenium events (event wiring lands with W9EVENTS; construct them here).

Behavior Note BN-08: de-TeX'd classes render from native constructions; metrics differ from the LaTeX-derived originals; scaling behavior is better-defined.

Acceptance: Brace parametric tests across widths (smooth, symmetric, correct curl); Matrix layout fixtures (spacing/alignment vs Reference conventions) with delimiter-scaling tests; DecimalNumber formatting edge-case corpus + glyph-recycling test (update does not re-typeset); structural fixtures for the remaining classes; BN-08 drafted.
close_reason:
The de-TeX'd natives landed for the half that needs no typesetter; the text-backed half is SPLIT OUT, not dropped — fm-ebl carries its acceptance criteria unmodified, blocked on fm-p5d (the Scribe bridge). Every dependent of fm-y69 that needed the text classes (fm-3kr, fm-jh7, fm-v4l, fm-wy1, fm-i1q) has been re-pointed at fm-ebl, so nothing is unblocked by this close that should not be. GOVERNANCE §5 clause 2: a postponed item moves to a later bead publicly, with its criteria travelling intact.

LANDED HERE: Brace / BraceLabel / LineBrace as a parametric path family; SurroundingRectangle, BackgroundRectangle, Cross, Underline; Checkmark and Exmark as drawn marks. Plus two pieces of substrate the tier needed and the crate lacked — per-point stroke tapers (VMobject::with_stroke_profile, carrying set_stroke(width=[0,6,0]) by linear resize onto the point run) and the detached positional layer (bbox_point, moved_to_aligned, next_to, next_to_point, aligned_to, arranged) mirroring Stage's critical-point semantics exactly.

THE BRACE IS CORRECT AT ANY WIDTH, BY CONSTRUCTION. The Reference renders one \underbrace{\qquad} and resizes it: widening is a special case over six hard-coded submobject indices of that render, narrowing has no special case and squashes the curl via set_width(stretch=True). Ours generates the shape, with three clamps proved rather than tuned — cap+waist ≤ 0.40w < 0.50w (hooks cannot reach the centre point), thickness ≤ 0.10w < cap (inner hooks cannot cross), height > 1.2·thickness (the point cannot punch through its runs). The property test walks widths 0.001 to 200 checking all three. The thickness clamp was not in the first draft: the test caught a real inversion at width 0.01, where a brace narrower than its own stroke turned inside out — precisely the regime where the Reference distorts, so it would have been easy to ship and easy to excuse. The tip is closed-form where the Reference scans the rendered glyph with np.argmin.

CHECKMARK/EXMARK DIVERGE FROM THE BEAD TEXT, ON EVIDENCE. The bead said "draw from bundled glyphs (no pifont)". The faces were checked, not assumed: U+2713 ✓ is mapped by IBM Plex Sans and Noto Sans Math (not Computer Modern); U+2717 ✗ is mapped by NO bundled face, nor are U+2714/2718/2715. A glyph exists for the check and none exists for the cross. U+00D7 is present but is a thin multiplication sign, the wrong weight for \ding{55}; bundling a dingbat face for two glyphs expands the closure. Both are therefore drawn, in one shared unit box — drawing only the cross would leave a matched pair mismatched, since the Reference's two dingbats come from one font and read as siblings. This is ADR-0005's precedent (drawn path as mainline when the authored glyph is absent) applied to marks. Recorded in BN-08 with the cmap table.

BN-08 drafted at docs/behavior_notes/BN-08-de-texed-natives.md, per §16.8's assignment of that number to the de-TeX'd classes. A numbering collision was found and FLAGGED RATHER THAN SILENTLY FIXED: a file already holds BN-08 for the animation contract, and BN-07 is duplicated across two files. Renumbering a published, user-facing note is a documentation act with its own review, and RULE 1 forbids deleting files, so fm-nn8 carries the reconciliation.

Gates: scripts/check.sh green; 935 tests passing, up from 915; fmn-library 80 unit tests, up from 63. ubs: 3 criticals, all panic! in test code (two mine, one pre-existing), the house's fixture-test idiom — adjudicated false positives.

title: W9: The replay journal + effect model — record everything, replay cheaply, invalidate conservatively
description:
Implement replay (§13.4, R16): the journal records COMMANDS AND EFFECTS — play/wait/add/remove operations, RNG substream states at barriers, camera/audio state, content hashes of every file/font/asset read, callback version hashes, ffmpeg invocations — with OPAQUE BARRIERS for non-replayable operations and CONSERVATIVE invalidation (when in doubt, a barrier).

Three consumers, one record: (1) the supervisor's edit-replay (W9SUPER: restore checkpoint, replay journal from the last valid barrier — entries whose recorded hashes still match replay from cache; a changed callback hash invalidates from that point); (2) the PURITY CLASSIFIER's evidence (§9.5: the effect model IS the classifier's vocabulary — segments whose recorded effects are pure are frame-parallel eligible; classifications are journaled per segment, R20); (3) the PIPELINE's synchronization vocabulary (§17.4: any operation that must observe rendered pixels is a pipeline barrier that drains in-flight frames; ordinary manim scene code never hits one — assert this on the corpus).

Soundness doctrine (R16): replay-cache unsoundness is the failure mode — the design answer is conservative invalidation everywhere: unrecognized effects are opaque; divergent operation classes become barriers BY DEFAULT; a replay that would diverge (hash mismatch mid-replay) falls back to full re-execution, correctly, silently, and records why.

Also here: the one-command REPRO BUNDLE (§18) — scene + input closure packaged so every bug report is a deterministic replay — and the journal's appearance in provenance sidecars.

Acceptance: record/replay equivalence tests (replayed session ⇒ bit-identical final state + frames on pure content); invalidation tests (edited callback → replay stops at the right barrier); opaque-barrier tests (an unrecognized effect forces re-execution, never wrong reuse); purity-evidence round-trip with W4PURITY; pipeline-barrier drain test; a repro-bundle end-to-end test (bundle → fresh machine sim → identical render).
close_reason: Replay journal + effect model + repro bundle landed in fmn-scene (FMNA/3+4). Command/effect/asset/subprocess/checkpoint records; plan_replay with conservative invalidation naming its reason; ReplayAudit divergence fallback; EffectClass embedding W4 purity evidence (R20); PixelObserving pipeline-barrier vocabulary with corpus assertion; Custom→Opaque coercion; §18 repro bundle with closure verification. 10 acceptance tests incl. bit-identical fresh-stage replay and bundle end-to-end. 538 workspace tests green.

title: W6: fmd-font — factor the Font module out of fmd + build the glyf outline decoder (cross-repo)
description:
Cross-repo task in franken_markdown (§2.3, §11.1, §2.9 — the upstream ledger's first seed entry). Factor fmd's text::Font sfnt machinery (cmap formats 4/12, glyf/loca, composite glyphs, hmtx, kern + focused GPOS, subsetting) into a new fmd-font workspace crate, and EXTEND it with the piece FrankenManim needs and fmd never did: the GLYF OUTLINE DECODER — simple and composite glyphs decoded to quadratic contours (TrueType outlines are already quadratic — zero-loss into our QuadPath model) with phantom-point-correct metrics (left/right side bearings, advance interaction with hmtx, composite offset/anchor semantics).

Bundled faces (§11.1): Computer Modern roman/bold/italic/bold-italic (the default face — the 3b1b typographic identity), CM Typewriter (code), IBM Plex Sans, Noto Sans Math (symbol coverage) — all OFL, all shipped in-crate; a bare install renders every built-in scene identically everywhere; NOTHING depends on host fonts (D-08). User TTFs load by path; family-name platform scanning is a convenience tier. Honestly tiered out with revisit triggers (§16.6): CFF/CFF2, variable fonts, color glyphs, GSUB ligature machinery beyond the bundled-face sets, mark positioning, bidi/complex shaping.

Security (§16.5, R14): fonts are untrusted input — bounded table sizes, offset validation, composite-recursion limits, fuzz target from day one (malicious font tables are a DoS surface even in safe Rust).

Governance (R8): fmd-font rides UPSTREAM_LEDGER.md + SUITE.lock like any foundation crate; FrankenManim CI builds both repos from the lock. G0-3 (the fmd-math spike) needs CM outlines decoded — this bead's decoder is its prerequisite.

Acceptance: outline decoding golden tests for CM glyphs (including composites and accent glyphs) as quad contours; metrics tests vs known values; round-trip through W2's QuadPath; fuzzer wired; the fmd workspace conversion done without breaking fmd's existing build (OQ-3's mechanics resolved and documented).
close_reason: Landed cross-repo. Upstream (franken_markdown fc5c246 + d7cda47, pushed): workspace conversion per ADR-0004 (root package + fmd-font member; 'pub use fmd_font as text' keeps fmd's whole surface; full fmd suite stays green), the greenfield glyf outline decoder (simple + composite with full F2Dot14 transforms, scaled/unscaled offsets, anchor matching, USE_MY_METRICS phantom-point metrics; depth/point/component budgets; synthetic hostile tests + deterministic mutation/truncation sweeps standing in for the fuzzer, cargo-fuzz follow-up per ADR-0003), golden + census-locked tests (all 1979 real Plex/Noto composites decode with extents exactly matching authored bboxes; CM authored-bbox slop measured and bounded), and the bundled OFL faces shipped in-crate behind the bundled-faces feature (§11.1). Downstream here: SUITE.lock re-pinned to d7cda47, fmd-font allowlist row, first foundation git-dep wired into fmn-text, governed_closure now enforces git-dep rev == SUITE.lock pin, and the QuadPath round-trip acceptance test (1:1 segment mapping incl. shared-anchor break-curve semantics, exact extents, arc-length identity to 1e-12). 550 tests green; fmt/clippy clean; ubs criticals are panic!-in-tests false positives.

title: W9: The Studio — preview server, inspector, scrubbing, TUI, security model
description:
Implement the Studio (§13.5, D-14, leapfrog #6): localhost with an EXPLICIT security model — loopback-only binding, per-request capability token, Host/Origin validation, size limits, no filesystem serving beyond embedded UI assets, event-rate limits, session expiry. Untrusted content renders only in the isolated worker (W9SUPER).

Streams: baseline is MULTIPART PNG (we own PNG — no dependency, works everywhere); MJPEG as the ffmpeg-accelerated option; browser-local WASM rendering is the endgame (G5). On supported Apple silicon the preview renders through the METAL ANNEX by default (W5METAL — speed welcome, bit promises irrelevant for preview) with the CPU fallback declared (OQ-12/G3's rule).

Surfaces: TIMELINE SCRUBBING over W4TIMELINE + checkpoints (seek anywhere; pure segments reconstruct instantly, stateful segments snap to checkpoints); THE INSPECTOR — family tree, live record fields (the RecordBuffer's typed views), uniforms, TYPESET SPAN MAPS (W6SPAN's in-Studio payoff: hover a glyph, see its source span); DEBUG OVERLAYS — tiles, control cages, bounds, winding, depth (§18); a kitty/sixel TUI in the fp-frankentui lineage for SSH sessions (leapfrog #5's terminal leg).

Embedded UI: assets compiled into the binary (no runtime file serving, no CDN — the one-binary story extends to the Studio).

Acceptance: security tests (non-loopback refused; missing/stale token refused; oversized/flooding events limited; no path escapes); stream conformance (multipart PNG consumable by stock browsers); scrub correctness tests (seek(t) state matches play-through, via W4TIMELINE's machinery); inspector data-accuracy tests against engine state; TUI smoke test over a pty; annex-preview fallback test.
notes: Timeline substrate for scrubbing landed with fm-hfe: Timeline::seek restores the nearest checkpoint, replays whole segments, and lands via reconstruct_pure_frame for pure segments (O(1)) or by stepping frames for stateful ones. Two things the Studio will want on top: (1) a checkpoint POLICY — the timeline currently checkpoints every segment boundary, which is right for short scenes and wasteful for long ones; the knob belongs to whoever owns the scrub bar. Timeline::checkpointed_segments() already reports the cheap seek targets for the UI. (2) note that authoring a Timeline freezes .animate targets at authoring time (documented in the module doc); a Studio that re-authors on edit gets this for free, one that mutates steps in place does not.
close_reason: Studio acceptance implemented and fully green; CLI-level MJPEG/launch/checkpoint-policy composition is explicitly tracked by dependent fm-c53.

comments.author: LilacTern
comments.text: Claimed after the activation check found only W5 active, so W9 is the second active workstream and remains below the cap; all five dependencies are closed and bv identifies this bead as a direct unlock. Existing coverage audit found a bounded crash-isolated supervisor and worker protocol with distinct Seek/Scrub requests plus validated inline PNG/RGBA frames; Timeline already owns checkpointed pure/stateful reconstruction; EventInbox already crosses the host boundary without callbacks or Stage references; Lumen PreviewRenderer already prefers Metal and reports the truthful fast-CPU fallback. No Studio HTTP host, browser stream, inspector contract, debug-overlay snapshot, or terminal renderer exists. Architecture pin: host.rs will be a strict bounded HTTP/1.1 loopback service with exact Host and Origin authority checks, a caller-supplied 256-bit capability token compared in constant time, injected monotonic Clock for expiry and rate limiting, exact embedded routes only, and no filesystem or untrusted-scene execution. Every scene mutation/query is forwarded through Supervisor to the isolated worker; the live protocol gains typed Event, Inspect, and Overlay requests while existing Seek/Scrub remain the timeline authority. A bounded FrameHub will convert only validated worker PNG/RGBA responses and emit stock-browser multipart PNG. inspect.rs will take bounded read-only Stage snapshots for DAG family links, record fields, uniforms, span registries from TextLayout/Typeset, and overlays derived from Binning/Stage data. scrub.rs will distinguish transient preview seek, which restores the prior Stage, from committed seek. tui.rs will encode real kitty PNG and sixel output over generic Write; the PTY acceptance test will use a safe test-only rustix PTY edge already present in the governed lock, with its feature inventory updated explicitly. Runtime additions are workspace crates only (fmn-anim, fmn-mobject, fmn-text, fmn-tex); there will be no new third-party runtime dependency and no insecure token derived from deterministic scene RNG. Browser-local live WASM remains the already-recorded G5 follow-on; multipart PNG stays the permanent floor.

comments.author: LilacTern
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTATION + ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE (2026-07-29): fmn-studio now provides a strict bounded HTTP/1.1 loopback host with exact embedded routes, canonical Host/Origin validation, caller-supplied nonzero 256-bit capabilities with redacted output and constant-time matching, expiry and sliding-window rate limits on an injected monotonic clock, bounded bodies/headers/clients, no filesystem surface, and joined client-thread lifecycle. Every scene request crosses the concrete Supervisor boundary into the replaceable worker. Protocol 1.1 adds validated Event, Inspect, Overlay, and bounded digest-checked strict-JSON StudioData messages. FrameHub validates inline PNG/RGBA, converts tight/strided RGBA through the native codec, rejects unmapped shared memory, bounds history/bytes, and streams stock-browser multipart PNG using a monotone publication sequence independent of timeline frame index so backward scrubs remain visible. Inspector snapshots use deterministic root-order DFS ids with explicit node/depth/link/field/value/source/tile/point/JSON ceilings, live record revisions, uniforms, DAG links, Scribe-native span bindings through the Scene facade, and accurate tiles/control points/bounds/winding/depth overlays; truncated paths never report fabricated winding. Scrub preview restores Stage bytes and time while committed seek leaves Timeline::seek state live. Kitty PNG and deterministic fixed-palette sixel encoders are bounded, subprocess-free Write adapters; the acceptance suite writes Kitty bytes through a real safe rustix PTY. The metal feature reexports Lumen’s truthful PreviewRenderer selector and CPU fallback.

Fresh-eyes review additionally removed public ordinary equality from CapabilityToken, made JSON validation strict and nesting-bounded, separated preview publication order from semantic frame indices, bounded graph links/tile capture and DFS stack growth, joined all client threads, and preflighted Kitty allocation before base64 encoding. Validation on the exact staged implementation: cargo fmt --check exit 0; cargo check -p fmn-studio --all-targets exit 0; cargo clippy -p fmn-studio --all-targets -- -D warnings exit 0; cargo test -p fmn-studio exit 0 (7 unit, 6 protocol, 6 Studio including PTY, 13 supervisor); cargo test -p fmn-studio --features metal studio_metal_feature_uses_the_truthful_preview_selector exit 0; rch exec -- scripts/check.sh exit 0 with full workspace tests/doctests and crate-DAG OK for all 22 crates. UBS over all 13 owned changed paths exits 0 with 0 critical findings; its remaining warnings are test assertions/inventory heuristics. Cargo prints the known deliberately malformed asupersync fixture diagnostic while every command exits 0. The governed DAG correctly rejected direct Scribe/Choreo/Marionette edges during development; the final design uses the narrow fmn-scene studio_bridge and keeps only test-only direct dev edges. Optional MJPEG, executable host/worker launch composition, and the user-facing long-scene checkpoint-density knob are explicitly handed to dependent fm-c53 at the common fmn-cli/fmn-output composition root; browser-local live rendering remains the existing fm-l97 + fm-oee G5 follow-on. Multipart PNG is complete and remains the permanent compatibility floor.

title: GATE G4b — Certified Reproducibility: --reproducible end-to-end
description:
Convergence gate G4b (plan §20.3; sibling of G4a after G3; leapfrog #2). Criteria:

(1) The INPUT CLOSURE complete (§16.7): sources/modules, engine + SUITE.lock, toolchain + target features, config bytes, RNG seeds, asset/font hashes, execution-engine/backend identities + SIMD build tier, locale/timezone, capability policy — content-hashed into the sidecar provenance manifest. (2) fmn-dmath exclusively on certified paths (and the fixed-point raster boundary if G0-6 so decided). (3) Bundled-assets-only mode enforced (no AssetFetcher, bundled fonts only). (4) BIT-IDENTICAL raw frames + canonical PNGs + WAV across the certified matrix (linux-x86-64, linux-aarch64, macos-aarch64; Windows per OQ-6's separate decision) — including the deterministic parallel PNG-sequence bytes (W8CODEC2) and the deterministic sound mix (W8MIX). (5) Sidecar manifests emitted and verified. (6) PERFORMANCE GATES: PG-1(G4) — ≤0.35x the Python Reference — and PG-5 (the full determinism sweep including frame-parallel and pipelined schedules) blocking.

The closing property, stated once: the only uncertified artifact class left in the system is ffmpeg's — by construction, not by exception list. Gate review records the cross-platform hash evidence and a third-party-reproducible demo (repro bundle → fresh machine → identical bytes).

title: W3: Updaters, ValueTrackers, and the .animate builder — corrected where the Reference is buggy
description:
Implement the dynamic-behavior surface (§8.6): insertion-ordered dt and non-dt updaters with suspend/resume; ValueTracker / ExponentialValueTracker / ComplexValueTracker; always_redraw / f_always closure binding into the clock; and the .animate builder implementing the Reference's REAL rules — animation arguments set once per chain; override_animate methods un-chainable; dynamic target lookup at build time.

Two deliberate corrections (D-05; Appendix C rulings — each a Behavior Note): (1) add_updater(call=True) runs the update ONCE (the Reference double-calls — C-5); (2) Group.__add__ returns a NEW group like Mobject.__add__ (the Reference mutates in place on one path — C-6; consistent value semantics).

Semantics that must be exact: updater execution order is insertion order within dt and non-dt groups; the interaction with animation suspend_mobject_updating (an animated mobject's updaters pause unless opted in); updaters observing post-interpolation state at the scene level is CHOREO's frame-order business (§9.3) but the hooks live here; updater add/remove during iteration has a defined outcome (snapshot the list per tick).

Builder mechanics: recording chained calls into a deferred target (this doubles as the Rust fluent API's recording machinery per G0-1 — one implementation, two front doors); prepare_animation accepts Animation | _AnimationBuilder ONLY, rejecting bare methods precisely as the pinned Reference does (§9.1 shares this contract).

Acceptance: ordering tests (mixed dt/non-dt insertion sequences); suspend/resume matrix; the two corrections tested with Behavior Notes drafted; builder fixture corpus (chained-call recording, once-only args, override_animate no-chain, dynamic target).
close_reason: Dynamic-behavior surface landed (§8.6): reworked updater model — one insertion-ordered list mixing typed Dt/NonDt kinds with UpdaterId removal tokens, Reference-exact update order (children first, suspension + no-updaters-in-family pruning), per-tick list snapshot, insert/remove/clear/match, suspend_updating + resume_updating (incl. transitive ancestor clear + call_updater pass); C-5 fixed (call=true runs update(0) exactly once); ValueTracker/ExponentialValueTracker/ComplexValueTracker as typed f64-lane entry state with Reference encodings (ln for exponential; increment = set(get+d) through encoding); always_redraw container-swap binding + f_always; C-6 fixed (group_add always builds a new group); .animate builder with the REAL rules — deferred-command recording (G0-1 shape), args once-per-chain (ArgsAlreadySet), override un-chainable both directions (OverrideNotChainable), build-time target generation + dynamic Mob-target resolution, IntoAnimate as the typed prepare_animation contract (bare methods unrepresentable). BN-07-updater-and-group-fixes.md drafted (C-5, C-6). 18 new tests (dynamics + animate_builder corpora); scenarios updated to the typed updater API. All gates green (297 tests). Note: always_redraw uses container-swap pending fm-ncq's full become; fmn-anim's Animation joins IntoAnimate at fm-67a.

title: W5: Refuse stale or mismatched Lumen derived artifacts in FrameJob
description: FrameJob's safe public construction/render path documents that MonoTable, Binning, FrameConfig, and RenderPlan must share the same plan/map/viewport, but production validation checks only output format, destination dimensions, and total tile count. Same-grid different exact viewports, stale map-derived monotone geometry, stale bin maps, and reordered/resynced plan indices can therefore return Ok with an incorrect certified frame; out-of-range stale command indices are silently skipped. Make artifact identity enforceable: store and validate exact viewport, map, and a plan epoch/content identity in every derived artifact, or make matching artifacts inseparable by construction. Acceptance: fallible construction/render refuses mismatched MonoTable map, mismatched Binning map, same-tile-count/different-exact viewport, and stale/reordered plan identity; matching-artifact golden bytes remain unchanged. Evidence locations: crates/fmn-render/src/engine.rs FrameJob validation/render paths, fill.rs MonoTable::map, bin.rs Binning derivation.
notes:
Implemented fail-closed, collision-resistant artifact identity across RenderPlan, MonoTable, Binning, FrameJob, pruning, and tile-cache admission. GeometryIdentity hashes complete append-only compiled geometry including full hint payload, arclength rows, and subpath boundaries; PlanIdentity adds referenced style values and painter-ordered instance shape/style/offset/order. FrameJob construction is now fallible and names map, viewport, geometry, and painter-plan mismatches. Binning pruning is transactional on stale plans. Regression coverage includes mismatched monotone map/geometry, mismatched bin map, same-grid different exact viewport, painter reorder, stale cache admission, and stale prune. Existing certified frame tests remain green.

Validation provenance: rch exec -- cargo check -p fmn-render --all-targets -p fmn-conformance --tests (remote green); rch exec -- cargo test -p fmn-conformance --test certified_engine (remote 7/7); cargo fmt --all; rch exec -- scripts/check.sh used RCH documented local fallback for the non-compilation wrapper and passed fmt, check --all-targets, clippy --all-targets -D warnings, full workspace cargo test/doc tests, and the 22-crate DAG check. fmn-render 172 tests and certified_engine 7 tests passed. git diff --check and staged diff --check passed. Final staged UBS exited 1 solely because of five audited heuristic false positives: two ordinary frame-byte comparisons inside #[cfg(test)] misclassified as secret comparisons, and three calls to the deterministic color-transfer function srgb_decode misclassified as JWT decoding. UBS otherwise reported no unsafe, dependency, concurrency, check, clippy, or test defect.

Fresh-eyes follow-ups filed: fm-sq8.1 for retained-plan live-view invalidation and fm-sq8.2 for incomplete IR snapshot semantics.
close_reason: Fail-closed plan/map/viewport identities landed with adversarial regressions and full green gates; matching certified output remains unchanged.

title: G0-6: Determinism spike — one nontrivial frame hashed across four platforms; fix the certified arithmetic
description:
Executed decision spike resolving OQ-1: floating-point + fmn-dmath vs fixed-point raster arithmetic for certification (§20.1 spike 6 → §6.6, §10.5; risk R11, High).

Scope: render ONE nontrivial frame — it must exercise transcendental-dense paths (arcs, per-vertex atan2 joints, rate functions, glow falloff), gradient fills, strokes with joins, and alpha compositing — through the prototype renderer on linux-x86-64, linux-aarch64, macos-aarch64, and windows-x86-64, and compare raw-buffer hashes. Two sub-questions: (a) with f32/f64 floating screen-space arithmetic + fmn-dmath transcendentals + fixed-order reductions + FMA off, are the four platforms bit-identical? If yes, floating suffices for certified; if no, adopt the canonical fixed-point raster boundary (fixed-point screen coordinates + integer coverage accumulation at defined precision, explicit rounding) that §10.5 sketches. (b) Decide the certified matrix: linux-x86-64/linux-aarch64/macos-aarch64 certified from day one; windows-x86-64 functional-CI from W1 with bit-certification a SEPARATE declared decision (OQ-6, §16.7).

Prerequisite: an fmn-dmath prototype for the exercised functions (sin/cos/atan2/exp/tanh/sqrt at minimum) with documented accuracy — this spike is also fmn-dmath's first accuracy/portability shakedown.

Why now: everything in §10.5's parallelism contract, §6.1's tiered numeric doctrine, and the §17.3 SIMD lane rules is written against whichever arithmetic wins. Changing the answer after W5 exists would invalidate every self-golden.

Acceptance: hashes + methodology committed; OQ-1 resolved with the decision recorded in §23; the certified-matrix definition frozen into the input-closure spec (§16.7); if fixed-point wins, the precision/rounding constants specified.
close_reason:
OQ-1 RESOLVED: floating-point suffices. §10.5's canonical fixed-point raster boundary is RETIRED, NOT DEFERRED. ADR-0010; plan §23 trued up in the same commit; certified matrix frozen into docs/INPUT_CLOSURE.md §5; note at docs/g0/G0-6-determinism-ratification.md; raw data at docs/g0/g0-6-hashes/.

THE MEASUREMENT. One frame — gradient fills under the nonzero winding rule, a filled ring whose hole depends on winding DIRECTION, strokes with joins and arc-length tapers, per-vertex atan2 joint angles that reach pixels, the Reference's true_dot glow with its pow falloff (and its hard-dot branch), five rate functions driving the geometry, alpha compositing throughout — hashed through fmn-hash's canonical container, alongside per-function digests of all 16 fmn-dmath entry points.

  linux-x86_64   glibc   x86-64    native      cca55de642d54f2e...
  linux-aarch64  musl    aarch64   qemu-user   cca55de642d54f2e...
  macos-aarch64  Darwin  aarch64   native      cca55de642d54f2e...

ALL EIGHTEEN DIGESTS IDENTICAL ON ALL THREE. frame.f64 = 3ff2cac55c33a8b2..., frame.f32 = 9e94bf5e95765eca...

The legs vary things INDEPENDENTLY rather than repeating one comparison: x86-64-glibc vs aarch64-Darwin crosses both the ISA and the OS boundary at once; aarch64-musl shares an ISA with one and an OS family with the other. So the ISA, the libc and the OS are each shown not to be in the loop — which is the actual claim, and it is exactly why running one leg on musl was a stronger test than running it on glibc would have been.

NO-FMA EVIDENCE, AND A METHOD FAILURE WORTH RECORDING. llvm-objdump on the aarch64 build: 1652 scalar FP instructions, ZERO fmadd/fmsub/fnmadd/fnmsub/fmla/fmls, on a target where FMA is baseline. The scalar-op count is reported because it is what makes the zero mean anything — my first pass used plain objdump, which on this host cannot disassemble aarch64 at all: it emitted 3 lines and reported zero of every instruction, including the ones certainly present. A zero from a tool that found nothing is not evidence. determinism::fma_guard now refuses hand-written mul_add across the certified source roots, since rustc's no-contraction is a default rather than a setting.

WHAT I BUILT TO GET THERE. The prototype renderer (spikes/g0-8-accelerator, shared with G0-8) grew the two stages the frame needed and did not have: a nonzero-winding fill (exact in x, 4x supersampled in y, closed-form roots per sub-scanline, total-ordered crossing sort) with a defined gradient field, and the Reference's true_dot glow profile in full including pow(1-r, glow_factor). Plus per-vertex joint angles by atan2, reaching pixels through a miter-gain stand-in — because a joint angle that never reaches a pixel cannot be tested by a frame hash. All three are labelled IN THE SOURCE as defined stand-ins, not as §10.2's analytic-area fill (fm-5oi's) or §10.3's join model (fm-oac's): the question OQ-1 asks is whether two platforms compute the same bits from the same algorithm, and a spike claiming to be W5's renderer would have answered a question nobody asked.

G0-8's PUBLISHED NUMBERS ARE UNAFFECTED, deliberately. The Metal device layout (FlatIr) is byte-for-byte unchanged, the annex refuses non-Stroke IR and nonzero miter_gain BY NAME (checked before the device is opened, so the contract is testable without a GPU), and the stroke render loop was restructured to a row accumulator with the arithmetic preserved exactly — verified by re-running the G0-8 comparison and getting the identical max_abs/mean_abs/rms/max_u8/differing/ssim line. Refusing rather than skipping is also what D-18 requires: the frame that defines the certified bits must never reach a GPU.

THE FRAME IS NOW A CROSS-PLATFORM SELF-GOLDEN. Both digests are bit-locked as SINGLE constants in the spike's tests — not three per-platform ones — so the property fails on whichever machine breaks it instead of waiting for someone to re-run the sweep. That is the Scope::Certified shape docs/INPUT_CLOSURE.md §6 now points at.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DECIDE, stated so nobody reads more into it: (a) that f32 is safe for the fast CPU engine — f32 hashed identically everywhere, so it is PORTABLE, but G0-8 measured that it changes the PICTURE at curvature extrema; portable and correct are different questions, and fm-4wt now carries that comment; (b) that the SIMD tiers preserve any of this — they are the standing risk, since PG-5's per-commit sweep tests thread counts, not lane counts; (c) that linux-aarch64 HARDWARE behaves like linux-aarch64 emulation.

THE CAVEAT, RECORDED IN THREE PLACES RATHER THAN BURIED: the aarch64 Linux leg runs under qemu-user, because no aarch64 Linux hardware is reachable by this program. QEMU's softfloat is IEEE-754 correct for the basic operations and nothing certified uses anything weaker, so the leg is valid evidence about the ARITHMETIC — not about a machine. fm-sol replaces it with real hardware if any becomes available. Getting the leg at all required registering an arm64 binfmt handler on the dev box (owner-authorized), then cross-compiling to aarch64-unknown-linux-musl with rust-lld and running the static binary under qemu — compiling natively under emulation would have cost ~30x for an identical binary.

CERTIFIED MATRIX (sub-question b): linux-x86-64 / linux-aarch64 / macos-aarch64 certified from day one; windows-x86-64 functional-CI only, bit-certification remaining OQ-6's separate declared decision. Frozen into INPUT_CLOSURE.md §5, with the note that adding a platform is an ADR and not a CI-config change — the list IS the promise --reproducible makes.

DOWNSTREAM: fm-ig3 (certified CPU engine) is unblocked and now carries ADR-0010's four binding properties as acceptance criteria; fm-4wt carries the f32 finding and the SIMD lane-rule risk; fm-yp0 (G4b) enforces the frozen matrix; fm-sol owns the real-hardware replacement.

GATES: scripts/check.sh green; 937 workspace tests + 53 spike tests, 0 failing; spike fmt/clippy clean; the aarch64 record re-verified byte-identical after the final lint fixes. UBS: 1 critical, a panic! inside #[cfg(test)] code — the same false-positive class this repo has adjudicated before.

title: W10: The binding-tax program — batched crossings, GIL discipline, the opt-in acceleration ladder
description:
Implement §15.2's Rev-4 performance program for the Python boundary — arbitrary Python callbacks are the ONE serial, GIL-sensitive component no scheduler can dissolve, so the tax is engineered down and made visible:

MECHANISMS: method-resolution and callback handles CACHED (resolve once per (type, method), invalidate on class mutation); native→Python crossings BATCHED wherever semantics allow (updater groups crossing once per frame, not once per field); the GIL RELEASED across all native compilation, rasterization, conversion, and output waits (the interpreter and rasterizer overlap instead of alternating — §17.4's pipeline overlaps rendering with subsequent Python frame construction); dirty propagation batched once per callback group rather than per field write.

THE ACCELERATION LADDER (opt-in, never silent): above the always-correct Python updater sit explicit substitutions with identical semantics for their declared class — batched Python updater (fewer crossings) → array updater (one vectorized RecordBuffer operation) → native updater (Rust/engine-executable). Each is an EXPLICIT opt-in with documented semantics; silent substitution is prohibited (D-05's spirit: labeled, never silent).

VISIBILITY: callback-heavy scenes are DETECTED and reported with their phase breakdown (§17.1's Python-callback phase) so the tax is visible before anyone optimizes around it; PG-8's class table — native built-ins ≤1.10x Rust; per-frame-callback, point-transform-callback, and dynamic-subclass classes each with a PUBLISHED budget — is measured by W10PERF's rig against G0-5's baseline numbers.

Acceptance: crossing-count instrumentation + reduction tests (batching measurably reduces crossings on the callback corpus); GIL-release verification (a Python thread makes progress during a long native render); ladder correctness tests (each rung bit-equals the Python rung on its declared class); the detection report golden test; PG-8 baseline numbers recorded.

title: W11: npm/WASM packaging — the browser artifacts
description:
Package the WASM tiers (§20.2 W11, §10.7): the tier-1 frame renderer (W5WASM) as an npm package — ESM module + typed JS surface via wasm-bindgen, single-threaded default with the threads variant behind cross-origin-isolation documentation; the tier-2 serialized-timeline player as it lands at G5 (consuming W4TIMELINE's format; the browser Studio endgame's substrate).

Packaging discipline: artifact-size budgets CI-measured (R19 — fonts are the driver; the wasm bundle feature-gates faces and loads packs on demand where the design allows); version lockstep with the engine (the npm package version pins the engine commit; a serialized timeline records the engine version and the player refuses mismatches per §6.7's versioning policy); no CDN assumptions (the package is self-contained; consumers host it).

Acceptance: npm package builds + publishes in release CI (dry-run publish gate); a browser integration test (bundler + headless browser rendering a primitive scene from the package); size budget recorded; the version-mismatch refusal test; README/typing docs for the JS surface.
